classes.name: Core\Arr
classes.summary: Works with arrays. It finds, sorts, changes and combines elements. Every method returns a new array, and the array you pass in does not change.

doc.shortHtml: The direction Core\Arr::sort and sortByKey put elements in. It is the { order: … } option, and it is Asc when you leave it out.
Which part of an entry Core\Arr::diff and intersect compare. It is the { on: … } option, and it is Values when you leave it out. by and comparator apply to the part it selects.
Returns the number of entries in $a.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to count.

doc.returnHtml: The number of entries; 0 for the empty array.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the entries for which $predicate returns a truthy value. The callback receives ($value, $key) and may declare fewer parameters.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to filter.

params.name: predicate
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry. A truthy result keeps the entry. Truthy means the same here as in an if test.

doc.returnHtml: The kept entries under their own keys, never renumbered; an empty array when nothing passes.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces every value with the result of $fn for it. The keys stay the same.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to map.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters; its return type is the result's U.

doc.returnHtml: One entry per entry of $a, under the same key. Its value is the callback's result.

doc.shortHtml: Stores every value under the key that $fn returns for it.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to re-key.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters. It returns the entry's new key, an int or a string.

doc.returnHtml: The values under their new keys, in first-occurrence order. When two entries get the same key, the last one is kept. 1 and "1" are the same key.

doc.shortHtml: Puts the entries into groups. $key is called for each entry, and its result is the name of the group the entry goes into.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to partition.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters. It returns the group's name, an int or a string.

doc.returnHtml: One inner array per distinct result, in first-occurrence order. Each inner array keeps its entries under their own keys. 1 and "1" name the same group.

params.name: initial
params.descHtml: The starting value. Its type is U, which is also the type of the result.

doc.returnHtml: The last carry; $initial itself over an empty array, with no call made.

doc.returnHtml: The key as a string, whatever it was written as; null when nothing matches.

params.descHtml: The array to test.

params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters.

params.descHtml: The array to test.

params.name: predicate
params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters.

doc.returnHtml: false at the first falsy result; true for the empty array.

params.descHtml: The array to test.

doc.returnHtml: true for the empty array, false otherwise.

params.descHtml: The array to look in.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The array to search.

params.name: needle

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The array to search.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The value to look for, compared as contains compares.

doc.returnHtml: The key as a string, or null when no entry is identical. It never returns false.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to test.

doc.returnHtml: true for a list and for the empty array. false when any key is out of sequence, or is not its index written exactly in decimal digits.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every key in insertion order.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array whose keys are wanted.

doc.returnHtml: A list of the keys as strings. "10" stays "10" and is never an int. An empty array gives the empty array.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every value in insertion order, under new keys from "0".

params.descHtml: The array whose values are wanted.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0".

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value of the first entry.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to read.

doc.returnHtml: The value, or null for the empty array. In an array<?T>, this null looks the same as a stored null.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value of the last entry.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to read.

doc.returnHtml: The value, or null for the empty array. In an array<?T>, this null looks the same as a stored null.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the key of the first entry.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to read.

doc.returnHtml: The key as a string, or null for the empty array.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the key of the last entry.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to read.

doc.returnHtml: The key as a string, or null for the empty array.

members.name: slice
members.signature: slice(array<T> $a, int $offset, ?int $length = null, { preserveKeys?: bool }): array<T>

doc.shortHtml: Returns the entries in one range of positions. A position counts entries from the start, whatever the keys are.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to take from.

params.name: offset
params.descHtml: The position where the range starts. A negative offset counts back from the last entry. An offset before the first entry starts at the first entry.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: How many entries the range has. A negative length stops that many entries before the end, and null takes every entry to the end.

params.name: preserveKeys
params.descHtml: Keeps every entry's own key. By default every key is discarded, string keys included, and the result is renumbered from "0".

doc.returnHtml: The entries in the range; the empty array when the range ends before it starts.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a copy of the array with one range of positions replaced by the values of $replacement. The original array does not change.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to edit.

params.name: offset
params.descHtml: The position where the range starts. A negative offset works as in slice. An offset at the end appends.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: How many entries the range has. A negative length works as in slice. 0 inserts at the position, and null reaches the end.

params.name: replacement
params.descHtml: The values to put in place of the range. Without it, the range is removed.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0", kept entries and replacement alike.

doc.shortHtml: Splits the entries into chunks of $size entries. The last chunk is shorter when the count does not divide evenly.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to split.

params.name: size
params.descHtml: How many entries each chunk has; at least 1.

params.name: preserveKeys
params.descHtml: Keeps each entry's own key inside its chunk. By default every chunk is renumbered from "0".

doc.returnHtml: A list of chunks. The empty array gives no chunks.

errors.descHtml: $size is 0.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the array with every given value added after its last entry. It works like $a[] = $v, written as an expression.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to extend.

params.name: values
params.descHtml: The values to add, in written order.

doc.returnHtml: The entries of $a under their own keys, then each value under the next free integer key. That key is one past the largest key present. With no values, the result is $a itself.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the given values, then the values of the array.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to put them in front of.

params.name: values
params.descHtml: The values to put in front, in written order.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0". Every key is discarded, because a value put in front has no key of its own.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every entry except the first. first returns the value it removes.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to shorten.

doc.returnHtml: The remaining entries under their own keys, never renumbered; the empty array for an array of one entry or none.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every entry except the last. last returns the value it removes.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to shorten.

doc.returnHtml: The remaining entries under their own keys, never renumbered; the empty array for an array of one entry or none.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every entry whose value is not null. The type of the values no longer includes null.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to remove null values from.

doc.returnHtml: The other entries under their own keys, never renumbered. Core\Arr::values renumbers them.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to reverse.

doc.returnHtml: The same entries, last first.

doc.shortHtml: Makes every value a key, and every key its value.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to flip. Every value must be an int or a string. 1 and "1" become the same key.

doc.returnHtml: The old keys as string values, stored under the old values as keys, in first-occurrence order. A repeated value keeps its first position and takes its last key.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: An array of arrays.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0". The inner keys are discarded, because two inner arrays can have the same key.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: An array nested to any depth.

doc.returnHtml: A list of every value that is not an array, in order, renumbered from "0". Its type is mixed, because the depth depends on the data and not on the type.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The rows, each an array.

params.name: column
params.descHtml: The key of the cell to take; 0 and "0" name one cell, as $row[0] and $row["0"] do.

params.name: indexBy
params.descHtml: The key of the cell to use as the result's key. By default the result gets new integer keys.

doc.returnHtml: The cells in row order. A row without the column is skipped. A row without the indexBy cell goes under the next free integer key. When two rows have the same indexBy value, the last one is kept.

members.name: sort
members.signature: sort(array<T> $a, { by?: callable, order?: Core\Arr::Order, comparator?: callable, preserveKeys?: bool }): array<T>

doc.shortHtml: Returns the entries in order. The sort is stable, so equal entries keep their order. Four options choose the sort value, the direction, the comparison and the keys.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to sort.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: Called once per entry as ($value, $key), and may declare fewer parameters. Its result is compared instead of the entry.

params.name: order
params.descHtml: Core\Arr::Order::Asc (the default) or Core\Arr::Order::Desc. Desc reverses the comparison, so equal entries keep their relative order.

params.name: comparator
params.descHtml: Called as ($a, $b) on two values, or on two results of by. It returns a negative number, zero or a positive number. It replaces the natural order.

params.name: preserveKeys
params.descHtml: Keeps the key of each entry. By default, the result has new keys from "0".

doc.returnHtml: The sorted entries. A natural order exists only between two numbers, two strings (compared byte by byte), two bools or two nulls. "10" sorts before "9".

errors.descHtml: Two entries have no natural order and no comparator was given. An int and a string have no natural order, and neither does any object. The error is also thrown when the comparator returns NaN.

members.name: sortByKey
members.signature: sortByKey(array<T> $a, { order?: Core\Arr::Order, comparator?: callable, keys?: array<int|string> }): array<T>

doc.shortHtml: Returns the entries in key order. The sort is stable, and every key is kept.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to sort.

params.name: order
params.descHtml: Core\Arr::Order::Asc (the default) or Core\Arr::Order::Desc. Desc reverses the comparison, so equal keys keep their insertion order.

params.name: comparator
params.descHtml: Called as ($a, $b) on two keys, both strings. It returns a negative number, zero or a positive number. It replaces the natural order.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The keys to put first, in this order. The other keys follow in their current order. A listed key that $a does not have is skipped. With Desc, the other keys come first, then the listed keys from last to first.

doc.returnHtml: The same entries under the same keys, ordered by key; the natural order is bytewise, so "10" precedes "9".

errors.descHtml: The comparator returned NaN.
The call gives both keys and comparator.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $count copies of $value under the keys "0", "1", …. There is no start index. Use fillKeys to choose the keys.

params.descHtml: How many entries; 0 yields the empty array.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value of every entry.

params.descHtml: The first value.

params.name: end
params.descHtml: The last value that may appear. When a step goes past it, the list stops at the last value inside the range.

params.descHtml: The distance between two neighbouring values, 1 by default. It is always positive, because $start and $end set the direction.

errors.descHtml: step is 0 or negative.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The keys, given as the array's values. Each is an int or a string. The array's own keys are ignored.

params.name: values
params.descHtml: The values, in the same order. The array's own keys are ignored.

doc.returnHtml: One entry per pair, in the order of $keys. A repeated key keeps its first position and takes its last value. 1 and "1" are the same key.

errors.descHtml: The two arrays have different numbers of entries.

doc.shortHtml: Reads a sequence into an array. The sequence can be an Iterable<T>, an Iterator<T> or an array: anything foreach accepts.

params.descHtml: The sequence to read. It is read once.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: Stops after this many elements. It is the only protection against a generator that never ends. By default every element is taken, and 0 takes nothing.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0". An iterator has no keys, and the keys of an array are discarded.

doc.shortHtml: Writes the entries of every layer over $base. Where two have the same key, the value from the later array is kept. Integer keys and string keys work the same way.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The array underneath.

params.name: layers
params.descHtml: The arrays to write over it, in order. A later layer replaces the values of an earlier one.

doc.returnHtml: Every key of every argument. An existing key keeps its position and takes the last value written under it. A new key is appended.

doc.shortHtml: Works like overlay. Where both sides of a key are arrays and neither is a list, it combines them the same way. A list is replaced as a whole.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The array underneath.

params.name: layers
params.descHtml: The arrays to write over it, in order. A later layer replaces the values of an earlier one.

doc.returnHtml: Every key of every argument, as overlay returns them. When both values under one key are maps, they are combined the same way, and the later map does not replace the earlier one.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The array on top.

params.name: layers
params.descHtml: The arrays to add under it, in order. The value of an earlier layer is kept over the value of a later one.

doc.returnHtml: $base's entries in their own positions, then each layer's keys not yet present, appended in order.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every value of $a, then of each array in $others, under new keys.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The first array.

params.name: others
params.descHtml: The arrays whose values follow, in order.

doc.returnHtml: A list renumbered from "0"; every key is discarded.

members.signature: diff(array<T> $a, array<T> $b, { on?: Core\Arr::SetOn, by?: callable, comparator?: callable }): array<T>

doc.shortHtml: Returns the entries of $a that $b does not have. Entries are compared by strict identity. The options choose what is compared, and how.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array whose entries are kept.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The entries of $a that are also in this array are removed.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: Called once per entry as ($value, $key), and may declare fewer parameters. Its result replaces the part on selected. Under Core\Arr::SetOn::Keys, that part is the key.

params.name: comparator
params.descHtml: Called as ($a, $b) on two selected parts. It returns a negative number, zero or a positive number. It replaces identity, and every entry of $a is then compared with every entry of $b.

params.descHtml: Called once per entry as ($value, $key), and may declare fewer parameters. It returns the group's name, an int or a string. Without it, the value itself is the group.

doc.returnHtml: One uint per distinct group, keyed by the group in first-occurrence order. 1 and "1" are the same group.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to deduplicate.

params.descHtml: Called once per entry as ($value, $key), and may declare fewer parameters. Its result is compared by identity, but the entry itself is what is kept.

doc.returnHtml: The first occurrence of each value, under its own key and in its own position.

params.descHtml: The array to search.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to search.

doc.returnHtml: The largest value, the first of equals; null for the empty array. Two strings compare bytewise, so max(["1e2", "50"]) is "50".

errors.descHtml: Two entries have no natural order, such as an int and a string, or any object.

doc.shortHtml: Adds the entries together. int with int stays int. A float anywhere makes the total a float, and a decimal anywhere makes it a decimal.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The numbers to add.

doc.returnHtml: The total, of the widest type met; 0 as an int for the empty array.

errors.descHtml: The running int or decimal total goes outside its type's range. It is never converted to float. The error is also thrown when one array has both a float and a decimal, because they have no common type.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The numbers to multiply.

doc.returnHtml: The product, of the widest type met; 1 as an int for the empty array.

errors.descHtml: The running int or decimal product goes outside its type's range. It is never converted to float. The error is also thrown when one array has both a float and a decimal, because they have no common type.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the mean of the entries.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The numbers to average.

doc.returnHtml: A decimal when the total is a decimal, and a float otherwise; null for the empty array. A decimal result is exact, rounded half to even at the widest scale the quotient allows.

errors.descHtml: The running total goes outside its type's range, or the array has both a float and a decimal, as in sum. The error is also thrown when a decimal quotient is outside the range of decimal.

doc.shortHtml: Reads $a as the type T written at the call site. T is an inline shape such as { name: T }, or a class with #[Json\Derive]. Each field that T names is converted with as, and other keys are left out. Write array<T> to read a list.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The loose values to read: a form, a query string, a decoded document, or an array a program built. Text from outside the program is tainted, so a text field of T that it fills must be tainted too.

doc.returnHtml: A new T where every field has its declared type. For an array<T>, one T per entry, in the array's own order.

errors.descHtml: A field that T requires is missing, or as cannot convert its value to the declared type. Every failed field is one issue on the error, at its own dotted path. A form can then show the whole list of problems.
T is a class without #[Json\Derive], so there is no field list to read $a against.

classes.summaryHtml:
Works with arrays. It finds, sorts, changes and combines elements. Every method returns a new array, and the array you pass in does not change.

Core\Arr has the array functions as static methods. Each one returns a new array and never changes its argument. Core\Arr::sort returns the sorted array, and append returns the longer one. Keys are always string: $a[0] and $a["0"] are the same entry, keys returns array<string>, and a callback's key parameter is string. A callback receives ($value, $key) and may declare fewer parameters. reduce passes the carry first. A missing value is null: first, last, find, keyOf and min return null for an empty array. count returns a uint. $a + $b does not compile. overlay and underlay combine maps, and appendAll joins lists.

shapeAs<T> is the one member that answers something other than an array. It reads its subject as the type written at the call site — an inline shape, { name: string, score: int }, or a class carrying #[Core\Json\Derive] — converting every named field with as and leaving every key the type does not name behind, so a form carrying a CSRF token does not break a handler reading two fields out of it. That is the whole story for loose input: an array<T> is homogeneous and there is no per-key-typed one, so a form, a query string or a decoded document is converted once, at the boundary, where a failure is still a 400 — and nothing downstream is left holding a mixed to check. A field that is absent, or that holds a value as refuses for its declared type, throws ParseError carrying every field that failed at its own dotted path, rather than the first of them. { name?: T } marks a key that may be absent, and ?? and isset read one without throwing. Core\Request::queryAs and postAs are this member over what a request carried. Text that came from outside the program, such as a form or an array<mixed>, is tainted. A text field it fills must then be declared tainted too.

<?nvs
array<int> $scores = ['ada' => 92, 'bo' => 67, 'cy' => 85, 'di' => 74];
var $passed = Core\Arr::filter($scores, fn(int $n): bool => $n >= 70);
echo Core\Json::encode($passed), "\n";
var $ranked = Core\Arr::sort($passed, { order: Core\Arr::Order::Desc, preserveKeys: true });
echo Core\Json::encode(Core\Arr::keys($ranked)), "\n";
echo Core\Arr::first($ranked) ?? 0, ' ', Core\Arr::firstKey($ranked) ?? '-', "\n";
var $labels = Core\Arr::map($scores, fn(int $n, string $k): string => $k . ':' . ($n as string));
echo Core\Str::join(Core\Arr::values($labels), ' '), "\n";
echo Core\Arr::sum($scores), ' ', Core\Arr::count($scores), ' ', Core\Arr::average($scores) ?? 0, "\n";
int $total = Core\Arr::reduce($scores, fn(int $carry, int $n): int => $carry + $n, 0);
echo $total, ' ', Core\Arr::max($scores) ?? 0, "\n";
array<int> $evens = Core\Arr::filter(Core\Arr::range(1, 10), fn(int $n): bool => $n % 2 == 0);
echo Core\Json::encode(Core\Arr::values($evens)), ' ', Core\Arr::contains($evens, 4) ? 'yes' : 'no', "\n";
var $byLength = Core\Arr::groupBy(['fig', 'pear', 'kiwi', 'plum'], fn(string $w): int => Core\Str::length($w) as int);
echo Core\Json::encode($byLength), "\n";

echo $entry->name, ' ', $entry->score as string, ' ', $entry->note ?? 'no note', "\n";

classes.name: Core\Attributes
classes.summary: Reads the attributes written on a class, a method, a property or a parameter. You give the shape you want, and the compiler finds the matching attribute. The call costs nothing when the program runs.

params.descHtml: The class or function whose attributes are read.

doc.returnHtml: The payload object of the matching attribute, as T. The result is null when no attribute matches T. When more than one matches, the code does not compile, and the error names all<T> as the fix. A payload matches when it has at least the fields of T. So the empty shape {} matches every attribute, and a marker type with no fields gives that compile error when the target has a second attribute.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every attribute on $target, or on the part of it named $member, whose payload object matches the shape T written at the call site. nvs check finds them and replaces the call with the result, so nothing runs.

params.name: target
params.descHtml: The class or function whose attributes are read.

params.name: member

classes.summaryHtml:
Reads the attributes written on a class, a method, a property or a parameter. You give the shape you want, and the compiler finds the matching attribute. The call costs nothing when the program runs.

Core\Attributes::get<T> returns the one attribute on a target whose payload object satisfies the shape T written at the call site, or null; all<T> returns every one in declaration order, as array<T>. Retrieval is structural. A payload object attached bare (#[{ audit: true }]) or under a type name (#[Route(path: "/x")]) is found by any shape it satisfies, extra fields included. The target is a class's Class::constructor or a method's Class::method reference, and the second argument names one of its properties or parameters; the call is resolved in nvs check, so a computed member name answers nothing, and two matches for get is a compile error naming all.

<?nvs
type Route = { path: string };

#[Route(path: '/users')]
#[{ audit: true }]
class Controller
{
    #[{ column: 'name', unique: true }]
    public string $name = '';

    #[Route(path: '/show')]
    public static function show(#[{ inject: 'repo' }] int $id): int
    {
        return $id;
    }
}

?Route $route = Core\Attributes::get<Route>(Controller::constructor);
echo 'class: ', $route?->path ?? 'none', "\n";
?{ audit: bool } $audit = Core\Attributes::get<{ audit: bool }>(Controller::constructor);
echo 'audit: ', ($audit != null ? 'yes' : 'no'), "\n";
?{ column: string } $column = Core\Attributes::get<{ column: string }>(Controller::constructor, 'name');
echo 'column: ', $column?->column ?? 'none', "\n";
?Route $method = Core\Attributes::get<Route>(Controller::show);
echo 'method: ', $method?->path ?? 'none', "\n";
?{ inject: string } $param = Core\Attributes::get<{ inject: string }>(Controller::show, 'id');
echo 'param: ', $param?->inject ?? 'none', "\n";
array<Route> $none = Core\Attributes::all<Route>(Controller::show, 'id');
echo 'none: ', Core\Arr::count($none), "\n";
class: /users
audit: yes
column: name
method: /show
param: repo
none: 0

classes.summaryHtml:
Works with binary data, the bytes type. It reads, searches, compares and builds buffers, and converts values to and from a fixed binary format, such as a network message header.

Core\Bytes reads and builds bytes — a buffer of octets with no character in it. Every position, length and count is a byte offset: length is O(1), at answers one octet as a uint, and a negative index counts from the end — where Core\Str counts graphemes. A bytes value cannot be written directly in the code, and there is no . over buffers: a buffer is written through Core\Encoding (fromHex, encodeText), joined with join, built with fill and repeat, and laid out as a wire format with pack and unpack, whose code table names every field's width and byte order outright and refuses a value outside the field's range.

<?nvs
bytes $png = Core\Encoding::fromHex('89504e470d0a1a0a');
echo Core\Bytes::length($png), ' ', Core\Bytes::at($png, 0), ' ', Core\Bytes::at($png, -1), "\n";
echo Core\Bytes::startsWith($png, Core\Encoding::fromHex('89504e47')) ? 'png' : 'other', "\n";
echo Core\Encoding::toHex(Core\Bytes::slice($png, 1, 3)), ' ', Core\Bytes::indexOf($png, Core\Encoding::fromHex('0d0a')) ?? 'none', "\n";
bytes $header = Core\Bytes::pack('NnC', 305419896, 4660, 255);
echo Core\Encoding::toHex($header), "\n";
var $fields = Core\Bytes::unpack($header, 'NnC');
echo Core\Json::encode($fields), "\n";
array<bytes> $parts = [$header, Core\Bytes::fill(2, 0)];
bytes $frame = Core\Bytes::join($parts);
echo Core\Bytes::length($frame), ' ', Core\Encoding::toHex($frame), "\n";
echo Core\Bytes::compare(Core\Encoding::fromHex('01'), Core\Encoding::fromHex('02')), "\n";
8 137 10
png
504e47 4
123456781234ff
[305419896,4660,255]
9 123456781234ff0000
-1

doc.shortHtml: Returns the cache in the memory of this server process. Every request this process serves reads the same entries. The cache is empty again when the process stops. Use it for ordinary application caching.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Cache\Store for the entries of this process. Every request this process serves can read them. An entry can be missing at any time. The cache deletes old entries to stay under its size limit, and another server process has its own entries. If your program is wrong when get returns null, use shared instead.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the cache in the external store that [cache.shared] url names. Every server process and every machine that uses this store reads the same entries.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Cache\Store for the configured shared store. Every server process that uses the store reads the same entries.

errors.descHtml: The program does not have the capability cache.shared. Or no [cache.shared] url is set, or the client cannot read that URL. Each of these is a missing setting, not a failed store.
The configured store cannot be reached. The call throws this error. It does not return null, because a missing entry and a failed store mean different things.

classes.summaryHtml:
Keeps values between requests. memory keeps them in the memory of the server process. shared keeps them in an external store such as Redis. Each one returns a Core\Cache\Store.

Core\Cache keeps a value after the request that made it ends. It has two caches, and both return a Core\Cache\Store with the same methods: put, get, forget, putSecret and getSecret.

**Core\Cache::memory() keeps values in the memory of this server process.** Every core of one nvs serve, or the one nvs run, sees the same values. It needs no configuration and no network, so it is fast. A restart empties it, and a second server process or machine does not see it. Use it for ordinary caching: a slow result, a parsed template, a table that many requests read.

**Core\Cache::shared() is a store on the network,** such as Redis, at the [cache.shared] url the person who runs the server sets. Every process on every machine sees the same values, and they stay after a restart. Use it when another server must find the value, or when your program would be wrong if the value were missing: a session, a lock, a quota.

The memory cache has a size limit, [cache.memory] max_size. When it is full, it forgets the value written longest ago, and put does not fail. On both caches any get may return null, so your program must be able to build the value again. put copies the value into the cache, and get returns a copy.

<?nvs
var $cache = Core\Cache::memory();
echo $cache->get('greeting') ?? 'not in the cache', "\n";

// Every request on this server can now read this value.
$cache->put('greeting', 'hello', { ttl: 30s });
echo $cache->get('greeting') ?? 'not in the cache', "\n";

$cache->forget('greeting');
echo $cache->get('greeting') ?? 'forgotten', "\n";
not in the cache
hello
forgotten

classes.name: Core\Cache\SecretEntry
classes.summary: A secret and how long it stays valid, such as a token and the time until it expires. The `fill` function of `getSecret` returns one.

doc.shortHtml: Creates the entry that a getSecret fill returns. It contains the secret that the fill fetched, and how long that secret stays valid.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The secret to store. A plain string is also accepted. The call does not change whether a value is secret. Only the type of the value decides that.

params.name: ttl
params.descHtml: How long the entry stays readable, counted from the moment it is stored. Use the lifetime that the source of the secret gives, such as a token's expiry.

doc.returnHtml: The entry. It has no methods to read the secret or the lifetime. A fill returns it, and your program reads the secret with getSecret.

classes.summaryHtml: A secret and how long it stays valid, such as a token and the time until it expires. The fill function of getSecret returns one.

classes.name: Core\Cache\Store
classes.summary: One cache, from `Core\Cache`. It saves a copy of a value under a key and returns a copy when you read it. A change to the value after you save it does not change the cache.

doc.shortHtml: Saves a copy of $value in the store under $key. It replaces any value already there. The copy is deep, so the entry shares nothing with the request that wrote it.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name to store under. A tainted string is allowed, because the key is never part of a returned value.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to copy in. It cannot be a callable or a secret. The same rule applies to a value sent to an isolate.

params.name: ttl
params.descHtml: How long the entry stays readable, counted from this call. Without it, the entry stays until the cache deletes it to stay under its size limit, or until another put replaces it. A ttl of zero or less deletes the entry under the key and stores nothing.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A later get can still return null, because an entry can be deleted at any time.

errors.descHtml: The value cannot be stored. It is or contains a callable, or an object with a secret property that was not revealed.
Only on a shared cache: the store cannot be reached, or it does not accept the write.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a copy of the entry stored under $key. If there is no entry, it returns null.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name to read. A tainted string is allowed, as on put.

doc.returnHtml: The value as it was copied in, or null when there is no entry. An entry can be missing at any time, so your program has to handle null.

errors.descHtml: The entry contains a class that this program does not have. Core\Serialize::decode throws the same error. This happens when a new version of the program changes its classes but the store keeps old entries.
Only on a shared cache: the store cannot be reached. A missing entry returns null on both caches and is not an error.

doc.shortHtml: Deletes the entry under $key from this store. It works whether or not there is an entry.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name to delete. A tainted string is allowed, as on put.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. If there is no entry under the key, the call does nothing. An entry can be missing at any time, so the call does not tell you whether there was one.

errors.descHtml: Only on a shared cache: the store cannot be reached, or it does not accept the command.

members.name: putSecret
members.signature: putSecret(string $key, secret string $value, Core\Time\Duration $ttl, array<secret bytes> $keys): void

doc.shortHtml: Encrypts $value with the newest key in $keys and stores the encrypted bytes under $key. This is the only way to put a secret in a cache. The cache never contains the unencrypted value.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name to store under. A tainted string is allowed, as on put. The name is part of the encrypted entry. If the entry is moved to another name, it cannot be decrypted.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The secret to store. A plain string is also accepted. The call does not change whether a value is secret. Only the type of the value decides that.

params.name: ttl
params.descHtml: How long the secret stays readable, counted from this call. It is required. The lifetime is also stored inside the encrypted entry, so a copy of the entry written back later still expires at the same time.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The list of keys, newest first, in the same format as for Core\SignedCookie. The newest key encrypts. Every key in the list can decrypt. After you add a new key, entries written with an older key in the list can still be read.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. Code that knows the entry's name but not the keys cannot read it. A changed, moved or replayed entry reads as missing. This does not protect a secret from a compromised process, because the keys are in the same memory.

errors.descHtml: $keys is empty, or one of its keys does not have the required length. This is a bug in the program, so it throws an error and is not treated as missing.
Only on a shared cache: the store cannot be reached, or it does not accept the write.

members.name: getSecret
members.signature: getSecret(string $key, array<secret bytes> $keys, { fill?: callable(): Core\Cache\SecretEntry, wait?: Core\Time\Duration }): ?secret string

doc.shortHtml: Decrypts the secret stored under $key, trying every key in $keys. If no key can decrypt it, the result is null.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name to read. Use the same name as in putSecret, because the name is part of the encrypted entry.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The list of keys, newest first. Every key is tried. After you add a new key, an entry encrypted with an older key in the list can still be read.

params.name: fill
params.descHtml: A callable that runs when the entry is missing. It returns a Core\Cache\SecretEntry with the secret and how long it stays valid. Only one caller in this process runs it, while the others wait. It runs in that caller's request, with that caller's capabilities. If fill throws, the waiting callers get no value, and the next caller runs fill again. An error in one request never reaches another request.

params.name: wait
params.descHtml: How long this caller waits for another caller's fill. The default is [cache.memory] fill_wait. You cannot wait forever.

doc.returnHtml: The secret, or null. An entry that no key in $keys can decrypt returns null. An expired entry also returns null. Neither is an error, so after a key change the secret is fetched again. A plain get on the same name also returns null, because getSecret is the only way to read a secret.

errors.descHtml: $keys is empty, or one of its keys does not have the required length, as on putSecret. It is also thrown when fill reads the same key it is filling, because that call would wait for itself.
Another caller in this process was still running fill when this call's wait was up, which defaults to [cache.memory] fill_wait.
Only on a shared cache: the store cannot be reached. A missing entry returns null, as on get.

classes.summaryHtml: One cache, from Core\Cache. It saves a copy of a value under a key and returns a copy when you read it. A change to the value after you save it does not change the cache.

classes.name: Core\Cap
classes.summary: Checks whether the running code has a capability, such as `fs.write`. Code can use it to skip a feature that is not allowed. It never grants a capability.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether the code running here has $capability at this point in the request. The check starts from the capabilities in nvs.toml. Any capability that the request or an enclosing isolate gave up is removed. This call grants nothing, and the guarded code is still checked when it runs.

params.name: capability
params.descHtml: A capability name as nvs.toml writes it, such as fs.read or net.connect. A literal name that is not a capability does not compile. A computed name that is not a capability returns false.

doc.returnHtml: true when the capability is granted for at least something, and false otherwise. A true does not mean every path or host is allowed. A grant limited to some paths still throws an error for a path outside them.

classes.summaryHtml: Checks whether the running code has a capability, such as fs.write. Code can use it to skip a feature that is not allowed. It never grants a capability.

classes.name: Core\Cldr
classes.summary: Plural rules for many languages. They pick the word form for a count, such as "1 file" or "2 files", and for a position, such as "1st" or "2nd".

doc.shortHtml: The six CLDR plural forms. The names are labels for the forms of a language, not numbers. Only Other means the same thing in every language. Most languages use only some of the six.
Returns the CLDR plural form of $count in $locale. A message catalog can choose its text with the rule of each language. A test such as == 1 is not enough for many languages.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: The number the message is about. A decimal keeps its digits after the point. So 1.0 and 1 can give different forms in a language whose rules read the fraction. An int has no fraction. A float is read with the digits it prints.

params.name: locale
params.descHtml: A BCP 47 tag. Only the language part is read, and case is ignored. So en-GB, en_US and EN all give the result for en.

doc.returnHtml: The plural category of $count in this language. It is Other for every count in a language that has no plural forms.

errors.descHtml: The tag has no language part, or Novis has no rules for its language. Novis never uses the rules of another language instead.
$count is a float that is not finite. It is also thrown for a float that prints more digits than the rules can check.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the form of $count as a position in a list, such as 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th in English. A template can use it to choose the right ending for the language.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: The position the message is about. The CLDR rules for positions are for whole numbers, so a count with a fraction gives Other. Macedonian and Georgian are different, because their rules read only the whole-number part.

params.name: locale
params.descHtml: A BCP 47 tag, read the same way as in pluralCategory. Only the language part is read, and case is ignored.

doc.returnHtml: The category of $count as a position in this language. It is Other for every count in a language with no special forms for positions, which is most languages.

errors.descHtml: The tag has no language part, or Novis has no plural rules and no position rules for its language. A language with plural rules but no position forms does not throw. It returns Other.
$count is a float that is not finite. It is also thrown for a float that prints more digits than the rules can check.

classes.summaryHtml: Plural rules for many languages. They pick the word form for a count, such as "1 file" or "2 files", and for a position, such as "1st" or "2nd".

classes.name: Core\Cli
classes.summary: Works with the terminal in a command-line program. It gives the program's arguments and the terminal's size and colours, asks the user questions, and shows output that updates in place.

doc.shortHtml: One of the three standard streams a process starts with. Whether output goes to a terminal is always checked for one stream, not for the whole process.
How much colour standard output can show. The cases are in increasing order, so you can compare two depths.

Returns the arguments this program was started with, without the program name. A program that declares a #[Command] gets its arguments from Core\Command::run instead. This is the raw list, for a program that parses its own arguments.
doc.returnHtml: An array<tainted string>, in the order the shell passed them. It is empty if the program was started with no arguments. Every element is tainted, because the words come from outside the program. A path, a URL or a query built from one must pass the check for that use first. The program name is not in the array, so you do not need to skip it. There is no $argv[0].

members.name: write
members.signature: write(string|Core\Cli\Text $value, { stream?: Core\Cli::Stream, newline?: bool }): void

doc.shortHtml: Writes $value to a standard stream. In a string, every control byte is replaced by the visible symbol that Core\Cli::escape gives it. A Core\Cli\Text is written unchanged, because its control bytes were already made safe.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The text to write. A tainted value is written like any other. Replacing the control bytes makes it safe for the terminal, so no other check is needed. A secret value is a compile error.

params.name: stream
params.descHtml: Which standard stream to write to. The default is Out. Err writes to this request's diagnostic output, which Core\Out::capture does not capture. In throws an error.

params.name: newline
params.descHtml: Whether to add one LF after the value. The default is false, so the method writes exactly the value it was given.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The bytes are written to the stream. If the write fails, the request ends.

errors.descHtml: $stream is Core\Cli::Stream::In. A program reads standard input and never writes to it. The case exists for Core\Cli::isTty, which can check all three streams.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $text with every control byte replaced by a visible symbol. ESC becomes ␛, a bare CR becomes ␍ and DEL becomes ␡. A C1 code point or an unterminated bidirectional control becomes �. LF and TAB stay unchanged. echo already makes these replacements, so you need this only to keep the safe text as a value.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The text to make safe. The result is not tainted, because nothing is left in it that could control the terminal.

doc.returnHtml: The same text with these replacements, and no other change. This is not an HTML escaper, so <, & and " stay unchanged.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether one standard stream is attached to a terminal. The check is made once for the process, so two calls in one run always give the same result.

params.name: stream
params.descHtml: Which stream to check. Each stream is checked on its own. A common case is standard output on a terminal while standard input is a pipe.

doc.returnHtml: true when that stream is a terminal, false when it is a pipe, a file or closed.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the width of the terminal in columns. It works like tput cols, without starting a child process. It is read once for the process.
doc.returnHtml: The column count, or 80 when no standard stream is a terminal. Never 0, so a caller may subtract a margin from it without checking.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the height of the terminal in rows, like tput lines. It is read once for the process, together with the width.
doc.returnHtml: The row count, or 24 when no standard stream is a terminal. It is never 0, as for width.

doc.shortHtml: Returns how much colour standard output can show. It follows NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE, FORCE_COLOR, COLORTERM and TERM. Most programs do not need it, because a Cli\Text is always written with the colours the terminal has. It is read once for the process.
doc.returnHtml: The depth as a Core\Cli::ColorDepth case. It is None when standard output is not a terminal and no setting forces colour on. So myprog | grep and a CI log get plain text.

doc.shortHtml: Returns how many terminal columns $value uses when it is written. Widths follow UAX #11 and are counted per grapheme (what a person counts as one character). A CJK ideograph and a fullwidth Latin letter use two columns, and a combining mark uses none. A control byte uses the width of the visible symbol the terminal shows for it.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The text to measure. A tainted value is allowed, because a column count contains nothing from the text.

doc.returnHtml: The column count. A tab moves to the next multiple of eight, and a newline ends the row. For text with several rows, the result is the width of the widest row. That is the width to pad a box to.

members.name: ask
members.signature: ask(string $question, { default?: string, validate?: callable }): tainted string

doc.shortHtml: Shows $question on the terminal and returns the line the user types. It works like readline. It does not read standard input, so a program that reads piped data can still ask. With no terminal, it returns default if one was given, and throws an error otherwise. It never waits for an answer that nobody can give.

params.name: question
params.descHtml: The text to show on the terminal. Control bytes are replaced as echo replaces them. So a question built from untrusted text cannot move the cursor or redraw the screen around the answer.

params.name: default
params.descHtml: The value returned when there is no terminal, or when the user types an empty line. Without it, both cases throw Core\Cli\NotInteractive.

params.name: validate
params.descHtml: A function called with each answer. If it returns a falsy value, the question is asked again. It runs only when there is a terminal, so it is never called with default.

doc.returnHtml: The line the user typed, without the line ending. It is always tainted, because it comes from outside the program, like a request body.

errors.descHtml: The call has no default, and there is no terminal, its input ended, or nobody answered before the prompt deadline.

doc.shortHtml: Asks $question as a yes/no question and returns the answer. The prompt shows what the Enter key means. If the answer is neither yes nor no, the question is asked again.

params.name: question
params.descHtml: The text to show on the terminal. Control bytes are replaced as in ask.

params.name: default
params.descHtml: The answer for an empty line, and for a run with no terminal. Without it, a run with no terminal throws an error, and an empty line asks again.

doc.returnHtml: true for yes and false for no. It is a plain bool and is never tainted, because only yes or no is kept from what was typed.

errors.descHtml: The call has no default, and there is no terminal, its input ended, or nobody answered before the prompt deadline.

members.name: select
members.signature: select(string $question, array<T> $choices, { labels?: callable, default?: T }): T

doc.shortHtml: Shows $choices as a numbered list and returns the one the user chooses. It returns the value itself, not its position in the array.

params.name: question
params.descHtml: The text to show above the list. Control bytes are replaced as in ask.

params.name: choices
params.descHtml: The values to choose from, listed in their own order. An empty array throws a LogicError, because there is nothing to return.

params.name: labels
params.descHtml: A function called with each option. It returns the line shown for that option. Without it, each option is shown as text, as echo would show it.

params.name: default
params.descHtml: The choice for an empty line, and for a run with no terminal. It has the element type of $choices, so it cannot be a value that is not offered.

doc.returnHtml: The chosen element of $choices, with that array's element type.

errors.descHtml: The call has no default, and there is no terminal, its input ended, or nobody answered before the prompt deadline.
$choices is empty, so there is nothing that could be chosen.

doc.shortHtml: Shows $choices as a numbered list and returns every value the user chooses. It works like select, but the user can choose several values. The numbers are typed together on one line, and an empty line chooses none.

params.name: question
params.descHtml: The text to show above the list. Control bytes are replaced as in ask. The valid range and separator are added after it, as confirm adds [y/n].

params.name: choices
params.descHtml: The values to choose from, listed in their own order. An empty array throws a LogicError, because there is nothing to choose.

params.name: labels
params.descHtml: A function called with each option. It returns the line shown for that option. Without it, each option is shown as text, as echo would show it.

doc.returnHtml: The chosen elements of $choices, in the array's own order and each at most once. The order they were typed in does not matter. An empty line returns an empty array. There is no default, so a run with no terminal throws an error.

errors.descHtml: There is no terminal, its input ended, or nobody answered before the prompt deadline. This prompt has no default to use instead.
$choices is empty, so there is nothing that could be chosen.

doc.shortHtml: Prints $question and reads the answer with the terminal's echo turned off. A password typed here does not stay on the screen or in the scrollback buffer.

params.name: question
params.descHtml: The text to show on the terminal. Control bytes are replaced as in ask.

doc.returnHtml: The line typed, both secret and tainted. It cannot be used in output, logs, dumps, Throwable messages or serialization. Like any tainted value, it must still pass the check for each place where it is used.

errors.descHtml: There is no terminal, its input ended, or nobody answered before the prompt deadline. secret has no default, because a password that nobody typed is not a password.

doc.shortHtml: Runs $body with a live area open on the terminal, and returns what $body returns. $body gets a Core\Cli\Live, whose set method replaces the area's rows in place. Use it in place of cursor commands like moveUp and clearLine. Those break when output is piped, and can leave the shell unusable if the program stops.

params.name: body
params.descHtml: The work to do while the area is open. Its return value is the return value of this method.

doc.returnHtml: Exactly what $body returned, with the same type. The terminal is restored however $body ends: a return, a throw, a fatal error or an internal panic. If the output is not a terminal, nothing is drawn, so no escape sequences are written.

doc.shortHtml: Runs $body with a progress bar open on the terminal, and returns what $body returns. It is a special case of live. The runtime draws the bar, and the program only counts up to $total.

params.name: total
params.descHtml: The number of units of work for a full bar. A total of 0 means the work is already done, and it draws a full bar.

params.name: body
params.descHtml: The work to do while the bar is open. Its return value is the return value of this method.

doc.returnHtml: Exactly what $body returned, with the same type, as for live.

classes.name: Core\Cli\Live
classes.summary: An area of the terminal that your program redraws while it works. `Core\Cli::live` gives one to your function. Each update replaces what the area showed before.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces the area's rows with $lines. The runtime controls the cursor. It redraws on a timer, not on every call, and writes only what changed on screen. It writes nothing if the run has no terminal.

params.name: lines
params.descHtml: The area's new rows, one Core\Cli\Text each. They replace the old rows. A row wider than the terminal is cut to the terminal width. It is not wrapped, because a wrapped row would stop the area from being redrawn.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The rows are drawn now, or together with the next update. A program cannot tell which. The last rows given are always drawn before the area closes.

errors.descHtml: This area is not the active one on the terminal. It has closed, or an inner Core\Cli::live is open inside it. A Cli\Live belongs to the call that made it. Using it outside that call is a bug in the program.

classes.summaryHtml: An area of the terminal that your program redraws while it works. Core\Cli::live gives one to your function. Each update replaces what the area showed before.

classes.name: Core\Cli\Progress
classes.summary: A progress bar that `Core\Cli::progress` gives to your function. Each step moves the counter forward and draws the bar again.

members.name: advance
members.signature: advance({ by?: uint, label?: string }): void

doc.shortHtml: Counts by units of work as done and redraws the bar, optionally changing the caption beside it.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: How many units this step finished. The default is 1.

params.name: label
params.descHtml: The caption next to the bar. Control bytes are replaced, as in every other terminal write. Without it, the caption does not change.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A count past the total shows a full bar. So a loop that counts too far draws a finished bar, not a broken one.

errors.descHtml: This bar is not the active area on the terminal. It has closed, or an inner area is open inside it. Core\Cli\Live::set throws for the same reasons.

classes.name: Core\Cli\Style

members.name: of
members.signature: of({ color?: Core\Cli\Color, background?: Core\Cli\Color, bold?: bool, dim?: bool, italic?: bool, underline?: bool, strikethrough?: bool }): Core\Cli\Style

doc.shortHtml: Creates a style as a value. Novis has no syntax for escape strings like "\e[1;31m" or markup like "<bold><red>", so you use this method instead.

params.name: background

params.name: bold

params.name: dim

classes.summaryHtml: How a piece of terminal text looks: its colours, and whether it is bold, underlined or struck through. A style does not change after you create it.

classes.name: Core\Cli\Text
classes.summary: Text for the terminal, which can have colours and styles. You join two pieces with `+`. Outside an HTTP request, `Core\Out::capture` returns the captured output as one.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $text as a Core\Cli\Text, with every control byte replaced by the visible symbol that Core\Cli::escape gives it. echo writes a Text unchanged, so the replacement is made here.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The text to convert. The result is not tainted, for the same reason as in Core\Cli::escape. Nothing is left in it that could control the terminal.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Cli\Text with the safe text. You can join it with another Text, and echo writes it. It has no styling. Use styled for styling.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $text as a Core\Cli\Text with $style. Control bytes in the text are replaced as in plain. So the only control bytes in the result are the ones from the style.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The text to convert. The result is not tainted, for the same reason as in plain. An escape sequence in the text is replaced, so the terminal does not act on it.

params.name: style
params.descHtml: The style to use, as a value. Novis has no markup or escape syntax for styles.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Cli\Text with the safe text between the style's escape sequence and a reset. The style is drawn for the terminal this process has. When standard output is not a terminal, there is no styling.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the text of this Core\Cli\Text as a string, without its styling. The text of every styled part is joined, and its control bytes are already replaced. A Core\Out::capture filter reads this before it writes a new Text.
doc.returnHtml: The text alone, with no escape sequences from a Cli\Style. You can pass it straight back to plain or styled. Replacing the control bytes a second time does not change the text.

classes.summaryHtml:
Text for the terminal, which can have colours and styles. You join two pieces with +. Outside an HTTP request, Core\Out::capture returns the captured output as one.

Core\Cli\Text is what Core\Out::capture answers when the program is not serving an HTTP request: the bytes the captured code wrote, already past the terminal sink, carried as a value rather than as a string so that writing them out again does not escape them a second time. It has no members and no constructor. A Text is produced by Core\Out::capture, written by echo, joined with . like any other value, and turned into a string with as string; a parameter or binding declared string refuses it until it is converted. Styling, colour and the rest of a terminal surface are not on this class.

<?nvs
var $captured = Core\Out::capture(fn(): void => {
    echo 'inner';
});

echo '[', $captured, "]\n";
echo 'joined: ' . $captured . "!\n";

string $text = $captured as string;
echo 'length=', Core\Str::length($text), "\n";
[inner]
joined: inner!
length=5

classes.name: Core\Command
classes.summary: Runs the commands a command-line program declares with `#[Command]` methods. It reads the command and its options from the program's arguments, and it prints a help page for each command.

doc.shortHtml: Which shell Core\Command::completions writes a completion script for. There are four cases and no case for other shells. Each script uses the syntax of its own shell, so each case needs its own generator.
Returns the help page for one command, or the list of all commands. Novis creates the page from the #[Command] methods when it compiles the program. You do not write the help text yourself.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The command to describe. Pass null to get the page that lists every command of the program.

doc.returnHtml: The page as a Core\Cli\Text, ending with a newline.

errors.descHtml: The program has no #[Command] with the name $name. The list of commands is fixed when the program compiles, so this is a mistake in the program.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the command line of this process and finds the #[Command] method that its first word names. It calls that method and returns the exit status for the process.
doc.returnHtml: The uint that the method returns, or 0 when the method returns void. A command line that matches no command is a usage error. Then the help page is printed to standard error, and the status is 2.

errors.descHtml: The method of the command is not a method of this program. It is also thrown when a parameter has a type that a command-line argument cannot be converted to yet. Both are mistakes in the program.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a tab-completion script for this program, in the syntax of the shell you choose. The script contains every command and every option of each command, the same as help.

params.name: shell
params.descHtml: The shell to write the script for.

doc.returnHtml: The script as plain text, ending with a newline. Save it in the completion directory of the shell.

errors.descHtml: The program has no name to register the script for. This is the case everywhere except in a command-line run, such as in a web request.

classes.summaryHtml: Runs the commands a command-line program declares with #[Command] methods. It reads the command and its options from the program's arguments, and it prints a help page for each command.

classes.name: Core\Compress
classes.summary: Compresses and decompresses data in a format you choose from `Core\Compress::Codec`, such as gzip. Decompression always has a size limit, so a small input cannot fill the server's memory.

doc.shortHtml: The format a Core\Compress method reads or writes. The first three are one deflate stream under three different headers. The last two are the other two Content-Encoding formats in use.
Compresses $data in the format $codec. The format is a case of Core\Compress::Codec.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The bytes to compress. A string is read as its UTF-8 bytes.

params.name: codec
params.descHtml: The format to write. Use Core\Compress::Codec::Gzip when you send the result over a network.

doc.returnHtml: The compressed data, as bytes. Compressing has no size limit, because the output is never much larger than the input.

doc.shortHtml: Decompresses $data from the format $codec. The output has a size limit that cannot be switched off.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The compressed data. If $data is tainted, the result is tainted too. Decompressing does not make data safe to use.

params.name: codec
params.descHtml: The format $data is in. The method does not detect the format. Data in another format throws an error.

params.name: maxBytes
params.descHtml: The most output this call produces, in bytes. It can be lower than [limits] max_decompressed, but not higher. 0 means zero bytes. It does not mean no limit.

params.name: maxRatio
params.descHtml: The most bytes of output for each byte of input. This is the second part of the size limit. A compression bomb is small data that decompresses to a huge size. With a limit in bytes alone, a small request can still reach that limit.

doc.returnHtml: The decompressed bytes. The result is never cut short. If the output would go over either limit, the method throws an error and returns no partial result.

errors.descHtml: $data is not valid data in the format $codec, or the output would go over either limit. It is never an IOError. A hostile archive and a full disk are different problems.

doc.shortHtml: Starts a compression in the format $codec that you feed in parts. It returns a Core\Compress\Compressor. Call add to add data and finish to get the result.

params.name: codec
params.descHtml: The format to write, any Core\Compress::Codec case. It cannot change while the stream is open, because one compressed result has one format.

doc.returnHtml: A new, open stream with no data in it yet.

doc.shortHtml: Starts a decompression from the format $codec that you feed in parts. It returns a Core\Compress\Decompressor. Call add to add data and finish to get the result. **It has the same size limit as decompress, which cannot be switched off.**

params.name: codec
params.descHtml: The format the parts are in. The method does not detect the format. Data in another format throws an error.

params.name: maxBytes
params.descHtml: The most output the whole stream produces, in bytes. It is checked against [limits] max_decompressed when the stream starts. The limit counts all parts together. It is not a limit for each add.

params.name: maxRatio
params.descHtml: The most bytes of output for each byte added to the stream. This is the second part of the size limit. It is measured against all the data that add received.

doc.returnHtml: A new, open stream with no data in it yet. It has the size limit it is checked against.

classes.summaryHtml: Compresses and decompresses data in a format you choose from Core\Compress::Codec, such as gzip. Decompression always has a size limit, so a small input cannot fill the server's memory.

classes.name: Core\Compress\Compressor
classes.summary: Compresses data that arrives in pieces. You add each piece, and `finish` returns the compressed data.

doc.shortHtml: Adds $data to the stream. finish compresses all parts in the order they were added.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The next bytes. A string is read as its UTF-8 bytes.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. finish returns all the compressed data at once.

errors.descHtml: The stream is already finished. Its result is complete, so start a new stream.

doc.shortHtml: Closes the stream and returns all the data that add received, compressed. The result is the same bytes Core\Compress::compress returns for all the parts joined.
doc.returnHtml: The compressed data, as bytes. After the call, the stream is finished and its parts are freed. The result is not tainted, even when the input is. Compressed data is not read as text anywhere.

errors.descHtml: The stream is already finished. A second finish throws this error and returns nothing.

classes.summaryHtml: Compresses data that arrives in pieces. You add each piece, and finish returns the compressed data.

classes.name: Core\Compress\Decompressor
classes.summary: Decompresses data that arrives in pieces. The whole result has a size limit, so a small input cannot fill the server's memory.

doc.shortHtml: Adds $data to the stream. finish decompresses all parts in the order they were added, with the size limit the stream started with.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The next bytes of the compressed data. Nothing is decompressed yet, so this call never throws a size error. finish checks the size limit for the whole stream.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The size limit counts the whole stream, not each call.

errors.descHtml: The stream is already finished. Its data cannot change, so start a new stream.

doc.shortHtml: Closes the stream and returns all the data that add received, decompressed. The result is the same bytes Core\Compress::decompress returns for all the parts joined, with the same size limit.
doc.returnHtml: The decompressed data as tainted bytes. The result is never cut short. After the call, the stream is finished and its parts are freed. The bytes are tainted because they come from input the program does not control.

errors.descHtml: The parts are not valid data in the stream's format, or the output would go over either limit the stream started with. The limit counts all parts together.
The stream is already finished. This is also true after a finish that threw an error.

classes.summaryHtml: Decompresses data that arrives in pieces. The whole result has a size limit, so a small input cannot fill the server's memory.

classes.name: Core\Config
classes.summary: Reads the settings of `nvs.toml` for the current request. You can change some settings for this request only, and reset them again.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value of one setting for this request. A setting this request changed with set gives the new value. Any other setting gives the value from the configuration file, or its built-in default.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The dotted name of the setting, such as log.level. A limit name alone is the setting of that name in [limits]. The limit names are memory, cpu_time, wall_time, max_tasks, max_output and max_regex_steps.

doc.returnHtml: The value as text, written the way the configuration file writes it, such as 128M or 30s. The result is null for a setting with no default, such as wall_time. It is also null for a name that has a group of settings or a list. A secret setting, such as db.main.password or http.csrf_key, gives a ?secret string. Your program cannot print it or write it to a log.

errors.descHtml: The name is a secret setting, and the call does not write it as a string literal. Write the name in the call, such as Core\Config::get('db.main.password').

doc.shortHtml: Changes a setting for this request only. Other requests do not see the change, and it ends when this request ends.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The name of the setting, in the same form that get uses.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value, written the way the configuration file writes it, such as 512M, 30s or 64.

doc.returnHtml: true when the change was made. false when it is not allowed, and the previous value stays in place. It is not allowed for a setting that only nvs.toml may set, or for a name that is not a setting. It is not allowed for a value that is not a valid size, duration or count. It is not allowed for a value above the limit's ceiling. The ceiling is [limits.hard], or the value the program started with when [limits.hard] does not set that limit. set never throws an error.

doc.shortHtml: Deletes this request's change to one setting. The value from the configuration file is in force again, or the built-in default when the file does not write the setting.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The name of the setting, in the same form that get uses.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A name this request never changed is not an error. There is nothing to undo.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every setting in force for this request, with the dotted names as keys. A setting this request changed has the new value. A setting the configuration file does not write has its built-in default.
doc.returnHtml: An array<string, string> sorted by name, with one entry per value. A name that has a group of settings gives one entry for each setting in it. A name that has a list gives no entry. A secret setting, such as db.main.password or http.csrf_key, has the value <secret>. get returns the real value.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a value your program reads from the [settings] block of nvs.toml. A value in the [app.settings] block of the application replaces the value in [settings].

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The name of the value, such as page_size. A value in a table, such as [settings.api] with base = "...", has the name api.base.

doc.returnHtml: The value with the type it has in the file. A TOML string is a string, an integer is an int, a float is a float and a boolean is a bool. A TOML array is an array, and a table is an array with the names as keys. The result is null when no block sets the name. Use as to convert it: Core\Config::setting('page_size') as int throws an error when the value is missing or is not a whole number.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a secret your program reads from the [secrets] block of nvs.toml, such as an API key. A secret in the [app.secrets] block of the application replaces the one in [secrets].

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The name of the secret, such as api_key. The block may write the value, or read it from a file with api_key_file. The name cannot come from the request.

doc.returnHtml: The secret as a ?secret string. Your program cannot print it or write it to a log. You can send it in an outgoing header, a form field or a database parameter. The result is null when no block sets the name.

classes.summaryHtml:
Reads the settings of nvs.toml for the current request. You can change some settings for this request only, and reset them again.

Core\Config reads and moves the configuration in force for the current request. Every value crosses as a string, spelled as nvs.toml would spell it ("512M", "30s"); a directive is named with dots (log.level), and a bare limit name — memory, cpu_time, wall_time, max_tasks, max_output — is the [limits] entry. set changes a directive for this request alone and answers false, leaving the value in place, for anything it may not do: a directive only the file may set, an unknown name, a value of the wrong shape, or a value above the [limits.hard] ceiling the operator kept. When [limits.hard] does not set a limit, its ceiling is the value the request started with, so a program cannot raise it. A program you start from the command line is the one exception: with no [limits.hard] memory, it may raise memory to any value. restore puts the file's value back, or the built-in default when the file does not write the key. get and all give the built-in default of every key the file does not write, such as 128M for memory. A key with no default, such as wall_time, is null.

[limits]
memory = "256M"

[limits.hard]
memory = "512M"
<?nvs
echo 'memory=', Core\Config::get('memory') ?? 'unset', "\n";

echo Core\Config::set('memory', '512M') ? 'raised to the ceiling' : 'refused', "\n";
echo Core\Config::set('memory', '1G') ? 'raised past it' : 'refused past the ceiling', "\n";
echo 'now=', Core\Config::get('limits.memory') ?? 'unset', "\n";

Core\Config::restore('memory');
echo 'restored=', Core\Config::get('memory') ?? 'unset', "\n";

echo Core\Config::set('no.such.directive', '1') ? 'set' : 'unknown name refused', "\n";
memory=256M
raised to the ceiling
refused past the ceiling
now=512M
restored=256M
unknown name refused

classes.name: Core\Crypto
classes.summary: Encryption, signatures and key derivation. Each algorithm is a case of an enum, so a wrong name does not compile. No method picks an algorithm for you.

doc.shortHtml: The authenticated encryption that seal and open use. There is no default, so each call names its cipher. Both cases are authenticated, so a message that was changed never opens.
Creates a new random key for seal and open. It uses the same secure random number generator as Core\Random. There is no key size argument, because the cipher has one key size.
doc.returnHtml: 32 bytes as secret bytes. secret is part of the type, so you cannot assign the key to a plain bytes. You also cannot print it with echo, log it or put it in a Throwable message.

doc.shortHtml: Encrypts and authenticates $message with $key, using the cipher $cipher. Each call uses a new random nonce. There is no argument for a mode, a padding or an IV, and no cipher name as a string. You choose a Core\Crypto::Cipher case, and every case is authenticated.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: The plaintext. A secret value is not allowed. To seal one, call Core\Secret::revealBytes first. Then a text search of your code finds every such place.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: A 32-byte key, such as generateKey returns. Both ciphers use a key of this size.

params.name: cipher
params.descHtml: The cipher to use. There is no default. Use XChaCha20Poly1305 when both ends are Novis, and Aes256Gcm when a browser must read the result.

doc.returnHtml: The sealed message. It is 40 bytes longer than $message with XChaCha20Poly1305, and 28 bytes longer with Aes256Gcm. It is different on every call for the same inputs, because each call uses its own nonce.

errors.descHtml: $key is not 32 bytes long, so it is not a key.
This process does not have enough memory for a buffer the size of the sealed message.

doc.shortHtml: Checks that $sealed is authentic for $key and $cipher, and returns the plaintext. If it is not authentic, it throws an error. A message with even one changed byte is not decrypted. This is why Core\Crypto has only authenticated ciphers.

params.name: sealed
params.descHtml: A message seal produced.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The 32-byte key that $sealed was sealed with.

params.name: cipher
params.descHtml: The cipher that $sealed was sealed with. With the other cipher, the message throws the same error as a forged message. You never get wrong bytes.

doc.returnHtml: The original plaintext, byte for byte.

errors.descHtml: $key is not 32 bytes long, so it is not a key.

$sealed is not an authentic message for $key and $cipher. It was changed, it is too short, or the key or the cipher is wrong. All these cases have the same message. A different message would tell an attacker which part of a forgery worked.

members.name: deriveKey
members.signature: deriveKey(secret string $password, bytes $salt, uint $iterations): secret bytes

doc.shortHtml: Derives a key from a password with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256. It computes $iterations rounds over $password and $salt. Use it for a value that a person typed. For material that is already uniformly random, use expandKey. The compiler does not stop you from passing a password to expandKey, so check which one you call.

params.name: password
params.descHtml: The password. A secret value is allowed, and it is not revealed. The result is secret bytes and contains no byte of the password.

params.name: salt
params.descHtml: At least 16 bytes. Make a new salt for each password, and store it next to the derived key. Core\Random::bytes(16) makes one. The salt is not a secret.

params.name: iterations
params.descHtml: How many rounds to compute, from 100,000 to 2,000,000. It is required and has no default. To derive the same key again later, you must use the same count as before.

doc.returnHtml: 32 bytes as secret bytes, the key size that seal and open use. The result is not random: the same three arguments always give the same key.

errors.descHtml: $iterations is less than 100,000 or more than 2,000,000, or $salt is shorter than 16 bytes. With fewer rounds, the key is easy to attack. With more rounds, one call uses so much CPU time that it blocks the process.

members.name: expandKey
members.signature: expandKey(secret bytes $material, bytes $salt, string $info): secret bytes

doc.shortHtml: Derives a key with HKDF-SHA256 from material that is already uniformly random. An example is a shared secret from a key agreement, or the root key of a service. $info names what the key is for. With a different $info, one secret gives a different key, so you never use the same secret in two places.

params.name: material
params.descHtml: The secret to expand. It must already be uniformly random. For a password, use deriveKey.

params.name: salt
params.descHtml: The salt of the extract step. It is not a secret, and it can be empty. An empty salt is the default of RFC 5869, a salt of zero bytes.

params.name: info
params.descHtml: The context string. Two calls with the same $material and a different $info give unrelated keys. So one secret can give keys for two uses.

doc.returnHtml: 32 bytes as secret bytes, the key size that seal and open use. The same three arguments always give the same key.

doc.shortHtml: Creates a new random private key of the kind $kind, and returns it as a key pair. It uses the same secure random number generator as Core\Random.
