errors.descHtml: The call is wrong, not the database. The placeholders and the array use different styles or different counts, a :name has no element, or an element cannot be bound. It is also thrown when the connection is closed, or when a statement is already streaming on it.
The server rejected the statement, at the start or while the rows were read. The error has the server's SQLSTATE and message. It is also thrown for a column type this driver cannot read yet.
The connection failed while the statement or one of its rows was being sent, or timeout passed before the loop ended. The connection cannot be used for the rest of the request.

doc.shortHtml: Reads a result one row at a time as stream does, and builds each row into an object of the class written at the call site, as queryAs does. The memory used stays the same however many rows there are.

params.name: sql
params.descHtml: The statement, bound the same way as in query. Use a ? or a :name for each value, and never write a value into the text. A tainted string does not compile here.

params.name: params
params.descHtml: The values to bind, with the same rule as query. Use list keys for ? and string keys for :name, and never both in one array.

params.name: timeout
params.descHtml: How long reading all the rows may take, with the same rule as stream. The limit applies while the rows are being read, so it covers every row and not only the first call. Without it, the loop waits as long as the server takes.

doc.returnHtml: The statement's rows for a foreach loop, each one created as a T, in the server's order. No row has been read yet when this returns. The connection is busy, as with stream. Only one T exists at a time. That is the only difference from queryAs.

errors.descHtml: The call is wrong, not the database. The placeholders and the array use different styles or different counts, a :name has no element, or an element cannot be bound. It is also thrown when the connection is closed, or when a statement is already streaming on it. A T without #[Db\Derive] also throws it here, although the compiler already reports that.

A row did not match T. A column is missing, or has a different type than the property. A SQL NULL is in a property that is not ?T, or a property's type has no column mapping. Every bad column of that row is reported at once in issues, and each path is the column's name. The loop stops there, because the rest of the result is not read.
The server rejected the statement, at the start or while the rows were read. The error has the server's SQLSTATE and message. It is also thrown for a column type this driver cannot read yet.
The connection failed while the statement or one of its rows was being sent, or timeout passed before the loop ended. The connection cannot be used for the rest of the request.

members.name: transaction
members.signature: transaction(callable(Core\Db\Transaction): T $fn, { isolation?: Core\Db\Isolation, readOnly?: bool, retries?: uint }): T

doc.shortHtml: Runs $fn inside a transaction and returns what $fn returns. If $fn returns, the transaction is committed. If $fn throws, the transaction is rolled back and the error is thrown again. An early return cannot leave the transaction open.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: The work to run. It gets a Core\Db\Transaction, which has the same query methods as the connection. The function may declare that parameter or no parameter.

params.name: isolation
params.descHtml: How much this transaction can see of other transactions running at the same time. Without it, the transaction uses the level set on the server. A nested call cannot set it. The level is for the whole transaction, not for a savepoint inside it.

params.name: readOnly
params.descHtml: Writes are not allowed during the transaction, so the server can plan for reads only. The default is false. A nested call cannot set it, for the same reason as isolation.

params.name: retries
params.descHtml: How many times $fn runs again when the commit reports a deadlock or a serialization failure. This applies to the outermost transaction only. The default is 0, because a function with side effects should run again only when you ask for it. Nothing else is retried, and there is no wait between attempts. A conflict from a statement inside $fn is thrown and not retried.

doc.returnHtml: What $fn returned, after the commit. A nested call on the same connection is a savepoint. So you can call a function that wraps its own writes in a transaction from inside another transaction.

errors.descHtml: $fn called rollBack. This call throws it even if code inside $fn caught it, because the rollback is recorded on the transaction itself.

A statement inside $fn was not allowed because of the way it was written. It is also thrown when the transaction is used after its transaction() call returned, or when a nested call sets its own isolation or readOnly.
The server rejected the BEGIN, or rejected the COMMIT after $fn returned, for example for a serialization failure or a deferred constraint. In both cases nothing is committed.
The connection failed while the transaction was open. The connection cannot be used for the rest of the request.

doc.shortHtml: Rolls back this transaction. It records $reason and throws Core\Db\RolledBack with it. You cannot request a rollback and then continue in the same transaction. So no code has to remember to check a flag such as setRollbackOnly.

params.name: reason
params.descHtml: Why the work is stopped. It becomes the reason property and the message of the thrown RolledBack, so write it for the person who reads the error.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. This method always throws.

errors.descHtml: Always. The transaction() call throws it even if code between here and there catches it, because that call checks the recorded reason, not the thrown error.
The transaction is used after its transaction() call returned, so there is nothing left to roll back.

classes.summaryHtml: Runs SQL statements inside one transaction. Either all of their changes are saved, or none of them are.

classes.name: Core\Db\Write
classes.summary: The result of a statement that changes data: how many rows it changed, and the id of an inserted row.

doc.shortHtml: Returns how many rows the statement changed.
doc.returnHtml: A uint. It is 0 for a statement that changed no rows. It is also 0 for a statement type that reports no count, such as create table. Use changed to tell the two apart.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the same count, exactly as the server reported it. It is null when this type of statement has no row count. affected cannot show that case.
doc.returnHtml: A ?uint. When it is not null, it is equal to affected. MySQL counts matched rows and changed rows separately. PostgreSQL does not send that difference, so there is no second count. A second count that always matched the first would mislead programs.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the key that this statement generated. The key belongs to this statement, so another statement on the same connection cannot change it.
doc.returnHtml: A ?uint: the key this statement generated, or null if it generated none. A statement that inserted no row returns null. PostgreSQL has no last insert id, so the key comes from a RETURNING clause. It is the first column of the last row returned, if that column is declared as an integer. On MySQL it is the AUTO_INCREMENT value the server reports for this write. On SQLite it is the rowid of a row this statement inserted, which may be 0. SQL Server always returns null, because the server does not send a generated key.

classes.summaryHtml: The result of a statement that changes data: how many rows it changed, and the id of an inserted row.

classes.name: Core\Debug
classes.summary: Shows any value in a readable form while you debug a program. It can print the value to stderr or return it as a string.

doc.shortHtml: Writes each value in a readable form, for debugging. It never writes to standard output. Outside a web request, it writes to standard error, in colour when standard error is a terminal that shows colour. Inside a web request, it writes a log record at the Debug level. In production, that record is not kept unless [log] level is "Debug". With [debug] inline, the dump is also added to an HTML response.

params.name: values
params.descHtml: Any number of values. Control bytes and bidirectional text characters are shown as visible text. A deep or long structure is shortened, and a cycle is shown as a cycle. A secret property is hidden.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A call with no arguments writes nothing. Core\Out::capture never captures a dump.

doc.shortHtml: Formats $value exactly as dump does, and returns it as a Core\Cli\Text. It writes nothing. You can put the result into your own output, and it is escaped only once.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to format. It is formatted the same way as a value given to dump.

doc.returnHtml: The plain text as a Core\Cli\Text, wherever the output goes. It has no colour and no newline at the end.

doc.shortHtml: Starts counting how many times each line runs. Read the counts with coverage. [debug] mode must include "coverage".

params.name: branches
params.descHtml: When true, each side of every if and loop condition is counted too. coverage does not return these counts. The coverage report of nvs test shows them. [debug] mode must then also include "branch".

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. Counting goes on until stopCoverage.

errors.descHtml: [debug] mode in nvs.toml does not include the name this method needs.

doc.shortHtml: Stops counting lines and branches. The counts so far are kept.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing. It does nothing when coverage is not running.

doc.shortHtml: Returns how many times each line ran. The keys are file paths. Each value is an array from a line number to its count.
doc.returnHtml: Only lines that ran are listed. Lines are counted from the first line when [debug] mode includes "coverage", and when nvs test runs with a coverage option. Otherwise the array is empty.

doc.shortHtml: Starts writing a trace of every call to the file at $path. Each line of the file is one JSON object. [debug] mode must include "trace".

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to write. The capability debug.trace must grant this path. Permission to write files is not enough.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The trace goes on until stopTrace.

errors.descHtml: [debug] mode in nvs.toml does not include the name this method needs.
The configuration does not grant debug.trace for this path.
A trace started by startTrace is already running.

doc.shortHtml: Stops the trace and closes its file.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing. It does nothing when no trace is running.

errors.descHtml: Not every call could be written to the file. The trace is stopped anyway.

doc.shortHtml: Starts timing every call, and writes the result to the file at $path in the speedscope format. [debug] mode must include "profile". Timing every call adds a small cost to each one. So code with many small calls looks slower in the profile than it is.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to write. The capability debug.profile must grant this path. Permission to write files is not enough.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The profile goes on until stopProfile.

errors.descHtml: [debug] mode in nvs.toml does not include the name this method needs.
The configuration does not grant debug.profile for this path.
A profile started by startProfile is already running.

doc.shortHtml: Stops timing calls and closes the profile's file.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing. It does nothing when no profile is running.

classes.summaryHtml:
Shows any value in a readable form while you debug a program. It can print the value to stderr or return it as a string.

Core\Debug::dump renders each argument as a typed record — int(42), string(2) "42", an array as array(n) [ … ] with its keys, an object as Class#id (n) { … } with its declared properties — and writes one per argument to the diagnostic channel: stderr in a CLI program, never stdout, and never into a Core\Out::capture. render answers the same text as a Core\Cli\Text without the trailing newline, so it can be echoed. A cycle is marked [cycle -> #1], a control byte is made visible, a secret property renders as [redacted], and the rendering is deterministic.

<?nvs
class Point
{
    public function constructor(public int $x, public int $y)
    {}
}
echo Core\Debug::render(42), "\n";
echo Core\Debug::render('42'), "\n";
echo Core\Debug::render(null), "\n";
array<int> $list = [10, 20];
echo Core\Debug::render($list), "\n";
array<string> $map = ['a' => 'x', 'b' => 'y'];
echo Core\Debug::render($map), "\n";
echo Core\Debug::render(new Point(1, 2)), "\n";
Core\Debug::dump($list);
echo "the dump went to stderr\n";
int(42)
string(2) "42"
null
array(2) [
  0 => int(10)
  1 => int(20)
]
array(2) [
  "a" => string(1) "x"
  "b" => string(1) "y"
]
Point#1 (2) {
  $x => int(1)
  $y => int(2)
}
the dump went to stderr

classes.name: Core\Decimal
classes.summary: Calculations on `decimal` numbers that the operators cannot do, such as a division with a chosen rounding, or a split into parts that add up exactly.

doc.shortHtml: Divides $value by $divisor and returns the exact result. If the result is not exact, it throws an error. Use it where you expect the division to come out even.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The dividend.

params.name: divisor
params.descHtml: What to divide it by.

doc.returnHtml: The result, with only as many digits after the point as it needs. 1.00 / 4 is 0.25.

errors.descHtml: When $divisor is zero, when the result has repeating digits, or when it does not fit in a decimal. The last two cases have the same message.

doc.shortHtml: Divides $value by $divisor and rounds the result to $scale digits with $mode. The / operator always rounds half to even. Use this method to choose the rounding.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The dividend.

params.name: divisor
params.descHtml: What to divide it by.

params.name: scale
params.descHtml: The number of digits after the decimal point, at most 28. The result always has exactly this many, so a rounded price keeps its trailing zeros.

params.name: mode
params.descHtml: How a value exactly between two results is rounded. It is the same Core\RoundMode that Core\Math::round takes. It is applied to the exact result of the division.

doc.returnHtml: The result, with exactly $scale digits after the point.

errors.descHtml: When $divisor is zero, when $scale is more than 28, or when the result does not fit in a decimal with that many digits after the point.

doc.shortHtml: Splits $amount into one part per ratio. The parts always add up to $amount exactly. If you divide and round each part yourself, a cent can be lost or added.

params.name: amount
params.descHtml: The sum to split. The parts have the same number of digits after the point, so a price with two digits splits into parts with two digits.

params.name: ratios
params.descHtml: One weight per part. Each weight is zero or more, and at least one is above zero. The keys are kept, so you can name each part.

doc.returnHtml: One part per ratio, in the same order and with the same keys. Each part is its share, rounded towards zero. The first parts then get one smallest unit more each, until nothing is left over.

errors.descHtml: When there are no ratios, when a ratio is negative, or when every ratio is zero. In each case there is no part to make.
When a part does not fit in a decimal. That happens when it needs more than 28 digits after the point, or more than a 96-bit mantissa.

doc.shortHtml: Multiplies $base by itself $exponent times and returns the exact result. The ** operator does not accept a decimal base, so use this method instead.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The value to raise.

params.name: exponent
params.descHtml: How many times to multiply it by itself. Zero gives 1. A negative exponent is not allowed. For the reciprocal, write Core\Decimal::divRound(1, Core\Decimal::pow($b, $n), $scale, $mode).

doc.returnHtml: The exact power. The digits after the point add up with each multiplication, so 2.50 squared is 6.2500.

errors.descHtml: When the power does not fit in a decimal. That happens with more than 28 digits after the point, or more than a 96-bit mantissa.

doc.shortHtml: Rounds $value to $scale places, toward negative infinity. The result is an exact decimal.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to cut.

params.name: scale
params.descHtml: The number of digits after the decimal point, at most 28. Without it, the result has none. The result always has exactly this many, so a shorter value is padded with zeros.

doc.returnHtml: The largest decimal with $scale digits that is not above $value. floor(-1.5) is -2, and floor(1.005, 2) is 1.00.

errors.descHtml: When $scale is more than 28. Also when $value has too many digits before the point to keep that many digits after it.

doc.shortHtml: Rounds $value to $scale places, toward positive infinity. The result is an exact decimal.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to cut.

params.name: scale
params.descHtml: The number of digits after the decimal point, at most 28. Without it, the result has none. The result always has exactly this many, so a shorter value is padded with zeros.

doc.returnHtml: The smallest decimal with $scale digits that is not below $value. ceil(-1.5) is -1, and ceil(1.001, 2) is 1.01.

errors.descHtml: When $scale is more than 28. Also when $value has too many digits before the point to keep that many digits after it.

doc.shortHtml: Cuts $value to $scale digits after the point, towards zero. The digits it keeps never change. This is useful for display and fixed-width columns.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to cut.

params.name: scale
params.descHtml: The number of digits after the decimal point, at most 28. Without it, the result has none. The result always has exactly this many, so a shorter value is padded with zeros.

doc.returnHtml: $value without the digits after $scale places. truncate(-1.9) is -1, and truncate(1.999, 2) is 1.99.

errors.descHtml: When $scale is more than 28. Also when $value has too many digits before the point to keep that many digits after it.

doc.shortHtml: Rounds $value to $scale digits after the point with $mode. You must always give the mode, because it decides a value exactly between two results.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to round.

params.name: mode
params.descHtml: How a value exactly between two results is rounded. It is the same Core\RoundMode that Core\Decimal::divRound and Core\Math::round take. It is required, so it comes before the optional $scale.

params.name: scale
params.descHtml: The number of digits after the decimal point, at most 28. Without it, the result has none. The result always has exactly this many, so a shorter value is padded with zeros.

doc.returnHtml: The rounded value with $scale digits. round(0.125, Core\RoundMode::HalfEven, 2) is 0.12, and round(0.125, Core\RoundMode::HalfUp, 2) is 0.13.

errors.descHtml: When $scale is more than 28. Also when $value has too many digits before the point to keep that many digits after it.

classes.summaryHtml:
Calculations on decimal numbers that the operators cannot do, such as a division with a chosen rounding, or a split into parts that add up exactly.

Novis's decimal scalar carries its own arithmetic as operators — +, -, *, % and / all work directly on it, exactly, with no class in the way. Division is the one operation that may be inexact, and the / operator's answer to that is fixed in the language: round half to even, at the widest scale the result admits. No setting changes this precision for the whole program. Such a setting would be a global variable that unrelated code reads.

Core\Decimal is where a program says something the operator cannot. These questions come up in money code, and nowhere else does the type system help with them:

  • "this division must come out even" — divExact answers the quotient when it is exact and throws ArithmeticError when it is not. A third of a bill is not a number you should get back by accident.
  • "round it here, this way" — divRound takes the number of places and the rounding mode as ordinary arguments, both required. Neither has a default, because a default for either would be that same ambient precision moved into a signature. The mode is Core\RoundMode, the same enum Core\Math::round takes.
  • "split this sum and lose none of it" — allocate splits an amount by a list of ratios into parts that add back to it exactly. Each part is its share truncated to the amount's own scale, and the units left over go one each to the earliest parts. The keys are the ratios', so a split written under the names of its parties answers under those names.
  • "raise it to a power, exactly" — pow multiplies a base by itself as many times as you ask. ** has no row for a decimal base at all, because a power that does not come out exact would have to round without being asked; a negative power is written as the division it is.
  • "cut it to this many places" — floor, ceil, truncate and round, which answer a decimal at the scale you name and not an int. round is the one with a decision to make, so it takes the mode; the other three are directions. Converting to int afterwards is a second step, written out, because a conversion that rounded on its own would be rounding you never asked for.

divRound rounds once, from the exact quotient. It is not the / operator's answer rounded a second time — rounding twice is how a quotient one digit past the place you asked for carries a tie the exact value never had.

The scale you name is the scale you get: divRound($x, $y, 5, …) answers at five places even where fewer would do, because a rendered price needs its trailing zeros. A scale past 28 is refused rather than quietly narrowed, as is a quotient whose digits will not fit at the scale you asked for.

<?nvs
decimal $bill = 100.00;
decimal $three = 3;
decimal $four = 4;

// An even split answers exactly, at the scale the quotient needs.
echo Core\Decimal::divExact($bill, $four), "\n";

// An uneven one refuses, rather than handing back 33.33... and letting the
// missing penny turn up in a reconciliation months later.
try {
    echo Core\Decimal::divExact($bill, $three);
} catch (ArithmeticError $uneven) {
    echo "not an even split\n";
}

// Where rounding is the business rule, it is written at the call site.
echo Core\Decimal::divRound($bill, $three, 2, Core\RoundMode::HalfUp), "\n";
echo Core\Decimal::divRound($bill, $three, 2, Core\RoundMode::Up), "\n";

// One eighth is 0.125 exactly, so two places is the tie the `Half*` modes are
// named for -- and the scale is the answer's, so it pads.
decimal $one = 1;
decimal $eight = 8;
echo Core\Decimal::divRound($one, $eight, 2, Core\RoundMode::HalfEven), '|',
     Core\Decimal::divRound($one, $eight, 2, Core\RoundMode::HalfUp), '|',
     Core\Decimal::divRound($one, $four, 5, Core\RoundMode::HalfEven), "\n";
25
not an even split
33.33
33.34
0.12|0.13|0.25000

A split is the one place none of that is enough: three even shares of five cents do not exist, whatever rounding you name, and the penny has to land somewhere. allocate lands it on the earliest part and answers parts that add back to the amount exactly.

<?nvs
// A five-cent bill split three ways. The parts cannot be equal, and they
// still add back to the amount.
decimal $nickel = 0.05;
foreach (Core\Decimal::allocate($nickel, [1, 1, 1]) as decimal $part) {
    echo $part, "\n";
}

// The keys are the ratios', so the parties keep their names -- and the
// leftover unit goes to the one written first.
array<decimal> $shares = ['alice' => 1, 'bob' => 2];
foreach (Core\Decimal::allocate(10.00, $shares) as string $name => decimal $share) {
    echo $name, ' ', $share, "\n";
}

// A power is repeated multiplication to the digit, scale included. The
// reciprocal is a division, so it names the rounding it needs.
decimal $rate = 1.05;
echo Core\Decimal::pow($rate, 2), '|',
     Core\Decimal::divRound(1, Core\Decimal::pow($rate, 2), 4, Core\RoundMode::HalfEven), "\n";
0.02
0.02
0.01
alice 3.34
bob 6.66
1.1025|0.9070

Cutting a value to a number of places is the same question from the other end, and the four members that do it answer a decimal rather than an int — which is what makes the scale worth naming at all. The scale you ask for is the scale you get, so a cut pads a narrower value as well as trimming a wider one, and it defaults to zero: a whole number, still a decimal.

floor, ceil and truncate are directions and take no mode. round is the one with a decision to make — which of two neighbours a value exactly between them goes to — so it names the mode, and the mode is written before the scale because the scale is the argument you may leave out.

<?nvs
// The scale you name is the scale you get, so a cut pads as well as trims.
decimal $price = 1.005;
echo Core\Decimal::floor($price, 2), '|', Core\Decimal::ceil($price, 2), "\n";

// Left out, it is zero: a whole number that is still a `decimal`, so the
// conversion to `int` is written after it rather than hidden inside it.
echo Core\Decimal::truncate($price), '|', Core\Decimal::floor($price) as int, "\n";

// Half a cent is the tie the `Half*` modes are named for, and the reason
// `round` has no default mode.
echo Core\Decimal::round($price, Core\RoundMode::HalfEven, 2), '|',
     Core\Decimal::round($price, Core\RoundMode::HalfUp, 2), "\n";

// Negative is where the three directions part: down the line, up the line,
// and towards zero. A negative `decimal` is built by subtraction.
decimal $loss = 0 - $price;
echo Core\Decimal::floor($loss), '|',
     Core\Decimal::ceil($loss), '|',
     Core\Decimal::truncate($loss), "\n";
1.00|1.01
1|1
1.00|1.01
-2|-1|-1

classes.name: Core\Encoding
classes.summary: Converts between `string` and `bytes`. It changes text to and from a character set, and writes bytes as base64, base32 or hex text.

doc.shortHtml: Converts the text $s to bytes in the encoding $charset. The conversion is exact. A character that $charset cannot represent throws an error.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to encode.

params.name: charset
params.descHtml: The encoding to write.

doc.returnHtml: The encoded bytes.

errors.descHtml: $charset cannot represent a character of $s. The message gives the character and its offset.

doc.shortHtml: Converts the bytes $b from the encoding $charset to a string. The conversion is exact. A byte sequence that is not valid in $charset throws an error.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The bytes to decode.

params.name: charset
params.descHtml: The encoding the bytes are in.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded text. Empty bytes give the empty string.

errors.descHtml: A byte sequence in $b is not valid in $charset. The message gives its offset.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $b is valid text in the encoding $charset. It makes the same test as decodeText, but returns false instead of throwing an error.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The bytes to check.

params.name: charset
params.descHtml: The encoding to check the bytes against.

doc.returnHtml: true when decodeText would succeed, false otherwise. With Charset::Latin1 the result is always true, because every one of the 256 byte values is valid.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $b as base64 text, with the alphabet of RFC 4648 § 4 and with padding.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The bytes to encode.

doc.returnHtml: The base64 text. Empty bytes give the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the base64 text $s back to bytes. It accepts only the alphabet of RFC 4648 § 4, with correct padding and no unused bits in the last symbol. Use fromBase64Url for URL-safe text.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The base64 text.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded bytes. The empty string gives empty bytes.

errors.descHtml: $s is not strict base64. It has a symbol outside the alphabet, such as - or _, missing or wrong padding, an incomplete last group, or unused bits that are not zero.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $b as URL-safe base64 text, with the alphabet of RFC 4648 § 5 and no padding. A JWT or a query string uses this form.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The bytes to encode.

doc.returnHtml: The URL-safe base64 text. Empty bytes give the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the URL-safe base64 text $s back to bytes. It reverses toBase64Url. It is as strict as fromBase64, and padding throws an error.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The URL-safe base64 text, with no padding.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded bytes. The empty string gives empty bytes.

errors.descHtml: $s is not URL-safe base64 without padding. It has a symbol outside the alphabet, such as +, / or =, an incomplete last group, or unused bits that are not zero.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $b in the base32 alphabet of RFC 4648 § 6, in upper case and with no padding. An otpauth: secret is written this way.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The bytes to encode.

doc.returnHtml: The base32 text. Empty bytes give the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the base32 text $s back to bytes. It reverses toBase32. It accepts upper and lower case, and correct padding or no padding. Neither changes the result.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The base32 text.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded bytes. The empty string gives empty bytes.

errors.descHtml: $s has a symbol outside the alphabet, such as a space between groups. Or it has an incomplete last group, unused bits that are not zero, or wrong padding.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $b as lowercase hexadecimal text, two digits per byte.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The bytes to encode.

doc.returnHtml: The hex text, twice as long as $b. Empty bytes give the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the hexadecimal text $s back to bytes. It accepts upper and lower case, two digits per byte, and nothing between the pairs. Other text throws an error.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The hexadecimal text.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded bytes, one byte for every two digits of $s. The empty string gives empty bytes.

errors.descHtml: $s has an odd number of digits, or a character that is not 0-9, a-f or A-F. A space, a colon and a 0x prefix all throw this error.

classes.summaryHtml:
Converts between string and bytes. It changes text to and from a character set, and writes bytes as base64, base32 or hex text.

Core\Encoding is where a string becomes bytes and back: encodeText and decodeText convert text through a Core\Charset case, and the base64, base64url, base32 and hex pairs spell a buffer as text and read it back. Every decoder is strict — a character outside the alphabet, padding that is missing or non-canonical, a sequence the charset cannot read — and throws rather than answering false or substituting ? or U+FFFD; isValidText is decodeText's question with a bool answer. A bytes value cannot be written directly in the code. Use fromHex or encodeText to write a buffer in source.

<?nvs
bytes $raw = Core\Encoding::encodeText('héllo', Core\Charset::Utf8);
echo Core\Bytes::length($raw), ' ', Core\Encoding::toHex($raw), "\n";
echo Core\Encoding::toBase64($raw), ' ', Core\Encoding::toBase64Url($raw), ' ', Core\Encoding::toBase32($raw), "\n";
echo Core\Encoding::decodeText(Core\Encoding::fromBase64('aMOpbGxv'), Core\Charset::Utf8), "\n";
bytes $latin = Core\Encoding::encodeText('héllo', Core\Charset::Latin1);
echo Core\Bytes::length($latin), ' ', Core\Encoding::toHex($latin), "\n";
echo Core\Encoding::isValidText($latin, Core\Charset::Utf8) ? 'utf-8' : 'not utf-8', "\n";
bytes $png = Core\Encoding::fromHex('89504e47');
echo Core\Bytes::at($png, 1), "\n";
try {
    bytes $never = Core\Encoding::fromBase64('not base64!');
    echo "decoded\n";
} catch (Throwable $e) {
    echo "refused\n";
}
6 68c3a96c6c6f
aMOpbGxv aMOpbGxv NDB2S3DMN4
héllo
5 68e96c6c6f
not utf-8
80
refused

classes.name: Core\Env
classes.summary: Reads the environment the program runs in: its environment variables, whether it runs in production or development, and facts about the system.

doc.shortHtml: The mode a program runs in. There are two modes. A mode sets the defaults of five settings, and you can still change each of those settings on its own.
The kind of run the code is in. Core\Env::context() returns one of these seven cases.
The operating system family the program runs on. Core\Env::OS is one of these six cases.

constants.name: EOL
constants.descHtml: The line ending this platform writes: \r\n on Windows and \n everywhere else. Use it to write text in the platform's own format. Core\Str::lines and Core\IO::lines do not use it, and split on all three line endings.

constants.name: OS
constants.descHtml: The operating system family, as a Core\Env::Platform case. Compare it with a case, such as Core\Env::OS == Core\Env::Platform::Windows.

constants.name: VERSION
constants.descHtml: This runtime's version: three numbers separated by dots, the same string nvs info prints. To compare versions, split it with Core\Str::split and compare the numbers.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value of the environment variable $name. The environment is read-only, so a program cannot change a variable.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The variable's name, with the same case as in the environment. It may not be tainted. A request that could choose the name could read every variable, one at a time.

doc.returnHtml: The value as a tainted string, or null if the variable is not set. The value is tainted because it comes from outside the program. Clean it before you use it in SQL, HTML or a shell command.

errors.descHtml: The variable contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8, so its value is not a string. The method does not return null here, because null means the variable is not set. It does not repair the bytes either.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value of the environment variable $name as a secret string. Use it for a password or an API key. The value can go into an outbound HTTP header, a form field or a database password. echo, a log and a response body do not accept it.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The variable's name. It may not be tainted, so a request cannot choose which secret the program reads.

doc.returnHtml: The value as a secret string, or null if the variable is not set.

errors.descHtml: The variable contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8, so its value is not a string. The message names the variable and not its value.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every environment variable, with the variable names as keys.
doc.returnHtml: An array<string, tainted string>, sorted by name. Every call returns the same order, on every platform. A variable whose name or value is not valid UTF-8 is left out. get with that name throws an error for it.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the mode the program runs in: production or development. You set the mode in nvs.toml, and Core\Config reads it like every other setting. No environment variable changes it, so a request cannot choose the mode.
doc.returnHtml: The mode as a Core\Env::Mode case. If the configuration does not set a mode, the result is Production, the stricter mode.

doc.shortHtml: Which kind of run the code is in: an HTTP request, a command-line program, a spawned script, a scheduled script, a queued job, a test or a connection. Use it to choose what a program does in each one.
doc.returnHtml: The kind of run as a Core\Env::Context case. It is the same value for the whole run and for every task the run starts.

classes.summaryHtml: Reads the environment the program runs in: its environment variables, whether it runs in production or development, and facts about the system.

classes.name: Core\Fatal
classes.summary: Runs your code after a request is stopped because it went over a limit, such as its memory or time limit. Use it to log what happened.

doc.shortHtml: Registers a function that runs when a resource limit stops this request. The limits are memory, CPU time, output, wall time, script depth and call-stack depth. The function runs once, with a small amount of memory and time kept aside for it. It is the only code that sees a FATAL error, because a catch never gets one.

params.name: handler
params.descHtml: The function to run. It gets one array. Its limit key is the name of the limit that stopped the request, as the setting writes it, such as memory or cpu_time. The function returns nothing, and it may have no parameter. If it throws, or goes over the memory and time kept aside for it, it stops at once.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The function belongs to this request only, and a second call replaces the first. It is deleted when the request ends, and no other request can see it.

doc.shortHtml: Registers a function that runs when an exception is not caught anywhere in this request. The function runs once, with the memory and time the request has left. It gets the exception itself.

params.name: handler
params.descHtml: The function to run. It gets the uncaught Throwable: the object the program threw, with its class, message and backtrace. The function returns nothing, and it may have no parameter. If it throws, or uses up what the request has left, it stops at once. The error that is reported is still the original uncaught one.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The function belongs to this request only, and a second call replaces the first. It is deleted when the request ends, and no other request can see it. Novis still writes its own record of the error. The exit status does not change.

classes.summaryHtml:
Runs your code after a request is stopped because it went over a limit, such as its memory or time limit. Use it to log what happened.

Core\Fatal::onLimit registers the callable the request runs when a resource limit — memory, CPU time, output, wall time, script depth or call-stack depth — stops it. A limit breach is a FATAL, which no catch sees; the handler is the only code that observes one. It runs once, out of a slice of the request's budget reserved for it, and never a second time: a handler that throws or exhausts that slice is abandoned where it stands. Registering is request-local, a later call replaces the earlier handler, and registering runs nothing. The handler receives one array whose limit key names the directive that fired, spelled as nvs.toml spells it (memory, cpu_time); it may declare no parameter at all.

<?nvs
Core\Fatal::onLimit(fn(array<string> $report): void => {
    echo 'stopped by the ', $report['limit'], " limit\n";
});
echo "handler registered\n";

Core\Fatal::onLimit(fn(): void => {
    echo "a replacement that takes no report\n";
});
echo "handler replaced\n";

var $work = Core\Arr::range(1, 1000);
echo 'work done: ', Core\Arr::count($work), " items, no limit reached\n";
handler registered
handler replaced
work done: 1000 items, no limit reached

classes.name: Core\Hash
classes.summary: Computes hashes and HMAC signatures of text or bytes, and compares two of them safely. You choose the algorithm as an argument.

doc.shortHtml: The algorithm a Core\Hash method computes. It includes checksums and the two broken digests that other systems still use, and BLAKE3. StrongDigest is the ten SHA-2 and SHA-3 cases, which Core\Hash::hmac accepts.
Computes the digest of $data with the algorithm $digest. The result is raw bytes. It is not hexadecimal text and not an int.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The data to hash. A string is read as its UTF-8 bytes.

params.name: digest
params.descHtml: The algorithm. Every Core\Hash::Digest case is allowed, also the broken ones.

doc.returnHtml: The digest as bytes, with the length of the chosen algorithm. Every algorithm accepts any input, also an empty one.

doc.shortHtml: Computes the HMAC of RFC 2104 for $data, with $key and the algorithm $digest. The result is raw bytes. Only a StrongDigest is allowed, so Digest::Md5 or Digest::Sha1 does not compile.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The data to sign. A string is read as its UTF-8 bytes.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The secret key, of any length. A long key is hashed first, and a short key is padded with zero bytes, as RFC 2104 § 2 says.

params.name: digest
params.descHtml: The algorithm, one of the ten SHA-2 and SHA-3 Core\Hash::Digest cases.

doc.returnHtml: The MAC as bytes, with the length of the chosen algorithm.

doc.shortHtml: Compares two digests in constant time. For two values of the same length, the time does not depend on where they first differ.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: One digest.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The other digest.

doc.returnHtml: true when the two have the same bytes, and false otherwise. Two values of different lengths return false at once. The length of a digest is not a secret.

doc.shortHtml: Starts a digest with the algorithm $digest that you feed in parts. It returns a Core\Hash\Stream. Call update to add data and finish to get the digest.

params.name: digest
params.descHtml: The algorithm, any Core\Hash::Digest case.

doc.returnHtml: A new, open stream with no data in it yet.

classes.summaryHtml:
Computes hashes and HMAC signatures of text or bytes, and compares two of them safely. You choose the algorithm as an argument.

Core\Hash::of computes any Core\Hash::Digest case over a string or bytes and answers the raw digest as bytes — never hex and never an int — so printing one goes through Core\Encoding::toHex. hmac takes only the strong cases: Core\Hash::Digest::Md5, Sha1, Crc32, Crc32c and Blake3 are compile errors there, while of accepts every case for checksum interop. Compare two digests with equals, which runs in constant time. Input that arrives in pieces goes through stream, which opens a Core\Hash\Stream.

<?nvs
bytes $digest = Core\Hash::of('abc', Core\Hash::Digest::Sha256);
echo Core\Encoding::toHex($digest), "\n";
echo Core\Encoding::toHex(Core\Hash::of('abc', Core\Hash::Digest::Md5)), "\n";
echo Core\Encoding::toHex(Core\Hash::of('abc', Core\Hash::Digest::Crc32)), "\n";

bytes $key = 'Jefe' as bytes;
bytes $mac = Core\Hash::hmac('what do ya want for nothing?', $key, Core\Hash::Digest::Sha256);
echo Core\Encoding::toHex($mac), "\n";

bytes $again = Core\Hash::of('abc', Core\Hash::Digest::Sha256);
echo Core\Hash::equals($digest, $again) ? 'same' : 'differ', "\n";
echo Core\Hash::equals($digest, Core\Hash::of('abd', Core\Hash::Digest::Sha256)) ? 'same' : 'differ', "\n";
ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad
900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72
352441c2
5bdcc146bf60754e6a042426089575c75a003f089d2739839dec58b964ec3843
same
differ

classes.name: Core\Hash\Stream
classes.summary: Computes a hash from data that arrives in pieces. You add each piece in order, and then read the hash once at the end.

doc.shortHtml: Adds $data to the stream. finish computes the digest of all parts in the order they were added.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The next part of the data. A string is read as its UTF-8 bytes.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The stream keeps a reference to $data until finish.

errors.descHtml: The stream is already finished. A digest cannot change, so open a new stream.

doc.shortHtml: Closes the stream and returns the digest of everything added with update. The result is the same as Core\Hash::of on all the parts joined together.
doc.returnHtml: The digest as bytes. After this call the stream is finished, and its data is freed.

errors.descHtml: The stream is already finished. A second call to finish throws this error.

classes.summaryHtml:
Computes a hash from data that arrives in pieces. You add each piece in order, and then read the hash once at the end.

A Core\Hash\Stream is opened by Core\Hash::stream with a Core\Hash::Digest case and digests everything update feeds it, in order, so finish answers exactly what Core\Hash::of answers over the concatenation. finish consumes the stream: a second finish, or an update after one, throws RuntimeError. Two digests of one input need two streams.

<?nvs
var $stream = Core\Hash::stream(Core\Hash::Digest::Sha256);
$stream->update('a');
$stream->update('bc');
bytes $streamed = $stream->finish();
echo Core\Encoding::toHex($streamed), "\n";

bytes $whole = Core\Hash::of('abc', Core\Hash::Digest::Sha256);
echo Core\Hash::equals($streamed, $whole) ? 'same' : 'differ', "\n";

try {
    $stream->update('more');
} catch (RuntimeError $e) {
    echo "finished\n";
}
ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad
same
finished

classes.name: Core\Heap
classes.summary: A priority queue. It always returns its smallest value first, and a comparison function you give can choose a different order.

doc.shortHtml: Adds $value to the heap in O(log n). The heap keeps duplicates, because it is a priority queue and not a set.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The element to add.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. If the comparator throws an error, push throws the same error.

errors.descHtml: The heap cannot compare $value with another element. There is no comparator or compareTo, and the two values have no natural order. Two numbers, two strings, two bools or two nulls have one. It also throws when the comparator returns NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the element that pop would return, which is the smallest in the heap's order. The element stays in the heap.
doc.returnHtml: The first element. The heap does not change.

errors.descHtml: The heap is empty. Call isEmpty first to check.

doc.shortHtml: Removes the smallest element in the heap's order and returns it, in O(log n).
doc.returnHtml: The element that was first. The next element becomes first. If the comparator throws an error, pop throws the same error.

errors.descHtml: The heap is empty. It also throws when sorting the other elements meets two values with no natural order, or a comparator that returns NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Counts the elements in the heap, duplicates included.
doc.returnHtml: The number of elements. An empty heap gives 0.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether the heap is empty. Call it before peek or pop, because they throw an error on an empty heap.
doc.returnHtml: true for an empty heap, false otherwise.

classes.summaryHtml:
A priority queue. It always returns its smallest value first, and a comparison function you give can choose a different order.

Core\Heap<T> keeps its elements ordered so that peek and pop always answer the smallest one. The order is decided once, at new: a comparator passed as the constructor's argument — new Core\Heap<T>(fn (T $a, T $b): int => …), answering negative, zero or positive as Core\Arr::sort's does — wins; without one, an object orders by its own Comparable::compareTo, and a scalar by its natural order. A max-heap is therefore the min-heap with its comparator reversed, not another class. peek and pop throw on an empty heap — ask isEmpty first — and a foreach over a heap yields its elements in pop order without removing any of them.

<?nvs
class Job implements Comparable
{
    public function constructor(public string $name, public int $cost)
    {}

    public function compareTo(Job $other): int
    {
        return $this->cost - $other->cost;
    }
}

var $jobs = new Core\Heap<Job>();
$jobs->push(new Job('deploy', 5));
$jobs->push(new Job('lint', 1));
$jobs->push(new Job('build', 3));

var $first = $jobs->peek();
echo 'next=', $first->name, ' of ', $jobs->count(), "\n";
while (!$jobs->isEmpty()) {
    var $job = $jobs->pop();
    echo $job->name, "\n";
}

var $largest = new Core\Heap<int>(fn(int $a, int $b): int => $b - $a);
$largest->push(3);
$largest->push(9);
$largest->push(5);
foreach ($largest as int $n) {
    echo $n, ' ';
}
echo 'still ', $largest->count(), "\n";
next=lint of 3
lint
build
deploy
9 5 3 still 3

classes.name: Core\Html
classes.summary: Makes HTML safe to put into a page. It escapes text, cleans untrusted HTML, and parses HTML documents.

doc.shortHtml: Escapes &, <, >, " and ' in $text as character references. It also replaces every unterminated bidirectional control character with �. You can write the result into a page, where a tainted string is not allowed.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The text to write into an HTML document. It is shown as text, not read as HTML.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Html\Markup with the escaped text. It is safe in element content and in an attribute value with either kind of quotes. It is not a string, so the page does not escape it a second time. toSource returns its text as a string. Text without the five characters and without an unterminated control character does not change. The five characters are always escaped, and no option turns this off. Input that already looks like a reference is escaped again, because & in the input is the text &.

doc.shortHtml: Joins a list of Core\Html\Markup fragments in order, with $separator between each two. It does the same as Markup + Markup for a whole list.

params.name: parts
params.descHtml: The fragments to join, in list order.

params.name: separator
params.descHtml: The markup written between each two parts. It is not written before the first part or after the last. With empty markup, nothing is written between parts.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Html\Markup with every part in order. An empty list gives empty markup. Nothing is escaped, because each part and the separator are already safe markup. Escaping them again would break that markup.

members.name: later
members.signature: later(callable(): mixed $fn, { placeholder?: Core\Html\Markup, error?: Core\Html\Markup, deadline?: Core\Time\Duration }): Core\Html\Markup

doc.shortHtml: Runs $fn as a separate task and returns a placeholder. Write the placeholder where the output belongs. When the page is finished, the output of $fn replaces the placeholder. Several later calls run at the same time.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: The function to run. It takes no arguments. Its output is what it echoes, followed by the Core\Html\Markup it returns, if any.

params.name: placeholder
params.descHtml: The markup the page shows until the output is ready. The default is empty.

params.name: error
params.descHtml: The markup shown instead of the output when $fn throws an error or runs past its deadline. The default is empty.

params.name: deadline
params.descHtml: The longest time $fn may run. Without it, only the request's own limits apply.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Html\Markup placeholder. Outside an HTML response, $fn runs at once and the result is its output.

errors.descHtml: When the page writes the same placeholder twice. A placeholder that the page never writes is not an error: its $fn does not run, and a warning is logged.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the source text of a Core\Html\Markup. There is no Markup as string cast, so this is the only way to get the text. Each call needs a written reason, so it is easy to find in code.

params.name: markup
params.descHtml: The markup whose text you need.

params.name: reason
params.descHtml: Why this code needs the text and not the markup, written for the next person who reads it. Nothing else reads it. An empty reason is not allowed.

doc.returnHtml: The source text of the markup, as a plain string. Typical uses are caching a rendered fragment, storing it in a database column, or writing it to a file. Another use is passing it to an output that is not HTML.

errors.descHtml: $reason is empty. Each call must say why it needs the text.

doc.shortHtml: Parses $document as HTML with the WHATWG algorithm, which browsers use. It returns the document node of the same kind of tree that Core\Xml::parse builds.

params.name: document
params.descHtml: The document text. Any text is a valid document, so this method never throws an error.

doc.returnHtml: The Core\Xml\Node of kind Document. Its children are the top level of the parsed page. For any input that is not empty, this is one html element with head and body in it. That is true even when the text does not contain these tags. Missing tags, wrongly nested tags and stray content go exactly where a browser puts them. So the tree is the page a browser would show. A <!DOCTYPE …> gives no node, because the tree has no kind for it. Names are lower case in HTML. In SVG and MathML they get the correct case, as the algorithm says. Elements nested deeper than 1000 levels are placed at level 1000, so walking the tree can never run out of stack.

doc.shortHtml: Parses $document as HTML and builds a new document from only the allowed elements and attributes. Use it for untrusted HTML. For untrusted text, use escape.

params.name: document
params.descHtml: The HTML to rebuild. Any text is a valid document, so this method never throws an error.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Html\Markup with the rebuilt document. You can write it into a page without escaping it again. The method builds a new document and does not edit the old one. An element that is not allowed loses its tag, but its content is kept. An attribute that is not allowed is not written. A script, style or other raw-text element is removed with its content. The list of allowed elements is fixed, and no argument can extend it. A list you write yourself could have security holes. The text and the order of the kept content stay as in the document.

classes.summaryHtml:
Makes HTML safe to put into a page. It escapes text, cleans untrusted HTML, and parses HTML documents.

Core\Html\Markup is the one type an HTTP request writes raw; every string written into a page is escaped. A Markup is made in three ways: an `html… template, whose text is trusted because it was written in the source and whose {$…} holes are escaped; Core\Html::escape, which escapes a string; and Core\Html::sanitize, which rebuilds an untrusted document with only its safe parts. + joins two Markup values and Core\Html::join joins a list; . on a Markup is a compile error. Core\Html::toSource is the only way back to a string, and it takes a written reason. Core\Html::parse reads any document onto a Core\Xml\Node` tree and never fails.

<?nvs
tainted string $name = '<script>alert(1)</script>';
string $bio = '<p>likes <b>tea</b></p><img src=x onerror=alert(1)>';
Core\Html\Markup $badge = html`<span class="badge">new</span>`;
Core\Html\Markup $line = html`<p>{$name} {$badge}</p>`;
Core\Html\Markup $safe = Core\Html::sanitize($bio);
echo $line + $safe, "\n";
echo Core\Html::join([$badge, $badge], html`, `), "\n";
echo Core\Html::toSource($badge, 'logging the fragment'), "\n";
<p><script>alert(1)</script> <span class="badge">new</span></p><p>likes <b>tea</b></p><img src="x">
<span class="badge">new</span>, <span class="badge">new</span>
<span class="badge">new</span>

members.signature: get(string|Core\Http\Target $url, { deadline?: Core\Time\Duration, connectTimeout?: Core\Time\Duration, headers?: array<secret string>, followRedirects?: uint, retryAttempts?: uint, retryBackoff?: Core\Time\Duration, retryIdempotencyKey?: string, json?: mixed, form?: array<secret tainted string>, body?: secret tainted string|secret tainted bytes|Core\Http\Part, contentType?: string, multipart?: array<secret tainted string|Core\Http\Part>, identity?: Core\Http\Identity, tlsCa?: string, tlsPin?: string|array<string>, tlsVerifyHost?: bool, tlsVerify?: bool, tlsMinVersion?: string, connectTo?: string, redirectToHttp?: bool }): Core\Http\Response

doc.shortHtml: Sends a GET request to $url, with a time limit. It connects only to an address that the outbound policy approved.

params.name: url
params.descHtml: Where the request goes. It is a URL that the program wrote, or a Core\Http\Target from Core\Http::allowUrl. A tainted URL is not allowed here. Check it with Core\Http::allowUrl first.

params.name: deadline
params.descHtml: The time limit for the whole call. It covers the connection, every redirect, every retry and every wait between retries. If it is not given, the runtime's [http.client] deadline is used. There is no way to write a call with no deadline.

params.name: connectTimeout
params.descHtml: How long the connection alone may take. This time is part of deadline, and is not added to it.

params.name: headers
params.descHtml: Extra request headers, by name. A secret value is allowed here, because a credential must reach the API it is for. A tainted value is not allowed. The runtime adds its own headers as well.

params.name: followRedirects
params.descHtml: How many redirects to follow. If it is not given, the runtime's [http.client] max_redirects is used, and its default is 0. Each redirect is checked against the outbound policy again, and its address is approved again.

params.name: retryAttempts
params.descHtml: The total number of attempts, including the first. 1 is the same as the default, and 0 throws an error. Retries wait a random delay (jitter), and all attempts share one deadline.

params.name: retryBackoff
params.descHtml: The base delay between retries. The delay grows exponentially, and each wait is a random time up to that delay (full jitter). If it is not given, it is 100ms. You cannot configure the jitter.

params.name: retryIdempotencyKey
params.descHtml: Sent as the Idempotency-Key header, with the same value on every attempt. It is required for post and patch when retryAttempts is given. Every other method also accepts it.

params.name: json
params.descHtml: The value to send as application/json. It is encoded once for the whole call. A secret inside it is sent, as it is in a header. A null value sends the JSON document null, not an empty body.

params.name: form
params.descHtml: The fields to send as application/x-www-form-urlencoded, by name.

params.name: body
params.descHtml: The bytes to send exactly as given, with the media type in contentType. Only one of json, form, body and multipart may be given. None of them is allowed on get or head. Both mistakes are compile errors.

params.name: contentType
params.descHtml: The media type of body. It has no effect without body, so giving it alone is a compile error.

params.name: multipart
params.descHtml: The parts to send as multipart/form-data, by name.

params.name: identity
params.descHtml: The client certificate to send when the server asks for one. Create it with Core\Http\Identity::read. Nothing is sent to a server that does not ask. Two different identities never share a pooled connection. A call without an identity does not share one with a call that has one.

params.name: tlsCa
params.descHtml: The PEM certificates to trust for this call. They replace the runtime's own root certificates. The URL's host must be in the anchors grant of capabilities.tls. If it is not, the call throws an error before it connects.

params.name: tlsPin
params.descHtml: One sha256//<base64> public-key pin, or several. The server is accepted if the hash of its SubjectPublicKeyInfo matches one of them. No certificate chain is checked. Use this to reach a server with a self-signed certificate. The host must be in the pin grant.

params.name: tlsVerifyHost
params.descHtml: If it is false, the chain is still checked, and only the name check is skipped. The host must be in the any_name grant.

params.name: tlsVerify
params.descHtml: If it is false, neither the chain nor the name is checked. The handshake signature is still checked, so the server has the key it sent. But nothing shows whose key it is. The host must be in the insecure grant.

params.name: tlsMinVersion
params.descHtml: The lowest TLS version this call allows, "1.2" or "1.3". It needs no grant, because it can only make the call stricter. A value below the runtime's [http.client.tls] min_version throws an error.

params.name: connectTo
params.descHtml: The IP address to connect to. The URL's host is not looked up, but the certificate is still checked against that host. The host must be in the net.connect_to grant. The deployment's address policy checks this address like a looked-up one. With a Core\Http\Target as the URL, this option throws an error, because the target already has its approved addresses.

params.name: redirectToHttp
params.descHtml: If it is true, a redirect from https to plain http may be followed. The redirect's host must also be in the net.downgrade grant. If it is not given, such a redirect throws an error. Otherwise one Location header would be enough for a server to remove a call's TLS. This option does not affect a plain http URL that you request directly.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Http\Response with the status and the body of the reply. A 404 or a 500 is a normal reply and is returned here. Only a request that gets no reply at all throws an error. An https URL is fetched over TLS. The certificate is checked against the certificate authorities that Novis includes.

errors.descHtml: The URL is not allowed. It is not a URL, its scheme is not http or https, or it has no host. Or net.connect does not grant the host. Or the host resolves to a loopback, private, link-local or unspecified address that net.internal does not list. An option is out of range. A deadline, connectTimeout or retryBackoff is not a positive duration. On stream, the same is true for idle and maxDuration. Or retryAttempts is zero. A header name or value contains a control byte, which would end the line early. An https server sent a certificate that does not verify against the certificate authorities Novis includes. Or the certificate is not valid for that name. Or the reply is not HTTP, or it is larger than the limit for one request. A body that is not text does not cause this error. Core\Http\Response::text throws for it. request gets the method as a value, so it checks two things before the first attempt. The other methods check them at compile time. The first is a body option on a Get or a Head. The second is retries on a Post or a Patch without retryIdempotencyKey.

The deadline passed before a reply arrived. It covers the connection, every redirect, every retry and every wait between retries. If a wait would end after the deadline, the error is thrown at once, without waiting.
The last attempt could not reach the pinned address, or the connection failed while the request was being sent or the reply read.

params.descHtml: The PEM certificates to trust for this call. They replace the runtime's own root certificates. The URL's host must be in the anchors grant of capabilities.tls. If it is not, the call throws an error before it connects.

params.name: tlsPin
params.descHtml: One sha256//<base64> public-key pin, or several. The server is accepted if the hash of its SubjectPublicKeyInfo matches one of them. No certificate chain is checked. Use this to reach a server with a self-signed certificate. The host must be in the pin grant.

params.name: tlsVerifyHost
params.descHtml: If it is false, the chain is still checked, and only the name check is skipped. The host must be in the any_name grant.

params.name: tlsVerify
params.descHtml: If it is false, neither the chain nor the name is checked. The handshake signature is still checked, so the server has the key it sent. But nothing shows whose key it is. The host must be in the insecure grant.

params.name: tlsMinVersion
params.descHtml: The lowest TLS version this call allows, "1.2" or "1.3". It needs no grant, because it can only make the call stricter. A value below the runtime's [http.client.tls] min_version throws an error.

params.name: connectTo
params.descHtml: The IP address to connect to. The URL's host is not looked up, but the certificate is still checked against that host. The host must be in the net.connect_to grant. The deployment's address policy checks this address like a looked-up one. With a Core\Http\Target as the URL, this option throws an error, because the target already has its approved addresses.

params.name: redirectToHttp
params.descHtml: If it is true, a redirect from https to plain http may be followed. The redirect's host must also be in the net.downgrade grant. If it is not given, such a redirect throws an error. Otherwise one Location header would be enough for a server to remove a call's TLS. This option does not affect a plain http URL that you request directly.

params.name: idle
params.descHtml: The longest time the body may be silent after the status and headers arrive. If it is not given, the runtime's [http.client] idle is used. There is no way to turn this limit off.

params.name: maxDuration
params.descHtml: The longest time the whole body may take. This limit stops a server that sends one byte at a time, just often enough to pass the idle check. If it is not given, the runtime's [http.client] max_duration is used. deadline covers only the connection, the status and the headers.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Http\Stream. Its status(), header() and headers() methods return the status and headers. Read the body with exactly one of events(), lines(), chunks() and saveTo().

errors.descHtml: The URL is not allowed. It is not a URL, its scheme is not http or https, or it has no host. Or net.connect does not grant the host. Or the host resolves to a loopback, private, link-local or unspecified address that net.internal does not list. An option is out of range. A deadline, connectTimeout or retryBackoff is not a positive duration. On stream, the same is true for idle and maxDuration. Or retryAttempts is zero. A header name or value contains a control byte, which would end the line early. An https server sent a certificate that does not verify against the certificate authorities Novis includes. Or the certificate is not valid for that name. Or the reply is not HTTP, or it is larger than the limit for one request. A body that is not text does not cause this error. Core\Http\Response::text throws for it. request gets the method as a value, so it checks two things before the first attempt. The other methods check them at compile time. The first is a body option on a Get or a Head. The second is retries on a Post or a Patch without retryIdempotencyKey.

The deadline passed before a reply arrived. It covers the connection, every redirect, every retry and every wait between retries. If a wait would end after the deadline, the error is thrown at once, without waiting.
The last attempt could not reach the pinned address, or the connection failed while the request was being sent or the reply read.

members.name: openSocket
members.signature: openSocket(string|Core\Http\Target $url, { deadline?: Core\Time\Duration, connectTimeout?: Core\Time\Duration, headers?: array<secret string>, identity?: Core\Http\Identity, tlsCa?: string, tlsPin?: string|array<string>, tlsVerifyHost?: bool, tlsVerify?: bool, tlsMinVersion?: string, connectTo?: string, protocols?: array<string>, idle?: Core\Time\Duration, maxDuration?: Core\Time\Duration, maxMessage?: uint, sendTimeout?: Core\Time\Duration, ping?: Core\Time\Duration }): Core\Http\Socket

doc.shortHtml: Opens a WebSocket to $url, and returns it when the server's 101 reply arrives. Use it for a realtime API that the program keeps talking to.

params.name: url
params.descHtml: The server to open the socket to. It is a ws or wss URL that the program wrote, or a Core\Http\Target from Core\Http::allowUrl. An http or https URL is not allowed here. A tainted URL must be checked with Core\Http::allowUrl first.

params.name: deadline
params.descHtml: The time limit for the opening handshake. It covers the connection and every address tried, and it ends when the 101 reply arrives. After that, idle and maxDuration limit the conversation. If it is not given, the runtime's [http.client] deadline is used. There is no way to write a socket with no deadline.

params.name: connectTimeout
params.descHtml: How long the connection alone may take. This time is part of deadline, and is not added to it.

params.name: headers
params.descHtml: Extra request headers, by name. A secret value is allowed here, because a credential must reach the API it is for. A tainted value is not allowed. The runtime adds its own headers as well.

params.name: identity
params.descHtml: The client certificate to send when the server asks for one. Create it with Core\Http\Identity::read. Nothing is sent to a server that does not ask. Two different identities never share a pooled connection. A call without an identity does not share one with a call that has one.

params.name: tlsCa
params.descHtml: The PEM certificates to trust for this call. They replace the runtime's own root certificates. The URL's host must be in the anchors grant of capabilities.tls. If it is not, the call throws an error before it connects.

params.name: tlsPin
params.descHtml: One sha256//<base64> public-key pin, or several. The server is accepted if the hash of its SubjectPublicKeyInfo matches one of them. No certificate chain is checked. Use this to reach a server with a self-signed certificate. The host must be in the pin grant.

params.name: tlsVerifyHost
params.descHtml: If it is false, the chain is still checked, and only the name check is skipped. The host must be in the any_name grant.

params.name: tlsVerify
params.descHtml: If it is false, neither the chain nor the name is checked. The handshake signature is still checked, so the server has the key it sent. But nothing shows whose key it is. The host must be in the insecure grant.

params.name: tlsMinVersion
params.descHtml: The lowest TLS version this call allows, "1.2" or "1.3". It needs no grant, because it can only make the call stricter. A value below the runtime's [http.client.tls] min_version throws an error.

params.name: connectTo
params.descHtml: The IP address to connect to. The URL's host is not looked up, but the certificate is still checked against that host. The host must be in the net.connect_to grant. The deployment's address policy checks this address like a looked-up one. With a Core\Http\Target as the URL, this option throws an error, because the target already has its approved addresses.

params.name: protocols
params.descHtml: The subprotocols to offer in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol, most preferred first. Each name is one word of letters, digits and the punctuation an HTTP token allows, such as ., - and _. A space, a comma or a control character throws an error. Core\Http\Socket::protocol returns the one the server chooses. If the server chooses a name that was not offered, the call throws an error.

params.name: idle
params.descHtml: The longest time the socket may be silent in either direction. If it is not given, the runtime's [http.client] idle is used. There is no way to turn this limit off. With ping set, a live but quiet server answers the pings, so only a dead server reaches this limit.

params.name: maxDuration
params.descHtml: The longest time the socket may stay open in total. This limit stops a server that sends one frame at a time, just often enough to pass the idle check. If it is not given, the runtime's [http.client] max_duration is used.

params.name: maxMessage
params.descHtml: The largest message, in bytes, that this side builds from the server's fragments. A larger message closes the socket with code 1009. The waiting receive then throws an error that names the limit. If it is not given, the runtime's [http.client.socket] max_message is used.

params.name: sendTimeout
params.descHtml: The longest time a frame may wait to be sent to a server that is not reading. It is also how long close waits for the server's own close frame. If it is not given, the runtime's [http.client.socket] send_timeout is used.

params.name: ping
params.descHtml: How long the socket stays silent before it sends a ping. A live server answers the ping, so idle closes only a dead connection. If it is not given, no ping is sent, because a ping is traffic the server did not ask for. A ping from the server is always answered, because the WebSocket protocol requires it.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Http\Socket for the conversation. receive() returns the server's next message as a Core\Socket\Message, the same class a server-side connection uses. send() and sendBytes() send the two kinds of message, and close() ends the conversation. The socket belongs to the task that opened it. It is closed with code 1001 when that task ends, so it never lives longer than its request, command or job.

errors.descHtml: The URL is not allowed. It is not a URL, its scheme is not ws or wss, or it has no host. This method does not accept http or https, and the other methods do not accept ws or wss. Or net.connect does not grant the host, or the host resolves to an address the deployment's policy denies. An option is out of range. A deadline, connectTimeout, idle, maxDuration, sendTimeout or ping is not a positive duration. Or a protocols entry is not one word. Or the server did not open a socket. It sent a redirect, which is never followed, and the message names its Location. Or it sent a status other than 101. Or it chose a subprotocol that protocols did not offer.

classes.summaryHtml: Sends HTTP requests to other servers, with one method for each HTTP verb. Each call returns the reply as a Core\Http\Response.

classes.name: Core\Http\Event
classes.summary: One server-sent event: its data, its name and its id. A `foreach` over `Core\Http\Stream::events()` gives one for each event the server finished sending.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the data of this event. Every data line of the event is joined with a newline, and the last newline is removed.
doc.returnHtml: The data, tainted like every byte of a reply. An event with no data line is not given to the loop at all.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the type of this event. The server sends it as an event line.
doc.returnHtml: The name, tainted. It is null when the event has no event line. The format calls such an event a message.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the last event id the server set. A program that resumes a stream sends it back in the Last-Event-ID header.
doc.returnHtml: The id, tainted, or null when no id was set. The format ignores an id that contains a NUL byte, so the result is null.

classes.summaryHtml: One server-sent event: its data, its name and its id. A foreach over Core\Http\Stream::events() gives one for each event the server finished sending.

classes.name: Core\Http\Events
classes.summary: The server-sent events of a streamed reply's body, in the order they arrived. A `foreach` over `Core\Http\Stream::events()` gives each one as a `Core\Http\Event`.
classes.summaryHtml: The server-sent events of a streamed reply's body, in the order they arrived. A foreach over Core\Http\Stream::events() gives each one as a Core\Http\Event.

classes.name: Core\Http\Identity
classes.summary: A client certificate and its key. A request sends it when the server asks the client to prove who it is.

doc.shortHtml: Reads a client certificate chain and its private key. A request sends them when a server asks the client for a certificate. The leaf certificate is checked against the key here. If they do not match, this throws an error before any connection is opened.

params.name: chainPem
params.descHtml: The chain as PEM. The leaf certificate comes first, then the intermediate certificates the server needs to check it. Other HTTP clients use the same order.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The private key of the leaf certificate. The TLS handshake is signed with this key. A key that can only do key agreement, such as X25519, throws an error.

doc.returnHtml: The identity. Pass it as a request's identity option. It is sent only when the server asks for it. Two different identities never share a pooled connection.

errors.descHtml: $chainPem is not a PEM certificate chain, or it contains no certificate. Or $key cannot sign a TLS handshake. Or the leaf certificate has a different public key from $key. A client identity is part of the program's own deployment, so this error always means a mistake in the deployed files.

classes.summaryHtml: A client certificate and its key. A request sends it when the server asks the client to prove who it is.

classes.name: Core\Http\Lines
classes.summary: The lines of a streamed reply's body, in the order they arrived. A `foreach` over `Core\Http\Stream::lines()` gives each line as a `tainted string`.
classes.summaryHtml: The lines of a streamed reply's body, in the order they arrived. A foreach over Core\Http\Stream::lines() gives each line as a tainted string.

classes.name: Core\Http\Part
classes.summary: Describes a request body, or one field of a multipart body. A file part is read from disk while it is sent, so the whole file is never in memory.

members.name: file
members.signature: file(string $path, { filename?: string, contentType?: string }): Core\Http\Part

doc.shortHtml: Creates a body, or one field of a multipart body, from the file at $path. The file is read while the request is sent, so it is not loaded into memory first. It needs the fs.read capability. The capability is checked at this call, so a path without access throws an error here.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to send. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

params.name: filename
params.descHtml: The file name sent to the server. By default, it is the last part of the path.

params.name: contentType
params.descHtml: The media type of this part. If it is not given, a multipart field is sent as application/octet-stream. A whole body uses the call's own contentType.

doc.returnHtml: A part. Pass it as body or as one key of multipart.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path.
Nothing exists at $path, or the operating system did not return its details.

members.name: bytes
members.signature: bytes(secret tainted string|secret tainted bytes $data, string $filename, { contentType?: string }): Core\Http\Part

doc.shortHtml: Creates a body, or one field of a multipart body, from bytes that are already in memory. You give the data a file name.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The bytes to send, as a string or a bytes.

params.name: filename
params.descHtml: The file name sent to the server. It is required, because the data has no name of its own.

params.name: contentType
params.descHtml: The media type of this part. The default is the same as for file.

doc.returnHtml: A part. Pass it as body or as one key of multipart.

classes.summaryHtml: Describes a request body, or one field of a multipart body. A file part is read from disk while it is sent, so the whole file is never in memory.

classes.name: Core\Http\Response
classes.summary: The reply to an outbound HTTP call: its status code, its headers, its body, and the TLS connection it came over. `Core\Http\Client::get()` returns one.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the reply's HTTP status code, exactly as the server sent it.
doc.returnHtml: The three-digit code from the status line. A 404 or a 500 is a normal reply and is returned here. Only a request that gets no reply at all throws an error.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the reply's body as text.
doc.returnHtml: The body, as a tainted string. Another server chose these bytes. The approved address tells you where they came from, but not what they contain. Each place that does not accept tainted text has its own check to clean it. There is no general one.

errors.descHtml: The body is not valid UTF-8, so it cannot be a string. The body is not repaired. A replacement character would change the body, and the program could not tell. bytes reads the same body without this check.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the reply's body as the bytes that arrived. Use it for replies that are not text, such as an image, an archive or a signature.
doc.returnHtml: Every byte of the body. It is tainted, for the same reason as text. The bytes are not checked. A reply that is not UTF-8 is returned here, but text throws an error for it.
