doc.shortHtml: Decodes the reply's body as JSON into an instance of T. It works like Core\Json::decodeAs on the bytes that bytes returns, with the same {maxDepth?} options. Write array<T> to read a JSON array as one instance per element.

params.name: maxDepth
params.descHtml: How deep the document may nest. A deeper document throws an error. A scalar document is depth 1.

doc.returnHtml: A new T built from the document's fields, or one T per element for an array<T>. Every text property of T must be declared tainted, because another server chose these bytes.

errors.descHtml: T has no #[Json\Derive] decoder. Or maxDepth is outside 1..=1024.

The body is not one complete JSON document within that depth. A reply with no body, or a body that is not UTF-8, also throws this error. Or the document is not the object T decodes from, or its fields are missing or have the wrong type. Each failed field is one issue on the error, with its own path. The reply's Content-Type header is not checked.

doc.shortHtml: Returns one header of the reply. The name matches in upper or lower case, whichever the server used.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The header name. Upper and lower case are treated the same, as RFC 9110 § 5.1 defines.

doc.returnHtml: The header's value, as a tainted string. If the server sent the header more than once, the values are joined with , in the order they arrived. The result is null if the reply has no such header.

errors.descHtml: The name is Set-Cookie. Two cookies joined into one string are not valid cookies, so this method does not join them. Use headers to read Set-Cookie.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every value the reply sent under one header name, as separate entries. Use it when the joined value from header is not enough. It is the only way to read Set-Cookie.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The header name. Upper and lower case are treated the same, as in header.

doc.returnHtml: One tainted entry per header line, in the order they arrived. The result is an empty array if the reply has no such header. A header sent once gives an array with one entry.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the details of the TLS connection this reply came over. They include the settings both sides agreed on, and whether the server's certificate was checked.
doc.returnHtml: The TLS details. The result is null if the reply did not use TLS. That is the case for a plain http call, or for a call that a test served from its table of replies.

classes.summaryHtml: The reply to an outbound HTTP call: its status code, its headers, its body, and the TLS connection it came over. Core\Http\Client::get() returns one.

classes.name: Core\Http\Socket
classes.summary: A WebSocket connection your program opened to another server: it sends and receives messages until one side closes it. `Core\Http\Client::openSocket()` returns one.

doc.shortHtml: Waits for the next message from the peer and returns it. When the connection is closed, it returns null.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Socket\Message. Its text() or bytes() returns the content, which is tainted because it comes from the network. Its topic() and value() are null, because only a message from another isolate sets them. null means the connection is closed, by the peer or by your program.

errors.descHtml: The peer sent nothing for longer than idle, or the socket's maxDuration ended while this call was waiting. A peer that sends only pings is not silent, so only maxDuration limits it.
The connection failed while this call was waiting for a message.
The peer sent a message larger than maxMessage. The socket is closed with code 1009 before the error is thrown. This stops the peer from filling the task's memory with a message that nobody reads.
Another receive() is already waiting on this socket. Each message goes to one receiver, so only the task that owns the socket reads from it.

doc.shortHtml: Sends one text message to the peer.

params.name: frame
params.descHtml: The text to send, as one RFC 6455 text message, however many frames it needs. A tainted value is allowed. Text your program sends to another server cannot run as code on your side.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing.

errors.descHtml: The socket is closed, so the message cannot be sent.
The frame was not written before sendTimeout ended. This usually means the peer has stopped reading. It is also thrown when the socket's maxDuration ends first.
The connection failed while the frame was going out.

doc.shortHtml: Sends one binary message to the peer. send sends a text message.

params.name: frame
params.descHtml: The bytes to send, as one binary message. A tainted value is allowed, as it is for send.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing.

errors.descHtml: The socket is closed, so the message cannot be sent.
The frame was not written before sendTimeout ended. This usually means the peer has stopped reading. It is also thrown when the socket's maxDuration ends first.
The connection failed while the frame was going out.

doc.shortHtml: Closes the connection. It sends the close frame and waits for the peer's close frame, up to sendTimeout. Then it frees the connection.

params.name: code
params.descHtml: The close code to send. If you leave it out, it is 1000, a normal close.

params.name: reason
params.descHtml: Text to send with the code, for a peer that logs it. If you leave it out, no text is sent.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. If the peer never sends its close frame, the connection is closed anyway, without an error. So a normal close needs no catch. Closing a socket that is already closed does nothing.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the subprotocol that the opening handshake chose, from the ones in protocols.
doc.returnHtml: The name the peer chose. It is null if the call offered no protocol or the peer chose none. If the peer chooses a name that was not offered, the handshake fails and no socket is returned.

classes.summaryHtml: A WebSocket connection your program opened to another server: it sends and receives messages until one side closes it. Core\Http\Client::openSocket() returns one.

classes.name: Core\Http\Stream
classes.summary: A reply whose body is read while it arrives. `status()` and the header methods work at any time. The body can be read once, with one of `events()`, `lines()`, `chunks()` or `saveTo()`.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the status code of the reply. It works before the body is read.
doc.returnHtml: The three-digit status code, as an int. A 4xx or 5xx code is returned like any other code. It does not throw an error.

doc.shortHtml: Returns one header of the reply, by name. When the server sent the header more than once, the values are joined into one, as RFC 9110 § 5.3 allows.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The header name. Upper and lower case do not matter.

doc.returnHtml: The header value, or null when the reply has no such header. The value is tainted, which means it came from outside your program, like every byte of a reply.

errors.descHtml: The name is Set-Cookie. Its values cannot be joined, so use headers to read them.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every value of one header of the reply, as separate items. header joins the same values into one string.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The header name. Upper and lower case do not matter.

doc.returnHtml: The values in the order they arrived, each tainted. A header that arrived once gives a list of one value. A header that never arrived gives an empty list.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the body as server-sent events, in the WHATWG EventSource format. Use it for a text/event-stream reply.
doc.returnHtml: An Iterable<Core\Http\Event> that a foreach can loop over once. An event is complete at the blank line that ends it. A comment line is skipped. A retry line is read and ignored, because your program decides when to reconnect.

errors.descHtml: The body of this stream has already been read. A body can be read only once, in one way. The error message names the method that read it.
A line of the reply is longer than the line limit, or the data of one event is longer than the event limit. Both limits are fixed, so a server cannot make your program use unlimited memory.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the body one line at a time. Use it for a reply that sends text line by line, such as JSON Lines.
doc.returnHtml: An Iterable<tainted string> that a foreach can loop over once. A line ends at \n, and a \r at the end of a line is removed. The last line does not need a \n.

errors.descHtml: The body of this stream has already been read. The error message names the method that read it.
A line of the reply is longer than the line limit.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the body as raw bytes, in pieces. Use it for a reply whose bytes have a format of their own.
doc.returnHtml: An Iterable<tainted bytes> that a foreach can loop over once. The size of each piece depends on the network and has no meaning, so you cannot choose a size. If you need blocks of a fixed size, collect the bytes yourself.

errors.descHtml: The body of this stream has already been read. The error message names the method that read it.

doc.shortHtml: Writes the body directly to the file at $path. Only one piece of the body is in memory at a time. Needs the fs.write capability for the path. It uses Core\IO::writeStream to write the file.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to write. Nothing may exist at the path yet. This method cannot replace a file. The overwrite option of Core\IO::writeStream can.

params.name: max
params.descHtml: The largest number of bytes to accept. It is required, because the server chooses the length of the reply, and the bytes use disk space.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. When writing fails part of the way through, the partial file is deleted before the error is thrown. So nobody later finds an incomplete file.

errors.descHtml: The body of this stream has already been read. The error message names the method that read it.
The configuration does not allow fs.write for this path, or the body is longer than max bytes.
Something is already at the path, or the operating system could not create or write the file.

classes.summaryHtml: A reply whose body is read while it arrives. status() and the header methods work at any time. The body can be read once, with one of events(), lines(), chunks() or saveTo().

classes.name: Core\Http\Target
classes.summary: A URL that `Core\Http::allowUrl` checked, with the addresses it was approved for. A call connects only to those addresses, so a second name lookup cannot send it somewhere else.
classes.summaryHtml: A URL that Core\Http::allowUrl checked, with the addresses it was approved for. A call connects only to those addresses, so a second name lookup cannot send it somewhere else.

classes.name: Core\Http\TlsInfo
classes.summary: The details of the TLS connection a reply came over: the TLS version, the cipher, the server's certificates, and whether they were checked. `Core\Http\Response::tls()` returns one.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the TLS version that both sides agreed on.
doc.returnHtml: TLSv1.3 or TLSv1.2, the way TLS tools print it. For a version that this build cannot name, the result is the version's 0x code from the registry.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the cipher suite that both sides agreed on, by its IANA registry name.
doc.returnHtml: A name such as TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256. If the registry has no name for the suite, the result is its 0x code.

doc.shortHtml: Returns whether the connection checked both the server's certificate chain and the name on it.
doc.returnHtml: true if the chain was checked up to a trusted root, and the URL's host matched the certificate. The trusted roots are the configured roots or the call's own tlsCa. false if the call skipped either check. A call can skip a check only if a [capabilities.tls] grant lists the host.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the certificate chain the server sent, as PEM, leaf first.
doc.returnHtml: One PEM block per certificate, leaf first. The result is an empty array if the server sent none. Every entry is tainted, because the server chose these bytes.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the subject of the leaf certificate, written as an RFC 4514 distinguished name.
doc.returnHtml: The same text that openssl x509 -subject prints, such as CN=api.example.com. It is tainted, for the same reason as peerChain.

errors.descHtml: The server sent no certificate, or its leaf certificate is not X.509 that this method can read. version, cipher, verified and peerChain still work, because they do not read inside a certificate.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the issuer of the leaf certificate, written as an RFC 4514 distinguished name.
doc.returnHtml: Who signed the leaf certificate, in the same format as subject. It is tainted for the same reason.

errors.descHtml: The server sent no certificate, or its leaf certificate is not X.509 that this method can read. version, cipher, verified and peerChain still work, because they do not read inside a certificate.

doc.shortHtml: Returns when the leaf certificate stops being valid. This is its notAfter field.
doc.returnHtml: The instant when the server's certificate expires. Operators often want a program to check this for the services it calls.

errors.descHtml: The server sent no certificate, or its leaf certificate is not X.509 that this method can read. version, cipher, verified and peerChain still work, because they do not read inside a certificate.
The certificate has no end date. Its notAfter is 9999-12-31, which is later than the last Core\Time\Instant.

classes.summaryHtml: The details of the TLS connection a reply came over: the TLS version, the cipher, the server's certificates, and whether they were checked. Core\Http\Response::tls() returns one.

classes.name: Core\IO
classes.summary: Reads, writes, copies and lists files and directories. Each method needs the `fs.read` or `fs.write` capability for its path, and throws an error instead of returning `false`. `open` gives a `Core\IO\File` to read or write part of a file.

doc.shortHtml: What an open handle may do. There is no binary or text mode: every handle reads and writes the bytes unchanged.
Returns the whole content of a file as text. It needs the fs.read capability for the path. The check uses the resolved path, so a symlink or a .. that leaves the allowed folders throws an error.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to read. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

doc.returnHtml: The file's content as a string, with nothing stripped. The content must be UTF-8 text; readText reads a file written in another charset.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path. The message names the capability the way nvs.toml writes it. Or the file is larger than [limits] max_output, the limit for a single read in a request. The same setting limits the captured output of a child process. Or the file is not valid UTF-8, and the message names the byte where the text stops.
The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. The file does not exist, is a directory, or could not be read.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces a file's whole content. It creates the file if it does not exist. It needs the fs.write capability for the path. Permission to read a folder does not give permission to write in it.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to write. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

params.name: content
params.descHtml: The bytes to write. They become the file's entire content. append is the method that adds to what is already there.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A failure throws an error. It never returns false, so a caller that ignores the result does not miss a failure.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.write for this path. This is checked before anything is created, so the failed write leaves no file behind.
The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. A directory is missing, the filesystem is read-only, or the process does not have permission.

doc.shortHtml: Adds content to the end of a file. It creates the file if it does not exist. It needs the fs.write capability for the path.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to add to. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

params.name: content
params.descHtml: The bytes to add. The file's current content is kept, and these bytes come after it. The operating system finds the end of the file when it writes. The file is not read first.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A failure throws an error. It never returns false, so a caller that ignores the result does not miss a failure.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.write for this path. This is checked before anything is created, so the failed append leaves no file behind.
The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. A directory is missing, the filesystem is read-only, or the path is a directory.

members.name: writeStream
members.signature: writeStream(string $path, array<bytes>|Iterable<bytes>|Iterator<bytes> $src, { max?: uint, overwrite?: bool }): void

doc.shortHtml: Writes a sequence of bytes chunks to $path as they arrive. Only one chunk is in memory at a time. Examples are an upload part, a response body or a decompressed archive. It needs the fs.write capability for the path.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to write. It must not already exist unless overwrite says otherwise.

params.name: src
params.descHtml: The chunks, in order: an array<bytes>, an Iterable<bytes> or an Iterator<bytes>. Each chunk is written and then freed, so memory use does not grow with the length of the source.

params.name: max
params.descHtml: The most bytes to accept across the whole stream. When it is not given, there is no limit. Nothing else limits the size of a file on disk, so this is the only limit.

params.name: overwrite
params.descHtml: Whether an existing file may be replaced. It is false by default, because the file name usually comes from a client.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. If a write fails part-way through, the partial file is removed before the error is thrown. A later reader never finds a cut-off file that the program thinks is complete.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.write for this path, or the stream ran past max bytes.
Something is already at the path and overwrite is false. Or the operating system did not allow the file to be created or written.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether anything is at $path. The result is true for a directory as well as a file. It needs the fs.read capability. The capability is checked before the path is used, so a path outside it throws an error.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The name to look for. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

doc.returnHtml: true if something is at the path, false if nothing is there. A missing path is a normal result here and not an error. size throws an error for it.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path. This error is different from false. A program without access to a folder cannot use this method to learn what is in it.
The operating system could not say whether the path exists. For example, the process may not open a parent directory. That is not the same as a missing path.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $path is a regular file. Symbolic links are followed, so a link to a file gives true. It needs the fs.read capability, which is checked before the path is used.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path to check. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

doc.returnHtml: true for a regular file. false for a directory, for any other kind of entry, and for a path where nothing exists. A missing path gives false and does not throw an error.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path. This error is different from false, as it is for exists.
The operating system could not say whether the path is a file. For example, the process may not open a parent directory. That is not the same as a missing file.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $path is a directory. Symbolic links are followed, so a link to a directory gives true. It needs the fs.read capability.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path to check. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

doc.returnHtml: true for a directory. false for a file, for any other kind of entry, and for a path where nothing exists. A path can exist and still give false for both isFile and isDir.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path.
The operating system could not say whether the path is a directory. For example, the process may not open a parent directory.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether this process can read what is at $path right now. It needs the fs.read capability, which is checked first. A path outside that capability throws an error.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file or directory to check. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

doc.returnHtml: true if the operating system would allow a read, false if it would not. A path where nothing exists gives false. The result is only true at the moment of the call, so a read after it can still fail.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether this process can write to what is at $path right now. It needs the fs.write capability. A program that may only read cannot check where it could write.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file or directory to check. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

doc.returnHtml: true if the operating system would allow a write, false if it would not. A path where nothing exists gives false. As with isReadable, the result is only true at the moment of the call.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.write for this path.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the size of the file at $path in bytes, as the operating system reports it. It needs the fs.read capability.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to measure. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

doc.returnHtml: The byte count as a uint. For a text file this counts bytes, not characters. Core\Str::length gives the length of a string in graphemes (what a person counts as one character).

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path.

The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. Nothing is at the path, or its metadata could not be read. A missing file has no size, so this method throws an error. exists returns false for it.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the time the file at $path was last written, as a Core\Time\Instant. It needs the fs.read capability.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file or directory to check. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

doc.returnHtml: The modification time as an exact point in time, with no time zone. Call ->in($zone) to get a calendar date and time.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path.
Nothing is at the path, or its metadata could not be read. Or the platform does not record a modification time, or the recorded time is outside the range of a Core\Time\Instant.

doc.shortHtml: Returns what the operating system reports about $path, as a Core\IO\Metadata. A program that needs several facts about a file makes only one system call. It needs the fs.read capability.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file or directory to measure. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\IO\Metadata. Its values are from the moment of the call. They do not change when the file changes later.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path.
Nothing is at the path, or its metadata could not be read. A missing file has no metadata, so this method throws an error. exists returns false for it.

doc.shortHtml: Copies a file. It needs fs.read for the source and fs.write for the destination. Permission to read a folder never gives permission to write in it.

params.name: from
params.descHtml: The file to read. It is left exactly as it was.

params.name: to
params.descHtml: The file to create. Anything already at this path is replaced, as write replaces it. The program names this path itself, together with the source.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A failure throws an error. It never returns false, so a caller that ignores the result does not miss a failure.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for the source or fs.write for the destination. Both are checked before either is used, so a failed check copies nothing.

The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. Nothing is at the source, the destination directory does not exist, or the process does not have permission. A destination that is the source file itself, however the path is written, also throws an error. The file stays as it was. The message names both paths.

doc.shortHtml: Moves a file by renaming it. It needs fs.write for both paths. The source needs fs.write too, because a move removes the source file.

params.name: from
params.descHtml: The path that stops existing.

params.name: to
params.descHtml: The new path of the file. Anything already there is replaced.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The operating system does the rename, so it is atomic. The destination always has either the whole new file or the file it had before. A move between filesystems fails. It is not done as a copy and a delete, because that is not atomic and needs different capabilities. To do that, call copy and then remove.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.write for one of the two paths. Both are checked before either is used.

The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. Nothing is at the source, the destination directory does not exist, or the two paths are on different filesystems. The message names both paths.

doc.shortHtml: Deletes the file at $path. It needs the fs.write capability, because deleting a file is a write.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to delete. To delete a directory, use removeDir.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. Removing a path where nothing exists throws an error. A program that deleted nothing is never told that it succeeded.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.write for this path. Permission to read a folder does not give permission to delete from it.
The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. Nothing is at the path, it is a directory, or the process may not delete it.

doc.shortHtml: Makes sure a directory exists at $path. It also creates every missing parent directory. It needs the fs.write capability.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The directory that must exist. Every missing directory above it is created too. All of them are inside the path the capability is checked for.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A directory that already exists is a success, not an error. The method only promises that the directory exists afterwards, so a caller needs no exists check first. removeDir works differently. It does not delete directories recursively.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.write for this path. This is checked before anything is created, so the failed call leaves no directory behind.
The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. The path is empty, a part of the path exists and is a file, or the process may not create a directory there.

doc.shortHtml: Deletes the empty directory at $path. It needs the fs.write capability. There is no recursive form, so one wrong argument cannot delete a whole tree. To empty a directory, a program walks it and removes each entry.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The directory to delete. It must be empty.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A failure throws an error. It never returns false.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.write for this path.
The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. Nothing is at the path, it is not a directory, or it still has entries in it.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the names of the entries in the directory at $path, as an array<string>. The list never contains . and ... It needs the fs.read capability. The order is the operating system's own, and the list is not sorted. Core\Arr::sort sorts it.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The directory to read. A file throws an error.

doc.returnHtml: One string per entry. Each one is a name, not a path. The caller joins it to $path. Use within to make that join safe when the name came from outside the program. The whole list is in memory at once, so use this method for a directory that fits in memory. walk reads the whole tree under a directory.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path.
The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. Nothing is at the path, it is not a directory, or an entry could not be read partway through the listing.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every entry in the tree under $path, as an Iterable<string> of paths relative to $path. list reads one directory, and this method reads the whole tree. It needs the fs.read capability for every directory it enters, including the first one. A symbolic link is returned as an entry and is never followed, so the walk always ends.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The directory the walk starts at. A file throws an error, as it does for list.

doc.returnHtml: One string per entry anywhere under $path. Each one is a path relative to $path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. The caller joins it to $path, and within makes that join safe. All entries of a directory come before any entry inside them. Within one directory, the order is the operating system's own.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for a directory the walk tried to read. The message names the directory where the walk stopped. That is the start directory, unless the capability covers only part of the tree.
The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. Nothing is at the path, it is not a directory, or a directory inside the walk could not be read to the end.

doc.shortHtml: Creates a new, empty, private directory and returns its path. The directory is under [io] temp_root, or under the tmp folder in the data folder. It is created at once, so no other program can take its name first. It needs the fs.write capability for the path it creates. A configuration that allows only the working directory does not cover the temporary folder.
doc.returnHtml: The absolute path of a directory that exists, is empty, and belongs to this script. Novis deletes it and everything in it when the script ends. This happens after the last line of your code runs, however the script ends. A program never has to delete it, and it is never left behind. You may remove it earlier, and that is not an error. A file that must stay after the script ends does not belong in a temporary directory.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.write for the temporary folder. The message names the path that the capability must cover.

The capability allowed the call, but no directory could be created. The temporary folder is full, read-only or missing. Or there is no temporary folder, because [io] temp_root is not set and the data folder cannot be used.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the absolute path that $path resolves to. The operating system follows every ., .. and symbolic link. It needs the fs.read capability, because resolving a name reads the directories on the way. This is not a path traversal check. Use within for a path from outside: it resolves the path and checks that it stays inside a folder.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path to resolve. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it. Every part of the path must exist, including the last one.

doc.returnHtml: The resolved absolute path. Resolving the result again gives the same path, so you can compare two results for equality. Core\Path::normalize cannot do this. Two different ways to write the path of one file normalize to different strings. They canonicalize to the same string.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path.

The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. A part of the path does not exist or is not a directory, or a symbolic link loops. A missing path cannot be resolved, so this method throws an error. exists returns false for it.

doc.shortHtml: Resolves $path against $base and then checks that the result is still inside $base. This is the path traversal check, so its result is accepted where a tainted string is not. Core\Path::normalize cannot make this check. It removes .. from the text, but a symbolic link in the path can still lead somewhere else. It needs the fs.read capability for both paths, because resolving a path reads the directories above it.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The directory the result must stay inside. It must exist, because the check uses its canonical path.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path to resolve against $base. This is the untrusted part, and the reason to use this method. A relative $path is joined to $base, also when it is written directly in the code. It is not joined to the folder of the file that calls within. An absolute path is resolved too, and then the same check makes it fail.

doc.returnHtml: The resolved absolute path, as a plain string. It has no .., no symbolic links and no repeated separators. It is the path the operating system itself uses for the file.

errors.descHtml: The resolved path is not inside $base. The message names the base and the argument, but never the place the argument led to. So the error shows nothing about the target of a symbolic link. If the configuration does not grant fs.read for either path, the same error class is thrown earlier.
The capability allowed the call, but nothing could be resolved. $base does not exist or is not a directory, or no parent directory of the joined path exists.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the whole content of a file, converted from the charset it is written in. If a byte cannot be converted exactly, it throws an error. It needs the fs.read capability for the path, as read does.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to read. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

params.name: charset
params.descHtml: The encoding of the file's bytes. It is Core\Charset::Utf8 when it is not given. Novis strings are UTF-8, so UTF-8 text is read unchanged.

doc.returnHtml: The file's content as a string, converted from $charset. It never contains a replacement character, because a conversion that cannot be exact throws an error.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path. Or the file's bytes are not valid $charset. In that case the message names the offset of the first invalid sequence.
The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. The file does not exist, is a directory, or could not be read.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every line of a file, without its line ending. The file is split into lines the same way Core\Str::lines splits a string. It needs the fs.read capability for the path, as read does.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to read. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

doc.returnHtml: An Iterable<string>. A foreach loop gives the lines in file order, and you can loop over it again as often as you like. \n, \r\n and a single \r each end a line. A line ending at the end of the file does not add an empty last line. An empty file has no lines.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant fs.read for this path.
The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. The file does not exist, is a directory, or could not be read.

doc.shortHtml: Opens a file and returns a handle to read and write it. The mode is an enum value. It needs fs.read for Read, fs.write for Write and Append, and both for ReadWrite.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The file to open. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it.

params.name: mode
params.descHtml: What the handle may do, as a Core\IO::FileMode case.

doc.returnHtml: An open Core\IO\File. It is closed by close, and by the end of the request if the program never calls it.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not grant a capability this mode needs for this path.
The capability allowed the call, but the operating system did not. The mode is Read and nothing is at the path, the path is a directory, or this process may not open it.

doc.shortHtml: Reads everything from the program's standard input in one call. The result is tainted, because the bytes come from whoever started the program. It needs no capability, because the program starts with its standard input already open.
doc.returnHtml: Every byte until the end of input, as one tainted string. It is the empty string when the input is already closed. A program started with no input gets that. Input ends when the writer closes it, so at a terminal this call waits for the user. To ask the user a question, use the prompts in Core\Cli, which have a time limit.

errors.descHtml: The read failed in the operating system. The process writing to the pipe stopped, or standard input was not open for reading.
The input is not valid UTF-8. The message gives the position of the first byte that is not text.

classes.summaryHtml:
Reads, writes, copies and lists files and directories. Each method needs the fs.read or fs.write capability for its path, and throws an error instead of returning false. open gives a Core\IO\File to read or write part of a file.

Core\IO reads or replaces a whole file as text. Every call is a capability check first: the path must fall under a root that nvs.toml grants as fs.read or fs.write, and a read grant is not a write grant. A path the configuration does not grant throws a RuntimeError naming the capability, and the program may catch it and carry on; a path the configuration allows but the operating system refuses — no such file, a directory — throws an IOError. The check resolves the path through its deepest existing directory, so a file that does not exist yet is spelled from one — ./out.txt, not out.txt — or the check refuses it as not granted. Without an nvs.toml, every call is refused.

[capabilities.fs]
read = ["."]
write = ["."]
alpha
beta
<?nvs
string $text = Core\IO::read('data.txt');
echo Core\Str::length($text), " bytes\n";

Core\IO::write('./copy.txt', $text . "gamma\n");
echo Core\Str::trim(Core\IO::read('./copy.txt')), "\n";

try {
    Core\IO::read('./missing.txt');
} catch (IOError $io) {
    echo "missing: no such file\n";
}
try {
    Core\IO::read('../outside.txt');
} catch (RuntimeError $denied) {
    echo "outside: refused\n";
}
11 bytes
alpha
beta
gamma
missing: no such file
outside: refused

classes.name: Core\IO\File
classes.summary: An open file. `Core\IO::open` returns one. It reads and writes a part of the file at a time, and `seek` and `tell` move to a position and return it. `close` closes it, and a handle that is still open is closed when the request ends.

doc.shortHtml: Reads up to $max bytes from the handle's position and moves the position past them. It needs no capability of its own, because open already checked it.

params.name: max
params.descHtml: The most bytes to read. Fewer are returned when the file ends first.

doc.returnHtml: The bytes read, as a string. The text always ends with a whole character. When $max ends inside a character, that character stays in the file for the next read. An empty string means the end of the file.

errors.descHtml: The handle has already been closed.
The bytes are not valid UTF-8, or the next character is longer than $max. The handle does not move, so the next read starts at the same byte.
The read itself failed, or the handle was not opened for reading.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the next line and moves the handle past it. The line ending is read but not returned. \n, \r\n and \r all end a line, as they do for Core\Str::lines and Core\IO::lines.
doc.returnHtml: The line without its line ending, or null at the end of the file. Because of the null, there is no separate eof method. A last line with no line ending is still a line.

errors.descHtml: The handle has already been closed.
The line is not valid UTF-8. The handle does not move, so the next call reads the same line.
The read itself failed, or the handle was not opened for reading.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $data at the handle's position and moves the position past it. It needs no capability of its own, because open already checked it.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The data to write, as a string or as bytes. It is written exactly as it is.

doc.returnHtml: How many bytes were written. This is always every byte of $data. A partial write is retried until it is complete, so a caller never needs a loop.

errors.descHtml: The handle has already been closed.
The write itself failed, or the handle was not opened for writing.

doc.shortHtml: Moves the handle to $offset bytes from the start of the file. You can move past the end of the file. If you then write, the gap is filled with zeroes.

params.name: offset
params.descHtml: How many bytes from the start of the file the next read or write happens at.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. Use tell to get the position.

errors.descHtml: The handle has already been closed.
The seek itself failed. For example, the handle is a pipe or a terminal, which has no position.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the handle's position, in bytes from the start of the file. The next read or write happens at this position. Every method of this class leaves the position just after the bytes it used.
doc.returnHtml: The position, as a uint. Zero on a handle nothing has read or written yet, unless FileMode::Append put it at the end.

errors.descHtml: The handle has already been closed.
Getting the position failed. For example, the handle is a pipe or a terminal, which has no position.

doc.shortHtml: Sets the file's length to $size bytes. A smaller size deletes everything after it. A larger size fills the new part with zeroes.

params.name: size
params.descHtml: How long the file is to be afterwards, in bytes from its start.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The handle's position does not move. After a file is shortened, the position can be past its new end. tell still returns the old position. A write there leaves a gap filled with zeroes before the written bytes.

errors.descHtml: The handle has already been closed.
The resize itself failed. The most common cause is a handle opened with FileMode::Read, which the operating system does not resize.

doc.shortHtml: Sends everything written on this handle to the operating system. Novis writes directly to the operating system, so there is never data waiting in the handle.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing. This method does not wait until the data is on the disk.

errors.descHtml: The handle has already been closed.
The flush itself failed in the operating system. No method of this class causes this error now, but the operating system may still report one.

doc.shortHtml: Takes an exclusive lock on the file. The lock lasts until the handle closes. It never waits: if another handle has the lock, it throws an error at once.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing. There is no unlock. The lock lasts as long as the handle, so close releases it, and so does the end of the request.

errors.descHtml: The handle has already been closed.
Another handle already has the lock, or the operating system did not allow it. Whether the lock stops reads and writes by handles that do not have the lock depends on the platform.

doc.shortHtml: Closes the handle and frees the file descriptor. Calling it is optional, because every open handle is closed when the request ends.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing.

errors.descHtml: The handle has already been closed. Closing twice is a bug in the program, so it throws an error and is not ignored.

classes.summaryHtml: An open file. Core\IO::open returns one. It reads and writes a part of the file at a time, and seek and tell move to a position and return it. close closes it, and a handle that is still open is closed when the request ends.

classes.name: Core\IO\Lines
classes.summary: The lines of a file, which `Core\IO::lines` returns. Use it in a `foreach` loop to get one line at a time, as a string.
classes.summaryHtml: The lines of a file, which Core\IO::lines returns. Use it in a foreach loop to get one line at a time, as a string.

classes.name: Core\IO\Metadata
classes.summary: What `Core\IO::stat` returns about one path: its size, when it was last changed, and whether it is a file or a directory. All four are read at the same moment. They do not change when the file changes later, so call `stat` again to get new values.

doc.shortHtml: The file's size in bytes at the moment stat was called. It needs no capability, because stat already checked the path.
doc.returnHtml: The byte count as a uint. For a directory, the number depends on the platform and has no portable meaning.

doc.shortHtml: When the file was last written, as a Core\Time\Instant. It is the same value that Core\IO::modifiedAt returns, taken from this stat result.
doc.returnHtml: The modification time as an exact point in time, with no time zone.

doc.shortHtml: Whether the path was a regular file. Most paths are either a file or a directory, but not all. A socket, a device node and a named pipe give false for both isFile and isDir.
doc.returnHtml: true for a regular file, false for anything else that was there.

doc.shortHtml: Whether the path was a directory. As with isFile, some paths are neither a file nor a directory.
doc.returnHtml: true for a directory, false for anything else that was there.

classes.summaryHtml: What Core\IO::stat returns about one path: its size, when it was last changed, and whether it is a file or a directory. All four are read at the same moment. They do not change when the file changes later, so call stat again to get new values.

classes.name: Core\IO\Walk
classes.summary: Every file and directory under a directory, which `Core\IO::walk` returns. Use it in a `foreach` loop to get each path, relative to the directory you started from.
classes.summaryHtml: Every file and directory under a directory, which Core\IO::walk returns. Use it in a foreach loop to get each path, relative to the directory you started from.

classes.name: Core\Json
classes.summary: Converts values to JSON text and back. `encode` writes a value as JSON, `decode` reads JSON into arrays and scalars, and `decodeAs` reads it into a class or a shape. A document that is not valid JSON throws a `ParseError`.

members.name: encode
members.signature: encode(mixed $value, { pretty?: bool, escapeUnicode?: bool }): string

doc.shortHtml: Converts $value to JSON text. It can be a scalar, an array, an anonymous object or an instance of a class with #[Json\Derive]. The text is on one line unless pretty is set.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to encode: null, bool, int, uint, float, decimal, string, an array, a { name: value } shape, or an instance of a class with #[Json\Derive].

params.name: pretty
params.descHtml: Writes the output across several lines, with indentation. By default, the output is on one line.

params.name: escapeUnicode
params.descHtml: Writes every non-ASCII character as a \uXXXX escape. By default, UTF-8 text is written as it is.

doc.returnHtml: The JSON text. It is a tainted string when $value can contain text from outside the program. That is a tainted string, or a mixed or object value, anywhere inside it.

errors.descHtml: $value contains something that JSON cannot represent. This is a NaN or infinite float, a value of a type with no JSON form, an instance of a class without #[Json\Derive], or more than 1024 levels of nesting.

doc.shortHtml: Parses the JSON text $json into a value. A JSON object becomes a string-keyed array, a JSON array becomes a list, and a scalar stays a scalar. Text that is not valid JSON throws an error.

params.name: json
params.descHtml: The JSON text to parse.

params.name: maxDepth
params.descHtml: The deepest nesting allowed. A scalar document is depth 1, and [1] is depth 2. The default is 512, and the largest value is 1024.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded value: null, bool, int, float, string, or an array. A JSON object is always a string-keyed array, never an object.

errors.descHtml: $json is not a valid JSON document, nests deeper than maxDepth, has an object with the same key twice, or contains a whole number too large for int. The error has one issue, and its path is empty.
maxDepth is 0 or above 1024.

doc.shortHtml: Parses the JSON object $json into an instance of T, a class with #[Json\Derive]. It reads every declared property, and it runs the constructor only when all of them match. Write array<T> to read a JSON array as one instance per element. You do not need to copy each field into the object yourself.

params.name: json
params.descHtml: The JSON text to parse. Its top level must be an object. When T is written as array<C>, its top level must be an array.

params.name: maxDepth
params.descHtml: The deepest nesting allowed. A scalar document is depth 1, and [1] is depth 2. The default is 512, and the largest value is 1024.

doc.returnHtml: A new T created from the fields of the document. For an array<C>, it is one new C per element, in the order of the document.

errors.descHtml: $json is not a valid JSON document, nests deeper than maxDepth, has an object with the same key twice, or contains a whole number too large for int. It is also thrown when the top level is not an object, or not an array for an array<C>. Fields that are missing or have the wrong type throw it too. Each failed field is one issue on the error, with its own path. The message gives the number of issues. A list stops at its first bad element, and each path contains the position of that element.
T cannot be read from JSON because it does not have #[Json\Derive]. It is also thrown when maxDepth is 0 or above 1024.

The call stack is full when a constructor runs. This happens when the call starts with the stack almost full, or when a constructor recurses deeply. A deep document within maxDepth does not throw this error.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether decode accepts $json at the default depth of 512. It parses the text to check it.

params.name: json
params.descHtml: The JSON text to check.

doc.returnHtml: true when $json parses. false for text that is not valid JSON, nesting deeper than 512, or a whole number too large for int.

classes.summaryHtml:
Converts values to JSON text and back. encode writes a value as JSON, decode reads JSON into arrays and scalars, and decodeAs reads it into a class or a shape. A document that is not valid JSON throws a ParseError.

Core\Json::encode writes any scalar, array or instance of a class carrying #[Core\Json\Derive] as JSON: a list becomes a JSON array, any other array a JSON object with its insertion order kept, and an instance of a class without the attribute is refused. decode answers mixed — an object as a string-keyed array — and throws ParseError on a malformed or too-deep document. decodeAs<T> reads a document straight into a class that carries #[Core\Json\Derive], checking every declared field — private ones included — against its type (?T is the only way a field admits null) and reporting every failure at once in one ParseError's issues. #[Core\Json\Field(name: "…")] gives one field its wire name. T is that class or an array<T> of it, and nothing else: decodeAs<array<User>> reads a document whose top level is a JSON array as one User per element, reporting a bad element under its index.

<?nvs
#[Core\Json\Derive]
class User
{
    public string $name;
    public ?int $age;
    #[Core\Json\Field(name: 'is_admin')]
    public bool $admin;
    public function constructor(string $name, ?int $age, bool $admin)
    {
        $this->name = $name;
        $this->age = $age;
        $this->admin = $admin;
    }
}
echo Core\Json::encode(['id' => 7, 'tags' => ['a', 'b'], 'ok' => true]), "\n";
var $doc = Core\Json::decode("{\"n\": 3.5, \"list\": [1, 2]}");
echo Core\Json::encode($doc, { pretty: true }), "\n";
User $u = Core\Json::decodeAs<User>("{\"name\":\"Ada\",\"age\":null,\"is_admin\":true}");
echo $u->name, ' ', $u->age ?? 'unknown', ' ', Core\Json::encode($u), "\n";
echo Core\Json::isValid('{oops}') ? 'valid' : 'invalid', "\n";
try {
    Core\Json::decodeAs<User>("{\"name\":1}");
} catch (ParseError $e) {
    echo Core\Arr::count($e->issues), " issues\n";
}
{"id":7,"tags":["a","b"],"ok":true}
{
  "n": 3.5,
  "list": [
    1,
    2
  ]
}
Ada unknown {"name":"Ada","age":null,"is_admin":true}
invalid
3 issues

classes.name: Core\Jwe
classes.summary: Encrypts a text into a JWE token that only the holder of the right key can read. `encrypt` writes the token and `decrypt` reads the text back. The key is a `Jwe\Key`, and the method that made the key chooses the algorithm.

doc.shortHtml: Encrypts $payload with $key and returns a compact JWE token. The content is encrypted with A256GCM. The method that made $key sets the key algorithm.

params.name: payload
params.descHtml: The text to encrypt. decrypt returns exactly this text, as a tainted value.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The key, made by one of the four static methods of Jwe\Key. That method also sets alg. A key made by Jwe\Key::own encrypts to its own public key.

doc.returnHtml: Five base64url parts without padding, joined by dots. They are the protected header, the encrypted key, the 12-byte IV, the ciphertext and the 16-byte tag. The encrypted key is empty for dir and ECDH-ES. Each call uses a new IV, so the token is different every time.

errors.descHtml: The public key or key pair in $key has a point that gives no usable shared secret.
This process does not have enough memory for a buffer the size of the token.

doc.shortHtml: Decrypts $token with each key in $keys, in order, and returns the payload. If no key works, it throws an error. The result is **tainted**. Decrypting proves who wrote the payload, but not that its content is safe to use.

params.name: token
params.descHtml: The token text, as it arrived. A tainted value is allowed here, because tokens usually come from outside.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The keys to try, in order. A token encrypted with any of these keys can be decrypted. A key made by Jwe\Key::password must be the only key, because each try is slow. A key made by Jwe\Key::recipient is a public key and decrypts nothing.

doc.returnHtml: The payload, exactly as it was encrypted, as a tainted string.

errors.descHtml: $keys is empty, or it contains a Jwe\Key::recipient key, or it contains a Jwe\Key::password key together with other keys.

No key in $keys can decrypt $token. The token may not have five parts, or its header has fields this class does not read. Its alg may not match $keys, or the token was changed. All cases have the same message, so an attacker cannot learn which check failed.
The token was decrypted, but its payload is not valid UTF-8 text.

classes.summaryHtml: Encrypts a text into a JWE token that only the holder of the right key can read. encrypt writes the token and decrypt reads the text back. The key is a Jwe\Key, and the method that made the key chooses the algorithm.

classes.name: Core\Jwe\Key
classes.summary: The key for `Core\Jwe`. Each static method makes one kind of key: `shared` from 32 secret bytes, `password` from a password, `recipient` from another party's public key, and `own` from your own key pair. You cannot read the key back out.

doc.shortHtml: Makes a key for dir. The shared key itself encrypts the content. No other key is derived or wrapped.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: 32 bytes that both sides already have. Core\Crypto::generateKey() returns such a key.

doc.returnHtml: A key for which encrypt writes "alg":"dir". With this key, decrypt accepts only that alg.

errors.descHtml: $key is not 32 bytes long, so it is not a valid key.

doc.shortHtml: Makes a key for PBES2-HS256+A128KW. A key is derived from a person's password. A random content key is then encrypted with it.

params.name: password
params.descHtml: The password, of any length. It can come from Core\Cli::secret or a form field. It is not hashed for storage. Use Core\Password for that.

doc.returnHtml: A key that encrypt derives with the minimum iteration count. The count and the salt are written into the header, so the other side can derive the same key.

doc.shortHtml: Makes a key for sending with ECDH-ES. It is the public key of the other party. Only that party's key pair can decrypt the token.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: A P256 or X25519 public key, already validated by Core\Crypto\PublicKey::read.

doc.returnHtml: A key for encrypt. Each call makes a new temporary key pair and writes its public key into the header as epk. This key cannot decrypt, because it is a public key.

errors.descHtml: $key is an Ed25519 or RSA key. Neither can be used for key agreement.

doc.shortHtml: Makes a key for receiving with ECDH-ES. It is your program's own key pair. It decrypts tokens that other parties encrypted to its public key.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: A P256 or X25519 key pair, read with Core\Crypto\KeyPair::read.

doc.returnHtml: A key that decrypt uses with the epk of the token. With this key, encrypt encrypts to the pair's own public key.

errors.descHtml: $key is an Ed25519 or RSA pair. Neither can be used for key agreement.

classes.summaryHtml: The key for Core\Jwe. Each static method makes one kind of key: shared from 32 secret bytes, password from a password, recipient from another party's public key, and own from your own key pair. You cannot read the key back out.

classes.name: Core\Jwt
classes.summary: Signs and checks JSON Web Tokens (JWT). `sign` and `signObject` write a token that always expires. `verify` checks a token your own program signed, and `verifyIssued` checks a token from another service. Both throw an error when the token is not valid.

members.name: sign
members.signature: sign(array<string> $claims, Core\Time\Duration $lifetime, secret bytes|Core\Crypto\KeyPair $key, { kid?: string, typ?: string, embedKey?: bool }): string

doc.shortHtml: Signs $claims into a JWT that expires $lifetime from now. $key signs the token, and the key decides the algorithm. This method always writes the expiry, so every token it returns has one.

params.name: claims
params.descHtml: The claims for the token, by name. This method writes exp and iat, so $claims may not contain them. Every other claim goes into the token unchanged.

params.name: lifetime
params.descHtml: How long the token is valid, such as 15m, 1h or 7d. It must be greater than zero. A token that is already expired is a bug in the program.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: A shared secret of at least 32 bytes, which signs with HS256. Core\Crypto::generateKey() returns one. A longer secret that you share with another service also works. The key can also be a Core\Crypto\KeyPair. It signs with ES256, EdDSA, RS256 or PS256, depending on its kind. There is no algorithm parameter, because the key decides the algorithm.

params.name: kid
params.descHtml: The key's name, written into the header. Use it when the receiver has several keys. By default there is no kid. The value is written exactly as given. It does not choose which key signs the token.

params.name: typ
params.descHtml: The header's typ. It is JWT if you leave it out. RFC 9068's access tokens use at+jwt.

params.name: embedKey
params.descHtml: Writes the public key of the pair into the header, as a minimal JWK (RFC 7638). A DPoP proof needs this. It is off by default. With a shared secret it throws an error, because a secret has no public key.

doc.returnHtml: The token as a string: a header, a payload and a signature in base64url, joined by two dots. You can put it in a header, a query string or a JSON body without escaping.

errors.descHtml: $key is a secret shorter than 32 bytes, or an X25519 pair, which cannot sign. { embedKey: true } is used with a shared secret. $lifetime is zero or negative. $claims contains exp or iat, or an entry without a name.
The process does not have enough memory for the token.

members.name: signObject
members.signature: signObject(object $claims, Core\Time\Duration $lifetime, Core\Crypto\KeyPair $key, { kid?: string, typ?: string, embedKey?: bool }): string

doc.shortHtml: Signs a shape or an object $claims into a JWT that expires $lifetime from now. A key pair signs it, and the pair decides the algorithm. The claims are written the way Core\Json::encode writes them, with iat and exp added at the end.

params.name: claims
params.descHtml: A shape, or an object of a class with #[Core\Json\Derive]. It is encoded as a JSON object. This method writes exp and iat, so $claims may not contain them. A value that cannot be encoded as JSON is a bug in the program.

params.name: lifetime
params.descHtml: How long the token is valid, such as 15m, 1h or 7d. It must be greater than zero. A token that is already expired is a bug in the program.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: A Core\Crypto\KeyPair. It signs with ES256, EdDSA, RS256 or PS256, depending on its kind. A shared secret is not allowed here. A token with these claims is for another service, and Core\Jwt::verify reads only the string claims that sign writes.

params.name: kid
params.descHtml: The key's name, written into the header. Use it when the receiver has several keys. By default there is no kid. The value is written exactly as given. It does not choose which key signs the token.

params.name: typ
params.descHtml: The header's typ. It is JWT if you leave it out. RFC 9068's access tokens use at+jwt.

params.name: embedKey
params.descHtml: Writes the public key of the pair into the header, as a minimal JWK (RFC 7638). A DPoP proof needs this. It is off by default.

doc.returnHtml: The token as a string, in the same format that sign returns. The payload is the claims object, with iat and exp as its last two fields.

errors.descHtml: $claims contains exp or iat. $claims cannot be encoded as JSON, for example a class without #[Core\Json\Derive], a secret value, a bytes value or a cycle. $key is an X25519 pair, which cannot sign. $lifetime is zero or negative.
The process does not have enough memory for the token.

doc.shortHtml: Checks that $key signed $token and that the token has not expired. Then it returns the token's claims. If a check fails, it throws an error. It never returns an empty value that a comparison could take for a valid token.

params.name: token
params.descHtml: The token as the request sent it, in its three-part form.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The shared secret that was given to sign, or the issuer's secret. The method compares the token's alg with the key's algorithm. It never uses alg to choose the algorithm.

doc.returnHtml: Every claim in the payload, by name, and each one is tainted. A signature shows who wrote a value, but not that the value is safe to use. The result includes exp and iat as strings of decimal digits.

errors.descHtml: $key is shorter than 32 bytes, so it cannot be a signing key.
The token was not signed with this key. The message is the same for every reason the signature check fails. It also throws when the token has expired, has no exp, or has a claim that is not a string.

members.name: verifyIssued
members.signature: verifyIssued<T>(string $token, Core\Jwt\KeySet|Core\Crypto\PublicKey $keys, string $issuer, string $audience, { leeway?: Core\Time\Duration, typ?: string, nonce?: string, maxAge?: Core\Time\Duration }): T

doc.shortHtml: Checks a token from another service and returns its claims as the type you wrote. It checks the header, finds the one key that may have signed the token, and checks the signature. Then it checks the time and the registered claims, in that order. If a check fails, it throws an error. It never returns an empty value.

params.name: token
params.descHtml: The token as the request sent it, in its three-part form. A token longer than 8 KiB throws an error and is not read.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The issuer's key set, in which the header's kid names exactly one key. It can also be one public key. The method never tries every key. A token without a kid is checked only against a set with exactly one key. The method compares the token's alg with the key's algorithm. It never uses alg to choose the algorithm.

params.name: issuer
params.descHtml: What the token's iss must equal, exactly.

params.name: audience
params.descHtml: What the token's aud must be, or must contain. A token with more than one audience must also have an azp equal to this value.

params.name: leeway
params.descHtml: How much the clocks may differ, at the start and at the end of the valid time. It is 60 seconds if you leave it out. A negative value or more than 5 minutes throws an error. It makes the expiry check less strict, but never turns it off.

params.name: typ
params.descHtml: The typ the header must have. The comparison ignores case and an application/ prefix. RFC 9068's access tokens use at+jwt. If you leave it out, any typ is allowed.

params.name: nonce
params.descHtml: The value the token's nonce claim must equal. It is compared in constant time. If you give it, a token without a nonce throws an error.

params.name: maxAge
params.descHtml: How old the token's auth_time may be. If you give it, a token without an auth_time throws an error.

doc.returnHtml: An object of the type you wrote, decoded from the payload the way Core\Json::decodeAs decodes a document. Its string properties must be declared tainted, or the call does not compile. A signature shows who wrote a claim, but not that the claim is safe to use.

errors.descHtml: leeway is negative or more than 5 minutes. The type you wrote is a list, and a token's payload is never a list. The key is an X25519 key, which cannot verify a signature.

The token was not signed with this issuer's key. Its header has a parameter that is not allowed, or no key matches it. The message is the same for all of these. It also throws when a valid token is outside its valid time. A registered claim with the wrong value throws too, and the message names the claim.

classes.summaryHtml: Signs and checks JSON Web Tokens (JWT). sign and signObject write a token that always expires. verify checks a token your own program signed, and verifyIssued checks a token from another service. Both throw an error when the token is not valid.

classes.name: Core\Jwt\KeySet
classes.summary: The public keys another service uses to sign its tokens. `read` reads them from the JWKS document that service publishes. `Core\Jwt::verifyIssued` then checks a token with the one key its `kid` names.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the signing keys from a JWKS document. A token can then be checked with the one key its kid names. A key of a kind this class does not use is skipped. A document with an error throws an error, and no key from it is used.

params.name: jwks
params.descHtml: The document as the issuer published it. This method only reads it. Fetching, caching and replacing the keys is the job of a package. The method keeps no state between calls.

params.name: rsaScheme
params.descHtml: The scheme for an RSA key that has no alg: RsaPkcs1 for RS256 or RsaPss for PS256. A key's own alg always wins. An RSA key with neither is not allowed, and the method does not guess. Other kinds of key have their own algorithm, so this option does not change them.

doc.returnHtml: A set of at most 16 public keys, each with the name the document gave it. A key is found in it by its kid. The set is never searched by trying every key.

errors.descHtml: { rsaScheme: … } names a kind that is not one of the two RSA kinds. No other kind has two schemes to choose from.

$jwks is not a valid key document. It is not JSON, or it has no keys array. A key has a private field, or a kid that is not a string. A key does not match its kind, such as an RSA modulus outside 2048 to 8192 bits. An alg does not fit its key's kind. Two keys have the same kid. The document has more than 16 keys that can be used. The document is longer than 1 MiB.

classes.summaryHtml: The public keys another service uses to sign its tokens. read reads them from the JWKS document that service publishes. Core\Jwt::verifyIssued then checks a token with the one key its kid names.

classes.name: Core\Ldap
classes.summary: Opens a connection to an LDAP directory, such as Active Directory. The name of a directory in the server's configuration is enough, or the program can give the settings itself.

doc.shortHtml: Whether a connection to a directory is encrypted.
Opens the directory named by an [ldap.<name>] block in nvs.toml. A second call with the same name in one request returns the same connection. Needs the ldap.connect capability for that name.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The block to open: "corp" is [ldap.corp].

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Ldap\Connection, logged in as the block's user. It is closed when the request ends.

errors.descHtml: ldap.connect does not grant $name, or no [ldap.<name>] block has that name.
This core already has the block's pool.max connections open, and none was free within the block's timeout.
No URL in the block responded, or the server did not accept the block's user and password. $kind says why.

members.name: open
members.signature: open({ url: string, user?: tainted string, password?: secret tainted string, tls?: Core\Ldap::Tls, timeout?: Core\Time\Duration, base?: Core\Ldap\Dn|string } $settings): Core\Ldap\Connection

params.name: settings
params.type: { url: string, user?: tainted string, password?: secret tainted string, tls?: Core\Ldap::Tls, timeout?: Core\Time\Duration, base?: Core\Ldap\Dn|string }

doc.shortHtml: Opens a directory at a URL the program gives. Needs the ldap.open capability for the URL's host. The host's address is also checked against the addresses no program may reach, such as private networks.

params.name: settings
params.descHtml: The directory to open and the account to log in with.

shape.descHtml: One ldaps:// or ldap:// URL. It cannot be tainted, because the password is sent to this host.
The account to log in as, as a DN, user@example.test or EXAMPLE\user. Left out, the connection does not log in.
The account's password. An empty password throws before anything is sent. A password with a zero byte (\x00) throws before it is sent.
Tls::Required, the default, encrypts the connection. Tls::None sends everything as plain text, and needs the host in [capabilities.ldap] cleartext.
How long one operation may take. Left out, it is 30 seconds.
The DN a search starts from when it does not give its own base. Text cannot be tainted.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Ldap\Connection. It is closed when the request ends.

errors.descHtml: url is not an ldap:// or ldaps:// URL, ldap.open does not grant its host, or the host's address is one no program may reach.
The server did not respond, the connection is not encrypted and the host may not use plain text, or the server did not accept the user and password. $kind says why.

classes.summaryHtml: Opens a connection to an LDAP directory, such as Active Directory. The name of a directory in the server's configuration is enough, or the program can give the settings itself.

classes.name: Core\Ldap\Ad
classes.summary: Filters that only Active Directory understands: group membership through nested groups, enabled and disabled accounts, and a test of the bits in a flag attribute. Each function returns a `Core\Ldap\Filter`, which you can combine with the filters of that class.

doc.shortHtml: Matches the entries that are members of a group.

params.name: group
params.descHtml: The group's DN. A string cannot be tainted. Build the DN with Core\Ldap\Dn::of when a part of it comes from a user.

params.name: nested
params.descHtml: With true, the filter also matches the members of a group that is itself a member of the group, at any depth. The default is false, which matches only the direct members.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Ldap\Filter.

doc.shortHtml: Matches the entries whose account is not disabled. It tests the bit with the value 2 in userAccountControl, and matches when that bit is not set.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Ldap\Filter. An entry with no userAccountControl, such as a group, also matches. Combine it with a filter on objectClass to find only users.

doc.shortHtml: Matches the entries whose account is disabled. It tests the bit with the value 2 in userAccountControl, and matches when that bit is set.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Ldap\Filter.

doc.shortHtml: Matches the entries where a number attribute has every one of these bits set.

params.name: attribute
params.descHtml: The attribute's name, such as sAMAccountName. It cannot be tainted.

params.name: bits
params.descHtml: The bits to test, as one number, such as 2 | 512.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Ldap\Filter.

errors.descHtml: $attribute is not an attribute name.

doc.shortHtml: Matches the entries where a number attribute has at least one of these bits set.

params.name: attribute
params.descHtml: The attribute's name, such as sAMAccountName. It cannot be tainted.

params.name: bits
params.descHtml: The bits to test, as one number, such as 2 | 512.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Ldap\Filter.

errors.descHtml: $attribute is not an attribute name.

classes.summaryHtml: Filters that only Active Directory understands: group membership through nested groups, enabled and disabled accounts, and a test of the bits in a flag attribute. Each function returns a Core\Ldap\Filter, which you can combine with the filters of that class.

classes.name: Core\Ldap\Ad\AccountFlags
classes.summary: The flags of a user or computer account, read from `userAccountControl`. Each flag is a function that returns a `bool`. `bits` returns the whole number. It includes every bit, also the bits that have no function of their own.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x1: a logon script runs.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x2: the account is disabled, so nobody can log in with it.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x8: the account needs a home directory.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x10: the account is locked out after too many wrong passwords. Active Directory computes this bit. It is read from msDS-User-Account-Control-Computed when the entry has it.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x20: the account may have an empty password.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x80: the password is stored with an encryption that can be reversed.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x100: the account is a local account for a user from another domain.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x200: the account is an ordinary user account.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x800: the account is a trust with another domain.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x1000: the account is a computer that is a domain member.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x2000: the account is a domain controller.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x10000: the password never expires.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x20000: the account is an MNS logon account.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x40000: the user must log in with a smart card.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x80000: a service on this account may act for any user it receives.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x100000: no service may act for this user, even a trusted one.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x200000: Kerberos uses only DES keys for this account.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x400000: Kerberos gives a ticket for this account without first checking the password.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x800000: the password has expired. Active Directory computes this bit. It is read from msDS-User-Account-Control-Computed when the entry has it.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x1000000: a service on this account may act for a user without that user's password.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Checks the bit 0x4000000: the account is a read-only domain controller.
doc.returnHtml: true when the bit is set, and false when it is not.

doc.shortHtml: Returns userAccountControl as the number Active Directory stored, such as 512.
doc.returnHtml: The number, with every bit. It does not include the bits Active Directory computes.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether the user must change the password at the next login. This is true when pwdLastSet is 0. A search that selects userAccountControl also reads pwdLastSet.
doc.returnHtml: true when pwdLastSet is 0, and false when it is not or the entry has no pwdLastSet.
