members.name: search
members.signature: search(Core\Ldap\Filter $filter, { base?: Core\Ldap\Dn|string, scope?: Core\Ldap\Connection::Scope, select?: array<string>, pageSize?: int, sizeLimit?: int, sort?: string, descending?: bool, offset?: int, window?: int, showDeleted?: bool }): Core\Ldap\Entries

doc.shortHtml: Finds the entries that match a filter. The server sends the entries in pages, and the next page is read when a foreach loop reaches it.

params.name: filter
params.descHtml: Which entries to return, such as Filter::equals('sAMAccountName', $login).

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The DN the search starts from, as a Dn or as text. Left out, it is the base of the [ldap] block. Text cannot be tainted.

params.name: scope
params.descHtml: How far below base the search looks. The default is Scope::Subtree.

params.name: select
params.descHtml: The attributes each entry has, such as ['cn', 'mail']. Left out, an entry has every attribute the connection's account can read.

params.name: pageSize
params.descHtml: How many entries the server sends at once. The default is 1000.

params.name: sizeLimit
params.descHtml: The most entries the search may find. The default, 0, is the server's own limit.

params.name: sort
params.descHtml: The attribute the server sorts the entries by, such as cn. Left out, the entries come in the server's own order.

params.name: descending
params.descHtml: true sorts from the largest value to the smallest. It needs sort. The default is false.

params.name: offset
params.descHtml: How many sorted entries the window skips. It needs window. The default is 0.

params.name: window
params.descHtml: How many sorted entries to return, starting after offset. It needs sort. With { sort: 'cn', offset: 20, window: 10 }, the search returns entries 21 to 30. total() then returns how many entries there are in all. The default, 0, returns every entry.

params.name: showDeleted
params.descHtml: true also finds deleted entries. Active Directory keeps a deleted entry for some time, with most of its attributes removed. isDeleted() checks whether an entry is one of them. The account needs the right to read deleted entries. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Ldap\Entries. Use it in a foreach loop to get each Core\Ldap\Entry.

errors.descHtml: A name in select or sort is not an attribute name, a number is out of range, window, offset or descending is given without the option it needs, the search has no base, or the connection is closed.
The server returned an error, such as NoSuchObject for a base that does not exist. A search that finds more entries than sizeLimit throws SizeLimitExceeded in the loop.

doc.shortHtml: Finds the entries that changed since the last call, with Active Directory's DirSync. Store the cookie() of the result, and give it to the next call. That call returns only the entries that changed after it.

params.name: filter
params.descHtml: Which entries to return, such as Filter::equals('objectClass', 'user').

params.name: select
params.descHtml: The attributes to watch, such as ['cn', 'mail']. A changed entry has only the attributes that changed. The attributes filter uses and isDeleted are always watched too. Left out, every attribute is watched.

params.name: cookie
params.descHtml: The cookie() of an earlier result. Left out, the result has every entry that matches filter.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Ldap\Changes. Use it in a foreach loop to get each changed Core\Ldap\Entry. A deleted entry has isDeleted() set to true.

errors.descHtml: A name in select is not an attribute name, there is no base, or the connection is closed.

classes.name: Core\Log
classes.summary: Writes log records. `write` writes one record as one line of JSON, with a level, a message and any extra fields. The server's `[log]` settings decide where records go and which levels are kept.

doc.shortHtml: How serious a log record is. Each of the five cases has the number of its syslog severity, so a syslog target can use it directly. A smaller number is more serious.
Writes one log record. Novis writes its own records about a stopped program in the same format, so every record in the log has the same shape. A log target gets JSON Lines: one JSON object per line.

params.name: level
params.descHtml: How serious the record is. Each case of Core\Log::Level has the number of its syslog severity.

params.name: message
params.descHtml: What happened, as one plain sentence. A tainted value is allowed here, because a log often records input from outside. A secret value does not compile, as in every message a person reads.

params.name: fields
params.descHtml: Extra data about the event. It is written as a fields object next to the message. When it is empty, the record has no fields key. Nothing in fields makes a write fail. A value the log format cannot contain, such as bytes, a callable or a cycle, is written as text that describes it.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. If a record cannot be written, it is lost and not written again. The log is not a place to store the program's data.

classes.summaryHtml: Writes log records. write writes one record as one line of JSON, with a level, a message and any extra fields. The server's [log] settings decide where records go and which levels are kept.

classes.name: Core\Mail
classes.summary: Sends email. `send` gives one message to the mail server that a `[mail.<name>]` block of `nvs.toml` names. The program writes the block's name. The host, the port, the password and the sender address stay in the block.

members.name: send
members.signature: send(string $endpoint, array<string> $to, string $subject, string $text, { cc?: array<string>, bcc?: array<string>, replyTo?: string, html?: string }): void

doc.shortHtml: Sends one message to the SMTP server that [mail.$endpoint] names. It returns when that server has accepted the message.

params.name: endpoint
params.descHtml: The name of the [mail.<name>] block in nvs.toml to send through. A tainted value does not compile here. The name selects a server setting, so you write it in the code and never read it from input.

params.name: to
params.descHtml: The recipients, one address per array entry. It is a list because a comma-separated string can be read in more than one way.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The subject. If it contains characters that a header line cannot contain, it is encoded with RFC 2047. So no subject can add a header. A long subject is split over several header lines, and a mail program joins them again.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The plain-text body. Every message has one.

params.name: cc
params.descHtml: More recipients. Their addresses are shown in the message.

params.name: bcc
params.descHtml: More recipients. Their addresses are not shown in the message. They are sent to the server only, and no header contains them.

params.name: replyTo
params.descHtml: The address that replies go to, when it is not the sender in the settings.

params.name: html
params.descHtml: An HTML version of $text. If you give it, the message is multipart/alternative and both versions are sent.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The mail server accepted the message. Delivery after that is the mail server's job.

errors.descHtml: The capability mail.send does not allow $endpoint. Or no [mail.<name>] block with that name sets host or from. Or the block sets only one of user and password. Or an address is not a valid address. Each of these is a mistake in the settings or the call, not a failed send.

The mail server could not be reached, closed the connection, or rejected a command. In the last case, the message contains the SMTP reply. It is also thrown when a block sets a password and the server cannot receive it safely. That is when the server has no STARTTLS, has no AUTH PLAIN, or has a certificate that does not verify. In all these cases, nothing is sent unencrypted.

classes.summaryHtml: Sends email. send gives one message to the mail server that a [mail.<name>] block of nvs.toml names. The program writes the block's name. The host, the port, the password and the sender address stay in the block.

classes.name: Core\Math
classes.summary: Functions and constants for numbers: rounding, powers, roots, logarithms, angles and limits. A result that does not fit its type throws an `ArithmeticError`, and a value outside a function's range, such as `sqrt(-1.0)`, gives `NaN`.

constants.name: PI
constants.descHtml: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, 3.14159… as the nearest float.

constants.name: TAU
constants.descHtml: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its radius, 2 * PI or 6.28318… as the nearest float. This is a full turn in radians.

constants.name: E
constants.descHtml: Euler's number, the base of the natural logarithm, 2.71828… as the nearest float. It is the default base of log.

constants.name: EPSILON
constants.descHtml: The smallest float that added to 1.0 gives a value other than 1.0, 2.220446049250313e-16. Use it as the tolerance when you compare two floats, in place of ==.

constants.name: INT_MAX
constants.descHtml: The largest int, 9223372036854775807.

constants.name: INT_MIN
constants.descHtml: The smallest int, -9223372036854775808. It is the one value abs cannot return as an int.

constants.name: UINT_MAX
constants.descHtml: The largest uint, 18446744073709551615.

constants.name: FLOAT_MAX
constants.descHtml: The largest finite float, 1.7976931348623157e308. The most negative one is -FLOAT_MAX.

constants.name: FLOAT_MIN
constants.descHtml: The smallest positive normal float, 2.2250738585072014e-308. The most negative float is -FLOAT_MAX.

constants.name: NAN
constants.descHtml: The float that is not a number. It is equal to nothing, itself included, so isNan is the only test for it.

constants.name: INFINITY
constants.descHtml: Positive infinity as a float, larger than every finite value. Negative infinity is -INFINITY, and isFinite is false for both.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $n without its sign, as the same kind of number. -3 gives 3 and -2.5 gives 2.5.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number whose sign is removed: an int, a float or a decimal.

doc.returnHtml: $n without its sign, with the same type as $n. An int gives an int, a uint is returned unchanged, a float gives a float and a decimal gives a decimal with the same decimal places. -0.0 becomes 0.0.

errors.descHtml: When $n is INT_MIN, whose positive value is one past INT_MAX.

doc.shortHtml: Returns -1 when $n is below zero, 1 when it is above zero and 0 when it is zero.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to check: an int, a float or a decimal.

doc.returnHtml: -1, 0 or 1, as an int. -0.0 is zero, so the result for it is 0.

errors.descHtml: When $n is NaN (a value that means "not a number"). NaN is not below, above or equal to zero.
When $n is a uint bigger than Core\Math::INT_MAX.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the smaller of two values. For the smallest value in an array, use Core\Arr::min.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: One value: a number, a string, a bool or null.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The other value, of the same type as $a.

doc.returnHtml: The smaller value. When the two are equal, the result is $a. NaN is smaller than every other float.

errors.descHtml: When the two values cannot be compared: an object, an array, or two values of different kinds.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the larger of two values. For the largest value in an array, use Core\Arr::max.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: One value: a number, a string, a bool or null.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The other value, of the same type as $a.

doc.returnHtml: The larger value. When the two are equal, the result is $a. NaN is smaller than every other float.

errors.descHtml: When the two values cannot be compared: an object, an array, or two values of different kinds.

doc.shortHtml: Keeps $n between $low and $high.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The value to keep in the range. It can be a number, a string, a bool or null.

params.name: low
params.descHtml: The smallest value the result can be.

params.name: high
params.descHtml: The largest value the result can be. It must not be below $low.

doc.returnHtml: $low when $n is below it, $high when $n is above it, and $n itself otherwise. Both ends are inside the range.

errors.descHtml: When $low is above $high. Also when two of the values cannot be compared: an object without compareTo, an array, or a number and a string.

doc.shortHtml: Rounds $n up to the next whole number. For a negative $n, up means toward zero.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to round up.

doc.returnHtml: A whole number, as a float. A $n between -1.0 and 0.0 gives -0.0. NaN and the infinities stay the same.

doc.shortHtml: Rounds $n down to the next whole number. For a negative $n, down means away from zero.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to round down.

doc.returnHtml: A whole number, as a float. A $n between -1.0 and 0.0 gives -1.0. NaN and the infinities stay the same.

doc.shortHtml: Removes the fractional part of $n. The result moves toward zero, so 2.7 gives 2.0 and -2.7 gives -2.0.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number whose fractional part is removed.

doc.returnHtml: A whole number, as a float. A $n between -1.0 and 0.0 gives -0.0. NaN and the infinities stay the same.

members.name: round
members.signature: round(float $n, { precision?: int, mode?: Core\RoundMode }): float

doc.shortHtml: Rounds $n to a number of decimal places. The mode option chooses the result for a value exactly halfway between two results.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to round.

params.name: precision
params.descHtml: How many decimal places to keep. The default is 0, which rounds to a whole number. -2 rounds to hundreds.

params.name: mode
params.descHtml: A Core\RoundMode case. The default is RoundMode::HalfUp, which rounds a half away from zero.

doc.returnHtml: The rounded float. NaN and the infinities are returned unchanged. $n is also returned unchanged when precision is above 22 or below -22, or when $n * 10 ** precision is 2 ** 53 or more.

doc.shortHtml: Divides $a by $b and removes the remainder. The result moves toward zero.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The integer to divide.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The integer to divide by. It may not be zero.

doc.returnHtml: The whole part of $a / $b. intDiv(7, 2) is 3, and intDiv(-7, 2) is -3. The % operator gives the remainder.

errors.descHtml: When $b is zero. Also when $a is Core\Math::INT_MIN and $b is -1, because the result is one more than Core\Math::INT_MAX.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the remainder after dividing $a by $b, for float values. The result has the sign of $a. For whole numbers, use the % operator.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The number to divide.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The number to divide by. It may not be zero.

doc.returnHtml: The remainder. mod(7.5, 2.0) is 1.5, and mod(-7.5, 2.0) is -1.5. When $a is an infinity, the result is NaN. When $b is an infinity, the result is $a.

errors.descHtml: When $b is zero.

doc.shortHtml: Divides $a by $b. When $b is zero, it returns INFINITY, -INFINITY or NaN. The / operator throws an error there.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The number to divide.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The number to divide by. It may be zero.

doc.returnHtml: $a / $b. When $b is zero, the result is INFINITY or -INFINITY. Its sign comes from the signs of both numbers together. When both numbers are zero, the result is NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the greatest common divisor of two integers. This is the largest integer that divides both with no remainder.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The first integer. Its sign does not change the result.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The second integer. Its sign does not change the result.

doc.returnHtml: The greatest common divisor, which is never negative. When one integer is 0, the result is the other one without its sign. When both are 0, the result is 0.

errors.descHtml: When the result does not fit an int. This happens only when one integer is Core\Math::INT_MIN and the other is Core\Math::INT_MIN or 0.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the least common multiple of two integers. This is the smallest positive integer that both divide with no remainder.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The first integer. Its sign does not change the result.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The second integer. Its sign does not change the result.

doc.returnHtml: The least common multiple, which is never negative. When one integer is 0, the result is 0.

errors.descHtml: When the result is bigger than Core\Math::INT_MAX. This happens quickly for two big integers that share no divisor.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the square root of $n.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to take the square root of.

doc.returnHtml: A float that is zero or more. A negative $n gives NaN. -0.0 gives -0.0, and Core\Math::INFINITY gives Core\Math::INFINITY.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the cube root of $n. A negative $n works too, so cbrt(-8.0) is -2.0.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: Any number.

doc.returnHtml: The cube root, with the same sign as $n: Core\Math::cbrt(-8.0) is -2.0. An infinity gives the same infinity, and NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the length of the longest side of a right triangle. $a and $b are the other two sides. The result is sqrt($a * $a + $b * $b), but it stays correct when $a * $a is too big for a float.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The length of one side. Its sign does not change the result.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The length of the other side. Its sign does not change the result.

doc.returnHtml: The length. It is never negative. When $a or $b is INFINITY or -INFINITY, the result is INFINITY, even when the other one is NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns E raised to the power $n. E is about 2.718.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The power to raise E to.

doc.returnHtml: E ** $n, which is never negative. Above about 709.78 the result is INFINITY. Far enough below zero, the result is 0.0. NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the logarithm of $n: the power you raise base to to get $n. The base is E unless you give one.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to take the logarithm of.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The base. It must be greater than zero, and it is E when you leave it out. For a power of 10.0 or 2.0 in that base, the result is exact.

doc.returnHtml: The logarithm. When $n is 0.0 and base is greater than 1.0, the result is -INFINITY. When $n is negative, or base is 1.0, the result is NaN.

errors.descHtml: When base is zero or negative.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the sine of an angle. The angle is in radians.

params.name: radians

members.signature: format(int|float|decimal $n, { decimals?: uint, decimalSeparator?: string, groupSeparator?: string }): string

doc.shortHtml: Writes a number as text for a person to read, with a fixed number of decimals. The digits are not grouped unless you give a groupSeparator.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to write: an int, a float or a decimal.

params.name: decimals
params.descHtml: How many digits to write after the decimal separator, from 0 to 100. The default is 0, which writes no decimal separator.

params.name: decimalSeparator
params.descHtml: The text between the whole part and the decimals. The default is ..

params.name: groupSeparator
params.descHtml: The text between each group of three digits, counted from the right. The default is empty, so the digits are not grouped.

doc.returnHtml: The text. The number is rounded to decimals places, and a half is rounded away from zero. A negative number starts with -. A number that rounds to zero has no -.

errors.descHtml: When $n is INFINITY, -INFINITY or NaN, or when decimals is more than 100.
When $n is a uint larger than Core\Math::INT_MAX.

classes.summaryHtml:
Functions and constants for numbers: rounding, powers, roots, logarithms, angles and limits. A result that does not fit its type throws an ArithmeticError, and a value outside a function's range, such as sqrt(-1.0), gives NaN.

Core\Math is the numeric function set; the arithmetic operators + - * / % ** and <=> are the language's and have no member here. abs, sign, min, max and clamp take an int, a float or a decimal and answer in the argument's own type; the rounding, root, exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric members take and answer float; intDiv, gcd, lcm, toBase and fromBase work over int. round names its tie rule as a Core\RoundMode case and defaults to HalfUp — and answers a float, so round(6.0, { decimals: 2 }) prints 6; a number shown with a fixed count of decimals is format's job, not round's. format groups digits only when asked, since there is no locale. A refusal throws — fromBase on a digit outside the base, format on an infinity — never answers false. The constants are class constants: Core\Math::PI, INT_MAX, EPSILON, NAN, INFINITY.

<?nvs
echo Core\Math::abs(-7), ' ', Core\Math::abs(-2.5), ' ', Core\Math::sign(-3), "\n";
echo Core\Math::max(3, 9), ' ', Core\Math::clamp(15, 0, 10), "\n";
echo Core\Math::round(2.5), ' ', Core\Math::round(1.2345, { precision: 2 }), ' ',
     Core\Math::round(2.5, { mode: Core\RoundMode::HalfEven }), "\n";
echo Core\Math::floor(1.8), ' ', Core\Math::ceil(1.2), ' ', Core\Math::truncate(-1.7), "\n";
echo Core\Math::intDiv(7, 2), ' ', 7 % 2, ' ', Core\Math::mod(7.5, 2.0), "\n";
echo Core\Math::sqrt(16.0), ' ', Core\Math::hypot(3.0, 4.0), ' ', Core\Math::log(100.0, { base: 10.0 }), "\n";
echo Core\Math::round(Core\Math::sin(Core\Math::PI / 2), { precision: 3 }), ' ', Core\Math::toDegrees(Core\Math::PI), "\n";
echo Core\Math::toBase(255, 16), ' ', Core\Math::fromBase('ff', 16), ' ', Core\Math::toBase(5, 2), "\n";
echo Core\Math::format(1234567.891, { decimals: 2, groupSeparator: ',' }), "\n";
echo Core\Math::gcd(12, 18), ' ', Core\Math::lcm(4, 6), "\n";
echo Core\Math::isNan(Core\Math::NAN) ? 'nan' : 'number', ' ', Core\Math::INT_MAX, "\n";
7 2.5 -1
9 10
3 1.23 2
1 2 -1
3 1 1.5
4 5 2
1 180
ff 255 101
1,234,567.89
6 12
nan 9223372036854775807

classes.name: Core\Metrics
classes.summary: Counts and measures what your program does, for a monitoring system to collect. `increment` adds to a counter, `observe` records a measurement and `gauge` sets a level. A program cannot read the values back.

members.name: increment
members.signature: increment(string $name, { by?: uint, labels?: array<string> }): void

doc.shortHtml: Adds to a counter. The first call with $name makes that name a counter, and it stays a counter.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The series name, [a-z][a-z0-9_]*. A name written directly in the code that does not match this pattern does not compile. A tainted name does not compile either.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: How much to add. The default is 1. It cannot be negative, because a counter that goes down looks like a restart of the process.

params.name: labels
params.descHtml: The label values of this series, with the label name as the key. A tainted or secret value is not allowed. Use an enum case, a value converted with as, or a route name.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A program cannot read a metric back. Only the monitoring system that collects the metrics can read them.

errors.descHtml: The name is already a different kind of metric, or it already has other label names. The message shows the first call and this one. A new series above the max_series limit is not an error. Novis does not record it and counts it, and the call returns normally.

doc.shortHtml: Records one measurement in a histogram, such as a duration or a size. The first call with $name makes that name a histogram, and it stays a histogram.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The series name, [a-z][a-z0-9_]*. A name written directly in the code that does not match this pattern does not compile. A tainted name does not compile either.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The measurement, in the unit of the series. Use seconds for a name that ends in _seconds, and bytes for a name that ends in _bytes.

params.name: labels
params.descHtml: The label values of this series, with the label name as the key. A tainted or secret value is not allowed. Use an enum case, a value converted with as, or a route name.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A program cannot read a metric back, the same as with increment.

errors.descHtml: The name is already a different kind of metric, or it already has other label names. The message shows the first call and this one. A new series above the max_series limit is not an error. Novis does not record it and counts it, and the call returns normally.

doc.shortHtml: Sets a gauge to $value. A gauge is a level that goes up and down, such as the number of items waiting. The first call with $name makes that name a gauge.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The series name, [a-z][a-z0-9_]*. A name written directly in the code that does not match this pattern does not compile. A tainted name does not compile either.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The new value of the gauge. The monitoring system sees the last value set before it collects.

params.name: labels
params.descHtml: The label values of this series, with the label name as the key. A tainted or secret value is not allowed. Use an enum case, a value converted with as, or a route name.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A program cannot read a metric back, the same as with increment.

errors.descHtml: The name is already a different kind of metric, or it already has other label names. The message shows the first call and this one. A new series above the max_series limit is not an error. Novis does not record it and counts it, and the call returns normally.

classes.name: Core\Mime
classes.summary: Finds out what kind of file some bytes are, such as a PNG image or a PDF, by reading the first bytes. `detect` returns a `Core\Mime::Type` case, and `mediaType` gives its name, such as `image/png`.

doc.shortHtml: The kind of file that Core\Mime::detect found in some bytes. The list of cases is fixed, so your program compares the result with a case. Every text format gives Unknown.
Returns the type of $data, read from the bytes themselves. There is no parameter for a file name, because an attacker can choose a file name's extension.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The bytes to check. Only the first 16 bytes or fewer are read. So the start of an upload gives the same result as the whole upload.

doc.returnHtml: The case for the kind of file. It is Core\Mime::Type::Unknown when no format matches, and for every text format. The result does not make the data safe. Bytes detected as image/png are still tainted, because only the first bytes were checked.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the IANA media type of $type, for a Content-Type header or a stored record. There is no method that turns a media type back into a case.

params.name: type
params.descHtml: The case to convert, usually one that detect returned.

doc.returnHtml: The media type as a string, such as image/png. For Core\Mime::Type::Unknown it is application/octet-stream, the usual type for bytes of an unknown kind.

classes.summaryHtml: Finds out what kind of file some bytes are, such as a PNG image or a PDF, by reading the first bytes. detect returns a Core\Mime::Type case, and mediaType gives its name, such as image/png.

classes.name: Core\Net
classes.summary: Opens network sockets. `connect` and `listen` open a TCP connection or a TCP listener, `bindDatagram` opens a UDP socket, and `connectLocal` and `listenLocal` do the same over a Unix-domain socket path. Each one needs a grant in the configuration.

doc.shortHtml: Opens a TCP connection to $host on $port. While the connection opens, other work keeps running. The configuration must allow the host in net.connect. The address of the host must not be in a range that the address policy denies.

params.name: host
params.descHtml: A host name or an IP address. It is checked against net.connect before its address is looked up. The connection goes to the one address that is found.

params.name: port
params.descHtml: The port to connect to, 1 to 65535.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long opening the connection may take. This limit ends when the connection is open. A later read uses the time limit that you give to that read.

doc.returnHtml: An open Core\Net\Stream. If your program does not close it, it is closed when the request ends.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not allow this host in net.connect. It is also thrown when the host has no address, or its address is in a denied range. It is also thrown when $port is not a valid port, or $within is not a positive length of time.
The connection was not open yet when the time in $within ended.
The connection failed. The other side refused it, it could not be reached, or it was reset while it opened.

doc.shortHtml: Opens a TCP socket that listens on $address and $port. The configuration must allow this exact address and port in net.listen. The address policy of net.connect does not apply, because its rules are for the hosts you connect to.

params.name: address
params.descHtml: An IP address, such as 127.0.0.1, ::1 or 0.0.0.0. A host name is not allowed. The grant names one address and port, and a host name can have two addresses.

params.name: port
params.descHtml: The port to listen on. With 0, the operating system chooses a port, and Core\Net\Listener::port returns it.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Net\Listener that listens. If your program does not close it, it is closed when the request ends.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not allow this address and port in net.listen. It is also thrown when $address is not an IP address, or $port is not a valid port.
The operating system did not allow the socket. The port is already in use, or the address does not belong to this host.

doc.shortHtml: Opens a UDP socket on $address and $port. Like a TCP listener, it needs this exact address and port in net.listen. Sending to another host needs a separate grant, which Core\Net\Datagram::send checks.

params.name: address
params.descHtml: An IP address, such as 127.0.0.1, ::1 or 0.0.0.0. A host name is not allowed, for the same reason as in Core\Net::listen: the grant names one address and port.

params.name: port
params.descHtml: The port to use. With 0, the operating system chooses a port, and Core\Net\Datagram::port returns it.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Net\Datagram on that address and port. If your program does not close it, it is closed when the request ends.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not allow this address and port in net.listen. It is also thrown when $address is not an IP address, or $port is not a valid port.
The operating system did not allow the socket. The port is already in use, or the address does not belong to this host.

doc.shortHtml: Connects to the Unix-domain socket at $path. While the connection opens, other work keeps running. The configuration must allow the path in net.local, which is a separate grant. net.connect never allows a path, because it has no rules for paths.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The absolute path of a socket that listens. It is never read as a host or as a URL. This is the only method that connects to a path.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long to wait for the connection. This limit is for this call only. A local connection waits only when the listener's queue of waiting connections is full.

doc.returnHtml: A connected Core\Net\Stream. If your program does not close it, it is closed when the request ends.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not allow this path in net.local. It is also thrown when this build has no support for Unix-domain sockets, or $within is not a positive length of time.
The connection was not open yet when the time in $within ended.
The operating system did not allow the path. Nothing listens there, the program has no permission, or the path is too long for the platform.

doc.shortHtml: Creates a Unix-domain socket at $path and listens on it. The configuration must allow the path in net.local. Listening needs this grant too, because any program on this host that finds the socket can connect to it.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The absolute path where the socket is created. Nothing may exist at this path yet. The path is not deleted when the socket closes, because something else may be there by then.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Net\Listener that listens. If your program does not close it, it is closed when the request ends. Its port() method throws an error, because a socket at a path has no port.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not allow this path in net.local, or this build has no support for Unix-domain sockets.
The operating system did not allow the path. Something already exists at the path, its folder does not exist, or the program has no permission to create it.

classes.summaryHtml: Opens network sockets. connect and listen open a TCP connection or a TCP listener, bindDatagram opens a UDP socket, and connectLocal and listenLocal do the same over a Unix-domain socket path. Each one needs a grant in the configuration.

classes.name: Core\Net\Datagram
classes.summary: A UDP socket, returned by `Core\Net::bindDatagram`. `send` sends one message to an address, and `receive` waits for one message and returns it as a `Core\Net\Datagram\Message`.

doc.shortHtml: Sends one message to $host on $port, and returns how many bytes were sent. The configuration must allow the host in net.connect. The address of the host must not be in a range that the address policy denies. These are the same checks as for a TCP connection.

params.name: host
params.descHtml: A host name or an IP address. It is checked against net.connect before its address is looked up. The message goes to the one address that is found.

params.name: port
params.descHtml: The port to send to, 1 to 65535.

params.name: payload
params.descHtml: The bytes of one message. A message is never sent in parts. A message that is too large for the network throws an error and is not split.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long to wait until the socket accepts the message. This limit is for this call only.

doc.returnHtml: How many bytes were sent. When the call succeeds, this is always the length of $payload.

errors.descHtml: The configuration does not allow this host in net.connect. It is also thrown when the host has no address, or its address is in a denied range. It is also thrown when $port is not a valid port, this handle is closed, or $within is not a positive length of time.
The socket did not accept the message within $within.
The operating system did not allow the send. The message is larger than the maximum size, or the network cannot be reached.

doc.shortHtml: Waits for one message, no longer than $within. It returns the message and the address that sent it. It needs no grant, because net.listen was checked when this socket was opened. Your program does not choose who sends to it.

params.name: max
params.descHtml: How many bytes to keep. The limit is 64 KiB, because no message is larger. A message arrives whole or not at all. If it is longer than $max, only the first $max bytes are kept, and the rest is lost. No later call returns the rest.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long to wait for a message. This limit is for this call only.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Net\Datagram\Message with the bytes, and the address and port they came from.

errors.descHtml: This handle is closed, or $within is not a positive length of time.
No datagram arrived within $within.
The operating system could not receive. On Windows, this error also reports that an earlier send from this socket could not reach its address.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the port this socket uses. If your program asked for port 0, this is the port that the operating system chose.
doc.returnHtml: The port, from 1 to 65535.

errors.descHtml: This handle is closed.
The operating system did not return the port of this socket.

doc.shortHtml: Closes this socket, and frees its port and the resources it uses. When a request ends, it closes every socket that it opened and did not close.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing.

errors.descHtml: This handle is already closed.

classes.summaryHtml: A UDP socket, returned by Core\Net::bindDatagram. send sends one message to an address, and receive waits for one message and returns it as a Core\Net\Datagram\Message.

classes.name: Core\Net\Datagram\Message
classes.summary: One message that `Core\Net\Datagram::receive` returned. `payload` gives its bytes, and `host` and `port` give the address it came from, which is where a reply goes.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the bytes of this message, as tainted bytes. If the message was longer than the $max of receive(), only the first $max bytes are here.
doc.returnHtml: The bytes that arrived. They can be empty, because a message with no bytes is still a message.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the IP address that sent this message, such as 127.0.0.1 or ::1. It is a plain string, so you can pass it to send() to reply. send() checks the grant and the address policy for it, the same as for any other address.
doc.returnHtml: An IP address, never a host name, because the address is not looked up in reverse.

doc.shortHtml: The port this datagram came from, which is where a reply goes.
doc.returnHtml: The sender's port, 1 to 65535.

classes.summaryHtml: One message that Core\Net\Datagram::receive returned. payload gives its bytes, and host and port give the address it came from, which is where a reply goes.

classes.name: Core\Net\Listener
classes.summary: A TCP server socket, returned by `Core\Net::listen` and `Core\Net::listenLocal`. `accept` waits for the next client and returns a `Core\Net\Stream` for it.

doc.shortHtml: Waits for the next client to connect, for no longer than $within, and returns a Core\Net\Stream for that client. It needs no setting of its own: nvs.toml was checked when Core\Net::listen opened this socket.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long to wait for a client. It is the limit for this call only.

doc.returnHtml: The connection to the client. The request closes it when it ends, if the program has not closed it before.

errors.descHtml: This handle is closed, or $within is not a positive length of time.
No connection arrived within $within.
The operating system failed the accept.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the port this listener uses. If your program asked for port 0, this is the port that the operating system chose.
doc.returnHtml: The port, from 1 to 65535.

errors.descHtml: This handle is closed, or Core\Net::listenLocal opened this listener at a path. Such a listener has no port.
The operating system did not return the port of this socket.

doc.shortHtml: Stops listening and frees the port. Connections that were already accepted stay open, because each one is a separate socket.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing.

errors.descHtml: This handle is already closed.

classes.summaryHtml: A TCP server socket, returned by Core\Net::listen and Core\Net::listenLocal. accept waits for the next client and returns a Core\Net\Stream for it.

classes.name: Core\Net\Stream
classes.summary: A connection to one client or server, returned by `Core\Net::connect`, `Core\Net::connectLocal` and `Core\Net\Listener::accept`. `read` and `write` move bytes, and each waits no longer than its `$within`.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the bytes that have arrived, up to $max bytes. It waits no longer than $within. Fewer bytes than $max is normal and not an error, because a socket returns only what has arrived.

params.name: max
params.descHtml: The largest number of bytes to return. When $max is very large, one read returns fewer bytes, because the buffer has a smaller limit.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long to wait for the first byte. This limit is for this call only.

doc.returnHtml: The bytes that arrived, as tainted bytes. When the other side has closed its half of the connection, the result is an empty bytes. This is how you see the end of the stream.

errors.descHtml: This handle is closed, or $within is not a positive length of time.
Nothing arrived within $within.
The connection failed. The other side reset it, or the network lost it.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $payload to the other side, and waits no longer than $within. It returns how many bytes the socket accepted. The socket may accept only some of the bytes. This is normal, and your program then sends the rest.

params.name: payload
params.descHtml: The bytes to send.

params.name: within
params.descHtml: How long to wait until the socket accepts bytes. This limit is for this call only.

doc.returnHtml: How many bytes of $payload were written. It is between 0 and the length of $payload.

errors.descHtml: This handle is closed, or $within is not a positive length of time.
The socket accepted nothing within $within.
The connection failed. The other side reset it, or closed its half for reading.

doc.shortHtml: Closes this connection and frees the resources it uses. When a request ends, it closes every socket that it opened and did not close.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing.

errors.descHtml: This handle is already closed.

classes.summaryHtml: A connection to one client or server, returned by Core\Net::connect, Core\Net::connectLocal and Core\Net\Listener::accept. read and write move bytes, and each waits no longer than its $within.

params.name: options
params.type: ?{ autoOrient?: bool, toSrgb?: bool, maxPixels?: uint, page?: uint, dpi?: float }

doc.shortHtml: Image::open starts from the bytes of an encoded image. It turns the image upright and converts its colours to sRGB, unless autoOrient or toSrgb is false. page chooses one page of a document, starting at 1. dpi is the resolution of that page, 150 by default. An image with one page has only page 1, and a page past the end throws an error. Bytes that are not an image throw an error when encode, variants or raw runs.
Image::create starts from a blank canvas. Without $fill, the canvas is transparent.
Image::fromRaw starts from RGBA8 pixels, as raw returns them.
Image::info reads the format, the size and the orientation from the header. No pixel is decoded.
Image::mime returns the MIME type of a format, for example image/webp.
Image::extension returns the file extension of a format, without the dot, for example jpg.

resize scales the image. With only width or only height, the image keeps its proportions. With both, fit decides how the image fills that size. The default is Fit::Cover. The image does not grow larger than it is, unless upscale is true.

members.name: crop
members.signature: crop({ x: uint, y: uint, width: uint, height: uint } $box): Image

params.name: box
params.type: { x: uint, y: uint, width: uint, height: uint }

doc.shortHtml: crop keeps only the box at x and y, with its width and height. The box must lie inside the image.
trim removes the border that has the colour of the top-left pixel. threshold is how far a colour may differ and still count, from 0 to 255. The default is 10.
rotate turns the image clockwise by $degrees. For an angle that is not a multiple of 90, the image grows to fit the turned picture, and background fills the corners.
flip(Axis::Horizontal) swaps left and right. flip(Axis::Vertical) swaps top and bottom.

members.name: composite
members.signature: composite(Image $overlay, ?{ gravity?: Gravity, x?: int, y?: int, opacity?: float, blend?: Blend } $options = null): Image

params.name: options
params.type: ?{ gravity?: Gravity, x?: int, y?: int, opacity?: float, blend?: Blend }

doc.shortHtml: composite draws $overlay on top of this image, with all of the overlay's own steps. gravity places it, and the default is Gravity::Center. x and y place its top-left corner in pixels instead, and may be negative. The parts outside this image are cut off. opacity is from 0.0 to 1.0, and the default is 1.0. blend mixes the colours, and the default is Blend::Normal. A format or metadata step of the overlay changes nothing.
flatten puts the image on a background of one colour. The result has no transparent pixels.
sharpen makes edges clearer. A larger sigma sharpens wider edges. The default is 1.
blur makes the image soft. A larger $sigma gives a stronger blur.
grayscale removes the colours and keeps the light and dark of each pixel.
brightness multiplies every colour by $amount. 1.0 changes nothing, and 1.2 is 20% brighter.
contrast moves every colour away from middle gray by $amount. 1.0 changes nothing. A value below 1.0 gives less contrast.
gamma changes the middle tones and keeps black and white. 1.0 changes nothing. A value above 1.0 makes the middle tones lighter.
tint colours the image with $color. The alpha of $color is how strong the tint is.

members.name: text
members.signature: text(string $text, Font $font, { size: float, color: Color, gravity?: Gravity, x?: int, y?: int, maxWidth?: uint, align?: Align } $options): Image

params.name: options
params.type: { size: float, color: Color, gravity?: Gravity, x?: int, y?: int, maxWidth?: uint, align?: Align }

doc.shortHtml: text draws $text on the image with $font, in color. size is the font size in pixels. x and y place the top-left corner of the text. Without them, gravity places it, and the default is Gravity::Center. With maxWidth, lines break at spaces to stay that wide. align sets how the lines line up, and the default is Align::Left. Text in any script is drawn as the font defines it. A line of Arabic or Hebrew runs from right to left.

doc.shortHtml: Image::measureText returns the width and height in pixels that text needs for the same text and options.

members.signature: format(Format $format, ?{ quality?: uint, progressive?: bool, lossless?: bool, effort?: uint } $options = null): Image

params.name: options
params.type: ?{ quality?: uint, progressive?: bool, lossless?: bool, effort?: uint }

doc.shortHtml: format sets the format that encode writes. Without it, the output has the format of the input.
metadata({ keep: true }) keeps the EXIF data in the output. Without it, encode removes all metadata.
encode runs every step and returns the encoded file.
raw runs every step and returns the pixels as RGBA8 rows, four bytes per pixel.
variants decodes the image once and returns one encoded file per entry, in the same order. An entry may resize the image and choose its own format and quality.

members.name: compare
members.signature: compare(bytes|Image $a, bytes|Image $b, ?{ tolerance?: uint, render?: bool } $options = null): Diff

doc.shortHtml: Image::compare compares two images of the same size and returns a Diff. Other sizes throw a LogicError. A pixel differs when its delta is above tolerance, which is 0 by default.
Image::hash returns a short hash of an encoded image. Two similar images have similar hashes. Each HashKind returns a hash of its own fixed length.
Image::hashDistance returns how many bits differ between two hashes. A small number means similar images. Two hashes of different lengths throw a LogicError.
Image::placeholder returns a short text that a web page can draw as a blurred preview of the image. Its average colour is the average colour of the image.
Image::palette returns at most count main colours of the image, the most common first. Transparent pixels are not counted. A count above 256 throws a LogicError.

classes.summaryHtml:
An image and a list of steps to run on it. Each step method returns a new Image and leaves this one as it was. Nothing is decoded until encode, variants or raw runs.

Novis\Image\Image is an image and a list of steps to run on it. Each step method, such as resize, crop or format, returns a new Image and does not change the old one. No pixel is decoded until encode, variants or raw runs the steps, so bytes that are not an image throw a ParseError only then. encode removes all metadata, such as the place a photo was taken, unless metadata({ keep: true }) is a step.

<?nvs
use Novis\Image\Format;
use Novis\Image\Image;

// A PNG of 3 by 2 pixels, written as hex.
bytes $png = Core\Encoding::fromHex(
    '89504e470d0a1a0a0000000d49484452000000030000000208060000009d74661a'
        . '0000000b49444154789c6360c00500001a0001bc3ce0410000000049454e44ae426082',
);

Image $photo = Image::open($png);
bytes $thumb = $photo->resize({ width: 6, upscale: true })->format(Format::Jpeg, { quality: 80 })->encode();

var $info = Image::info($thumb);
echo Image::mime($info->format), ' ', $info->width, 'x', $info->height, "\n";
image/jpeg 6x4

classes.name: Novis\Pdf\Document
classes.summary:
An HTML document to render as a PDF file, with the images, stylesheets and fonts it uses.
Each method returns a new `Document` and leaves this one as it was.

doc.shortHtml: A PDF standard the file follows. PdfA2b and PdfA3b are for archiving, and PdfUa1 is for screen readers.
Document::fromHtml starts a document from its HTML. The HTML may name assets, such as <img src="logo.png">. Add each one with asset.
asset adds a file the HTML names, such as an image or a stylesheet. A render reads only these files and data: URIs. Any other name throws a LogicError.
standard sets the PDF standard the file follows.
invoiceXml attaches the XML of an electronic invoice to the file. It needs the standard Document::Standard::PdfA3b. With any other standard, render throws a LogicError.
password encrypts the file. A reader needs the password to open it. A PDF/A standard does not allow a password, so render then throws a LogicError.
created sets the creation time in the file. Without it, the file has no creation time.

members.name: header
members.signature: header(callable(Page): Core\Html\Markup $fn, ?{ height?: string } $options = null): Document

doc.shortHtml: header sets a function that returns the header of each page. render calls it once for each page. The header is drawn in the top margin. height sets that margin, such as "2cm". Without it, the margin is the one @page gives.

members.name: footer
members.signature: footer(callable(Page): Core\Html\Markup $fn, ?{ height?: string } $options = null): Document

doc.shortHtml: footer sets a function that returns the footer of each page. It works like header, in the bottom margin.

slots sets a function that fills each <slot name="..."> in a table row. render calls it once for each page. It returns the HTML for each slot name. Nothing on the page moves, and HTML too tall for its cell is listed in Rendered::overflows.
render returns the PDF file and its pages. Two renders of the same document give the same bytes.

classes.summaryHtml:
An HTML document to render as a PDF file, with the images, stylesheets and fonts it uses. Each method returns a new Document and leaves this one as it was.

Novis\Pdf\Document is an HTML document that render turns into a PDF file. Each method returns a new Document and does not change the old one. The render reads only the files you add with asset and data: URIs, so a name that is not an asset throws a LogicError. render returns a Rendered with the file, its page count, and the CSS it could not draw.

<?nvs
use Novis\Pdf\Document;
use Novis\Pdf\Page;

// The logo is a file that the HTML names. `asset` adds it to the document.
bytes $logo = "<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"40\" height=\"20\"><rect width=\"40\" height=\"20\"/></svg>" as bytes;
string $html = "<html lang=\"en\"><head><title>Invoice 1042</title></head><body>"
    . "<img src=\"logo.svg\" alt=\"Shop\"><h1>Invoice 1042</h1><p>Tea: 2.50 EUR</p></body></html>";

// The footer is a function. The render calls it once for each page.
var $rendered = Document::fromHtml($html)
    ->asset('logo.svg', $logo)
    ->footer(fn(Page $page): Core\Html\Markup => html`<p>Page {$page->number} of {$page->count}</p>`)
    ->render();

echo Core\Bytes::startsWith($rendered->bytes, '%PDF-' as bytes) ? 'a PDF file' : 'not a PDF file', "\n";
echo $rendered->pageCount, " page\n";
a PDF file
1 page

classes.name: Novis\Pdf\Page
classes.summary: One page of a document. `Document::render` calls a header or footer function once for each page, with that page's `Page`.

types.name: Named
types.type: { name: string, value: string }

doc.shortHtml: new Page makes a page from its values. Document::render makes one for you. marks has the data-mark values of every page of the document, one list for each page.
isFirst returns true on the first page.
isLast returns true on the last page.
string returns the value that CSS string-set gives $name on this page. The name must have the same case as in the CSS. If no value is set yet, the result is null.
marks returns the values of every data-mark="name:value" on this page with this name. An element may have several marks, separated by ;.
marksUpTo returns the values of the marks with this name on this page and every page before it. A carried-forward total adds these values up.

doc.shortHtml: Pages::of chooses pages of a PDF file, in the order of $pages. Pages count from 1. Without $pages, every page is chosen. A page listed twice is used twice, and a page not listed is left out.

Pages::merge returns one PDF file with the chosen pages of each part, in order. A page number past the end of its file throws a LogicError. A file that is encrypted or does not parse throws a ParseError.

doc.shortHtml: new Chart makes a chart from its values. Chart::column and the other types make one for you. combined has the types and series that combine added.

Chart::column starts a chart of vertical bars. title is the chart's title. xTitle and yTitle are the titles of its axes. legend is 'right', 'top', 'bottom', 'left' or 'hidden'. labels shows each value on the chart.
Chart::bar starts a chart of horizontal bars. It takes the same options as Chart::column.
Chart::line starts a chart that joins the values of each series with a line. It takes the same options as Chart::column.
Chart::area starts a line chart with the space under each line filled. It takes the same options as Chart::column.
Chart::pie starts a pie chart. Each value of the first series is one slice. It takes the same options as Chart::column.
Chart::doughnut starts a pie chart with a hole in the middle. It takes the same options as Chart::column.
Chart::scatter starts a chart of points. A series' categories are the x values of its points. It takes the same options as Chart::column.

series returns the chart with one more series. $values is a range, such as $sheet->column('sales'). categories is the range of the labels under the values. name is the series' name in the legend. color is a color such as '#1F77B4'.

combine returns the chart with the type and the series of $other drawn on the same axes. You can combine two of column, line and area, such as columns of sales with a line of costs. The title and the legend come from this chart.

doc.shortHtml: Reader::open opens the spreadsheet in $source, the bytes of the file or a file your program opened. Other bytes throw a ParseError. A CSV file is UTF-8 text, or UTF-16 text with a byte order mark. csv sets its separator, quote, escape and encoding.
sheets returns each sheet in tab order, with its name, its position from 0, whether it is hidden, its size and its kind.
macros returns the names of the macro modules in an xlsm or xls file. The list is empty when the file has no macros. Reading a file never runs its macros.

merged returns the merged cells of the sheet $sheet, by name or by position from 0. Each one is a range such as "A1:C2". When you read rows, the value of a merged range is in its top-left cell. With merged: 'fill', every cell of the range has that value.
links returns the hyperlinks of the sheet $sheet. anchor is the cell, such as "B2", and target is where the link goes. external is true for a URL or a file. Reading a file never opens its links.
notes returns the notes of the sheet $sheet. Each one has its cell in noted, its text in note, and its author.
names returns the defined names of the workbook. reference is the text of the name, such as "Shop!$A$1:$C$9". sheet is null for a name the whole workbook can use.
tables returns the Excel tables of the sheet $sheet. table is the range, such as "A1:C10", and name is the table name.

evaluate computes every formula in the workbook. After it, rows gives each formula cell its computed result. It returns the cells it could not compute, and each one keeps the result saved in the file. kind is 'function', 'reference', 'circular' or 'token'.

images returns the pictures of the sheet $sheet. at is the top-left cell, and image is the bytes of the picture. A linked picture has empty image bytes, and link is its target. Reading a file never fetches a link.
properties returns the title, subject, author, company and keywords of the workbook, and the time it was created. A property the file does not have is null, and every property of a CSV file is null.

rows reads the sheet $sheet, by name or by position from 0, and gives one Row at a time. With header: true, the keys are the header cells. text: ["Zip"] reads the column Zip as the text Excel shows, so 1234 with the format 00000 is "01234". text: true reads every column this way.

The other methods add merged cells, links, notes, tables and more. They can use any row you already added.

members.signature: constructor(uint $index, Writer $writer, callable(uint, array<mixed>, RowOptions): void $add, callable(uint, ?uint, bool): void $ready, callable(bytes): void $send, callable(uint, string): uint $position, callable(uint, uint): string $columnRange): void

doc.shortHtml: new Sheet makes a sheet of a workbook. Workbook::sheet makes one for you. $add adds a row. $ready sends the rows that wait, checks that the sheet is open, and with true last checks for a data row. $position returns the column of a key.

add adds one row to the end of the sheet. A value goes to the column of its key, or by position from column A. height is the row height in points. hidden hides the row. level puts it in an outline group. style is its Style.
addAll adds each row of $rows in order, as add does. $rows can be an array or a generator, so a long list of rows does not have to be in memory.

cell returns the address of the column $key in row $row, such as 'C7'. $key is a column key or an upper-case column letter, such as 'qty' or 'C'. A key needs the columns option or a row with keys first.

column returns the cells of the column $key in the rows added so far, such as 'C2:C1043'. The header row is not in the range. Call it after the last row to get every row. Before the first data row, it throws a LogicError.
merge joins the cells of $range, such as 'A1:C1', into one cell.

members.name: link
members.signature: link(string $cell, string $target, ?{ text?: string, tooltip?: string } $options = null): Sheet

doc.shortHtml: link makes the cell $cell a link to $target. The target is an http: or https: address, a mailto: address, or a cell such as 'Totals!A1'. text is the text the cell shows. tooltip is the text a person sees over the link.

members.name: note
members.signature: note(string $cell, string $text, ?{ author?: string } $options = null): Sheet

doc.shortHtml: note adds the note $text to the cell $cell. author is the name the note shows.

validate checks what a person types into $range in Excel. Give one of list, whole, decimal, date, length or formula. min and max are the limits of a number, a date or a length. input is a message Excel shows, and error the message for a wrong value.

group puts the rows $rows, such as '5:9', or the columns, such as 'B:D', in an outline group. Add a group of rows before its rows, and a group of columns before the first row. collapsed hides the group.

table makes the cells of $range, such as 'A1:C9', an Excel table. Its first row is the header row. totals adds a row after the table. It maps a header to 'sum', 'average', 'count', 'min', 'max' or a Formula.

conditional adds one conditional format to $range. kind is 'cell', 'formula', 'colorScale', 'dataBar', 'iconSet', 'top', 'bottom', 'duplicates' or 'unique'. values are Excel formula text, so a text value has quotes, such as '"open"'. style is the Style of the cells the rule matches.

members.name: image
members.signature: image(string $cell, bytes $data, ?{ width?: float, height?: float, offsetX?: float, offsetY?: float } $options = null): Sheet

params.name: options
params.type: ?{ width?: float, height?: float, offsetX?: float, offsetY?: float }

doc.shortHtml: image puts the PNG, JPEG or GIF image $data at the cell $cell. Any other format, or a file that is cut short, throws a LogicError. width and height are in pixels. offsetX and offsetY move the image from the corner of the cell. An image that ends after column XFD or row 1,048,576 throws.

members.name: chart
members.signature: chart(string $cell, Chart $chart, ?{ width?: float, height?: float } $options = null): Sheet

doc.shortHtml: chart puts $chart at the cell $cell. width and height are in pixels. The chart is 480 by 288 pixels if you do not set them. A series range from column grows with the sheet, so a chart you add before the last row still shows every row.

print sets how the sheet is printed. orientation is 'portrait' or 'landscape'. fitToPage sets the number of pages wide and tall. repeatRows, such as '1:1', prints those rows on every page. area is the range to print. Set fitToPage before the first row. A second print throws a LogicError.

members.name: protect
members.signature: protect(?{ password?: string, allow?: array<string> } $options = null): Sheet

doc.shortHtml: protect locks the layout of the sheet, so a person cannot change it in Excel. It is not a security feature: any tool can remove the password. allow names what a person can still do, such as 'sort' or 'autoFilter'.

A workbook designed in Excel, with placeholders such as `{{customer.name}}` in its cells. Open one with `Template::open`.
`fill` puts your data in the placeholders. A row with a list placeholder, such as `{{items.qty}}`, is written once for each item.

doc.shortHtml: Template::open opens the template in $source, the bytes of an xlsx or xlsm file or a file your program opened. The filled file copies the formulas, links and sheets of the template without any change. For this reason, $source cannot be tainted, such as an uploaded file. To fill an uploaded template, call Core\Taint::assertTrusted on its bytes first, with the reason you trust it. zone is the time zone for an Instant, such as 'Europe/Berlin'. Without zone, an Instant throws an error.
set puts $value in the cell at $address, such as 'Summary!B2'. Call it before fill.

fill puts the value at each placeholder's path in $data into its cell. A placeholder that $data does not have throws an error. The keys 'customer.name' and 'customer' => ['name' => …] give the same placeholder. If $data has both, fill throws an error. A list in $data is an array or an Iterator, such as a generator. The items of an Iterator are read while the file is written. The file is written when you call download, save, to or bytes on the result.

Each `create` method sets where the file goes. Add a sheet with `sheet`, add its rows, and call `finish` at the end.

doc.shortHtml: Workbook::createForDownload sends the file to the browser as a download named $name. The headers are sent at once, and each part of the file when it is ready. If the program stops before finish, the download is cut off and the error log names $name.
Workbook::createForFile writes the file to $path. If the file exists, it is replaced. The path needs the fs.write capability in nvs.toml.
Workbook::createForStream writes the file to $file, a file that your program opened for writing. finish does not close $file.
Workbook::createInMemory keeps the file in memory. finish returns it in Written::bytes.

Workbook::fromRows makes a workbook with one sheet that has every row of $rows. Call download, save, to or bytes on the result to write it. $options has the workbook options and the sheet options. sheet is the name of the sheet, and the default is 'Sheet1'. An Iterator of rows, such as a generator, is written once.

sheet starts a new sheet named $name and returns it. The sheet before it is finished, and you cannot add rows to it after this. When the rows have keys, the first row shows them in bold, with a filter, and stays at the top. header, headerStyle, freeze and autofilter change this.

define gives the cells at $reference, such as 'Orders!$C$2:$C$9', the name $name. A formula can then use the name. $reference must be a cell or a range of this workbook. Another file, a web address or a formula throws a LogicError.
finish writes the end of the file and sends the last part. Call it once, after the last row. A workbook that is never finished is not a valid file. A download that is never finished is cut off.

A name that ends in .ods or .csv, or format: 'ods' or format: 'csv', sets the format. Each create method sets where the file goes. Add a sheet with sheet, add its rows, and call finish at the end.

classes.summaryHtml:
A map whose keys are objects or other values of any type. A key is found by identity: the same object, not an equal one. Build one with new Core\ObjectMap<K, V>(). A foreach over the map gives its keys in insertion order.

Core\ObjectMap<K, V> associates a value with an object, matched by identity: the one object is one key however many variables hold it, and two objects that agree on every property are two keys. array<T> cannot key on an object, so this is where a per-object side table lives. It is built with new Core\ObjectMap<K, V>(), get answers ?V rather than throwing — there is no $m[$k] subscript on it — and has is the one member that tells an absent key from a stored null. The map is Iterable: a foreach yields its keys in insertion order, walking a snapshot taken when the loop began, so the body may remove what it is walking.

<?nvs
class Tag
{
    public function constructor(public string $name)
    {}
}

var $red = new Tag('red');
var $blue = new Tag('blue');

var $weights = new Core\ObjectMap<Tag, int>();
$weights->set($red, 3);
$weights->set($blue, 7);
$weights->set($red, 4);

echo 'red=', $weights->get($red) ?? 0, "\n";
echo 'other red=', $weights->get(new Tag('red')) ?? -1, "\n";
echo 'count=', $weights->count(), "\n";

foreach ($weights as Tag $tag) {
    echo $tag->name, ' ';
}
echo "\n";

$weights->remove($blue);
echo $weights->has($blue) ? 'blue kept' : 'blue gone', "\n";
echo 'keys=', Core\Arr::count($weights->keys()), ' values=', Core\Arr::count($weights->values()), "\n";
red=4
other red=-1
count=2
red blue
blue gone
keys=1 values=1

classes.summaryHtml:
A set of objects or other values of any type, each one at most once. A value is matched by identity: the same object, not an equal one. Build one with new Core\ObjectSet<T>(). A foreach over the set gives its values in insertion order.

Core\ObjectSet<T> holds each object at most once, matched by identity: adding the same object twice leaves one member, and a second object equal in every property is a second member. It is built with new Core\ObjectSet<T>(); add, has and remove are the membership members, and the set is Iterable — a foreach yields its members in insertion order, over a snapshot, so the body may remove what it is walking. union, intersect and diff answer a new set and leave both operands untouched; the binary types that new set as a bare Core\ObjectSet, so it can be counted, asked has and walked as mixed (foreach ($both as mixed $m) and then $m as Tag), but a foreach … as Tag $t over it is refused.

<?nvs
class Tag
{
    public function constructor(public string $name)
    {}
}

var $red = new Tag('red');
var $blue = new Tag('blue');
var $green = new Tag('green');

var $seen = new Core\ObjectSet<Tag>();
$seen->add($red);
$seen->add($blue);
$seen->add($red);
echo 'count=', $seen->count(), "\n";
echo $seen->has($red) ? 'has red' : 'no red', "\n";
echo $seen->has(new Tag('red')) ? 'has other red' : 'no other red', "\n";

var $wanted = new Core\ObjectSet<Tag>();
$wanted->add($blue);
$wanted->add($green);
echo 'union=', $seen->union($wanted)->count(), "\n";
echo 'both=', $seen->intersect($wanted)->count(), "\n";
echo 'only seen=', $seen->diff($wanted)->count(), "\n";

$seen->remove($red);
foreach ($seen as Tag $tag) {
    echo $tag->name, "\n";
}
echo $seen->isEmpty() ? 'empty' : 'not empty', "\n";
count=2
has red
no other red
union=3
both=1
only seen=1
blue
not empty

These methods need no capability.

classes.name: Core\Out
classes.summary: Collects what a piece of code prints, so your program can use it as a value. `capture` runs a function and returns everything it printed.

doc.shortHtml: Runs $fn and returns everything it printed with echo. The printed text does not reach the output. You can call capture inside another capture, and each call collects only what its own function printed.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: The function to run. Its return value is not used.

params.name: through
params.descHtml: A function that takes the collected output and returns new output of the same class. capture returns that new value. Without it, capture returns the output as it was printed.

doc.returnHtml: What $fn printed. In a web request it is a Core\Html\Markup. In every other program it is a Core\Cli\Text. It is empty when $fn printed nothing. Use echo to print it again without escaping it twice. Use is to check the class, then its text method to get a string. Output from Core\Debug::dump is not collected.

errors.descHtml: The through function returned a value of a different class than it was given.

classes.summaryHtml:
Collects what a piece of code prints, so your program can use it as a value. capture runs a function and returns everything it printed.

Core\Out::capture runs a callable and returns everything it echoed as the carrier of the sink in force — a Core\Cli\Text, or a Core\Html\Markup under an HTTP request, typed Core\Html\Markup|Core\Cli\Text — never a plain string, so re-emitting it is one more echo and it is not escaped a second time. as string reads the text out. Nothing the callable wrote reaches the output below; a capture nests by call nesting, and there is no global buffer stack and no implicit flush. { through: $fn } transforms the carrier before it is returned, and the callable's own return value is discarded. Core\Debug::dump is never captured — it writes to stderr.

<?nvs
var $captured = Core\Out::capture(fn(): void => {
    echo 'a';
    echo 'b';
});
echo 'captured=[', $captured, "]\n";

echo Core\Out::capture(fn(): void => {
    echo 'outer<';
    echo Core\Out::capture(fn(): void => { echo 'inner'; });
    echo '>';
}), "\n";

echo '[', Core\Out::capture(fn(): void => {}), "]\n";

try {
    echo Core\Out::capture(fn(): void => {
        echo 'lost';
        throw new RuntimeError('stop');
    });
} catch (RuntimeError $e) {
    echo 'threw: ', $e->message, "\n";
}
captured=[ab]
outer<inner>
[]
threw: stop
