classes.name: Core\Password
classes.summary: Stores and checks passwords safely. `hash` turns a password into a string you can save, `verify` checks a password against that string, and `needsRehash` tells you when a saved hash should be made again.

doc.shortHtml: Turns $password into a hash you can store, using Argon2id. The library chooses the settings, so there is no algorithm or cost argument. The result contains everything verify needs later: the algorithm, the settings, a random salt and the hash itself.

params.name: password
params.descHtml: The password to hash. It may be a secret string. The result is not secret, because it is made to be stored.

doc.returnHtml: A string such as $argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$<salt>$<hash>. Each call uses a new random salt, so the same password gives a different string every time.

errors.descHtml: The request cannot use the 19 MiB of memory that one hash needs.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $password is the password $hash was made from. It uses the settings stored in $hash, so a hash made with older settings still works. It reads the Argon2id strings hash writes, and bcrypt hashes that PHP wrote with $2y$, $2a$ or $2b$. The check takes the same time for every wrong password.

params.name: password
params.descHtml: The password somebody typed. It may be a secret string.

params.name: hash
params.descHtml: The stored hash: a string from hash, or a bcrypt hash that PHP stored.

doc.returnHtml: true when $password matches $hash, false when it does not.

errors.descHtml: $hash is not a password hash this class can read. It does not parse, it uses another algorithm, or it starts with $2x$. This usually means the stored value is broken, so it is an error and not false.
$hash needs too much work: more than 1 GiB of memory, too many passes over that memory, or a bcrypt cost above 17. It is also thrown when the request cannot use the memory the hash needs.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $hash is weaker than a hash hash makes today. Call it right after verify returns true. If it returns true, hash the password again and store the new hash.

params.name: hash
params.descHtml: The stored hash to check.

doc.returnHtml: true when $hash uses another algorithm or version, or less memory or fewer passes than hash uses now. Every bcrypt hash returns true. false when $hash is as strong as a new hash, or stronger.

errors.descHtml: $hash is not a password hash at all. A hash that uses another algorithm does not throw: it returns true.

classes.summaryHtml:
Stores and checks passwords safely. hash turns a password into a string you can save, verify checks a password against that string, and needsRehash tells you when a saved hash should be made again.

Core\Password::hash takes a password and returns the string to store. It takes nothing else: no algorithm, no memory cost, no time cost and no salt. The library chooses the parameters. It uses Argon2id at the minimum settings OWASP recommends. ::needsRehash tells you when a stored hash uses weaker settings than the current ones.

The answer is a PHC string: the algorithm, the version, the cost parameters and the salt travel with the digest. That is what lets ::verify recompute under the settings a hash was made with, so credentials written years ago still verify while new ones are written at today's cost.

::hash is one of exactly two operations that take a secret and answer something that is not one — the other is Core\Secret::reveal. Storing a hash is the point, so the result is an ordinary string and reaches the sinks a password never could.

Every call draws its own salt, so hashing one password twice answers two different strings and two users who chose the same password are indistinguishable in the store. Compare with ::verify, never with ==.

**::needsRehash returns true only when a hash is weaker than the current settings.** A hash written under stronger settings returns false, so it is never replaced by a weaker one.

A user table of bcrypt hashes that PHP wrote works at once, and upgrades itself one login at a time. ::verify reads two formats: the Argon2id string that ::hash writes, and a bcrypt hash that starts with $2y$, $2a$ or $2b$. ::needsRehash returns true for every bcrypt hash, because a different algorithm counts as weaker. So the usual login code below is the whole migration. It verifies the password, sees that the hash is old, and hashes the password again. Nothing is converted offline, because only the password itself can produce a new hash. ::hash has no algorithm argument, so it never writes bcrypt. A bcrypt hash with a cost above 17 throws an error before any work is done. A hash that starts with $2x$ also throws, because that tag exists only to reproduce an old bug.

A stored value outside those two shapes throws rather than answering false. A storage layer handing back the wrong column otherwise looks exactly like every user typing the wrong password at once, and one of those is worth waking someone up for.

<?nvs
secret string $password = 'correct horse battery staple';

// One argument, and the parameters come back out inside the answer.
string $stored = Core\Password::hash($password);
if (Core\Str::startsWith($stored, '$argon2id$v=19$')) {
    echo "stored under argon2id, v19\n";
}

// The bound, both sides of it.
secret string $offered = 'correct horse battery staple';
secret string $wrong = 'hunter2';
if (Core\Password::verify($offered, $stored)) {
    echo "the right password verifies\n";
}
if (!Core\Password::verify($wrong, $stored)) {
    echo "the wrong one does not\n";
}

// A hash made now is current by definition; one made under a lower cost is not.
string $old = '$argon2id$v=19$m=8192,t=1,p=1$jJ+hokoSJRsAzYsgfwhV6g$BGyWXoH11l0/GF4ezLqvtQgPY0T/4fv4DukErq9R0cI';
if (!Core\Password::needsRehash($stored) && Core\Password::needsRehash($old)) {
    echo "fresh is current, m=8192 has fallen behind\n";
}

// The usual shape at a login: verify, then upgrade what you just proved.
if (Core\Password::verify($offered, $stored) && Core\Password::needsRehash($stored)) {
    $stored = Core\Password::hash($offered);
}
echo "done\n";
stored under argon2id, v19
the right password verifies
the wrong one does not
fresh is current, m=8192 has fallen behind
done

classes.name: Core\Path
classes.summary: Reads and builds file paths as text. It never touches the disk. Every method accepts `/` and `\` as separators on every platform, and writes `Path::SEPARATOR`.

constants.name: SEPARATOR
constants.descHtml: The path separator of this platform. It is \ on Windows and / on every other platform. Every method writes it, and every method accepts both / and \.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the last part of $path: the file name, or the name of the last folder. A separator at the end is ignored, so /srv/shop/ gives shop.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

params.name: withoutExtension
params.descHtml: When true, the extension is removed, so report.pdf gives report. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The name. For a path that is only a root, such as / or C:\, the result is the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the folder that contains $path. The option levels goes up more than one folder.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

params.name: levels
params.descHtml: How many parts to remove from the end. The default is 1. With 0, the result is the path with its separators cleaned up. A number larger than the path stops at the root.

doc.returnHtml: The folder, written with Path::SEPARATOR. When nothing is left, the result is the root for an absolute path and . for a relative one. dirname('') is ..

doc.shortHtml: Returns the extension of the last part of $path: the text after the last ., without the dot.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

doc.returnHtml: The extension, or null when there is none. A name that starts with a dot, such as .gitignore, has none. A name that ends with a dot, such as report., has none too.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $path with the extension of its last part changed to $extension. When $extension is null, the extension is removed.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

params.name: extension
params.descHtml: The new extension, without its dot, the same way Core\Path::extension returns it. It may have a dot inside, such as tar.gz. null removes the extension.

doc.returnHtml: The new path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR.

errors.descHtml: $extension is empty, starts with a ., or contains / or \. Or $path has no file name, such as / or ''.

doc.shortHtml: Adds each of $segments to the end of $base, with one separator between each part. The result always starts where $base starts. A segment that starts with / or a drive is added after $base and does not replace it.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The first path. The result starts where this path starts.

params.name: segments
params.descHtml: Any number of paths to add, in order. A leading /, \ or drive in one of them is removed.

doc.returnHtml: The joined path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. With no segments, the result is $base with its extra separators removed. A .. segment stays in the result and still means the parent folder.

doc.shortHtml: Splits $path into its parts: the folders and the file name, in order. Core\Path::join puts the parts back together into the same path.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

doc.returnHtml: The parts in order. When the path starts at a root, the root is the first part: /, a drive such as C:\, or a share such as \\server\share\. The root is written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. No part is empty, because a repeated separator or one at the end adds nothing. The empty path gives an empty array.

doc.shortHtml: Removes the . and .. parts from $path and writes it with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. The method works on the text only and never looks at the disk. The result can still point outside a folder, so it does not make a path safe. Core\IO::within checks that.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

doc.returnHtml: The same path without . parts, and with each .. removing the folder before it. A .. at the start of a relative path stays. A .. that would go above a root is removed, because a root has no parent. A repeated separator or one at the end is removed. The empty path gives ..

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $path starts at a root. A root is a separator, a drive followed by a separator, or a network share. The check is the same on every platform.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

doc.returnHtml: true for /tmp, \tmp, C:/log and \\server\share. false for a relative path such as logs/app.log, for C:log, and for the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the path that leads from the folder $base to $path. The . and .. parts of both paths are removed first, as Core\Path::normalize does.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The place the result leads to.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The folder the result starts from. The result has one .. for each folder of $base that $path does not share.

doc.returnHtml: A relative path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. It is . when both paths name the same place. It is null when no relative path exists: one path is absolute and the other is not, the paths start at different roots, or $base starts with more .. parts than $path does. Folder names are compared byte for byte. A drive letter and a server name ignore upper and lower case.

doc.shortHtml: Joins $path to the folder the program was started from, and returns the full path. Use it for a path that a user typed on the command line.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. A relative path is joined to the working folder. A full path is returned as it is, with its . and .. parts removed.

doc.returnHtml: A full path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR, with its . and .. parts removed. The method does not check that the file exists. The result is not tainted, so you can pass a path from Core\Cli::arguments to Core\IO::read.

errors.descHtml: The program is handling a web request. A server has no working folder that belongs to the app.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the full path of the source file that contains this call. The compiler writes the path in place of the call, so the call costs nothing when the program runs.
doc.returnHtml: The full path of the file, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. In a bundled program, the folder is the one beside the executable.

errors.descHtml: The source was given to the compiler as text, so there is no file to name.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the full path of the folder that contains this source file. The compiler writes the path in place of the call, so the call costs nothing when the program runs.

params.name: join
params.descHtml: A relative path, written directly in the code as a string such as 'data'. It is added to the folder. A variable or a full path does not compile. Use Core\Path::join(Core\Path::thisDir(), $part) for a part the program builds.

doc.returnHtml: The full path of the folder, with $join added when you give one, and with its . and .. parts removed.

errors.descHtml: The source was given to the compiler as text, so there is no folder to name.

classes.summaryHtml:
Reads and builds file paths as text. It never touches the disk. Every method accepts / and \ as separators on every platform, and writes Path::SEPARATOR.

Core\Path is string algebra over path text: no member reads the disk, so nothing here needs a capability, follows a symlink or checks that a file exists — that is Core\IO. Both / and \ are accepted on every platform, and a member that answers a path renders it with Core\Path::SEPARATOR — \ on Windows, / elsewhere. join only appends: a segment's own leading separator or drive is dropped rather than allowed to replace the base. normalize resolves . and .. lexically; neither member makes an untrusted path safe, which is Core\IO::within. Absence is null: extension on a name without one, relativeTo where no relative path exists.

<?nvs
class Show
{
    // A rendered path carries the platform's separator; print it as `/` either way.
    public static function slash(string $p): string
    {
        return Core\Str::replace($p, Core\Path::SEPARATOR, '/');
    }
}
string $p = '/var/www/html/index.php';
echo Core\Path::basename($p), ' ', Core\Path::basename($p, { withoutExtension: true }), ' ', Core\Path::extension($p) ?? 'none', "\n";
echo Show::slash(Core\Path::dirname($p)), ' ', Show::slash(Core\Path::dirname($p, { levels: 2 })), "\n";
echo Show::slash(Core\Path::withExtension($p, 'html')), "\n";
echo Show::slash(Core\Path::join('/var/www', 'html', '/index.php')), "\n";
echo Show::slash(Core\Path::normalize('/var/www/../log/./app.log')), "\n";
echo Show::slash(Core\Path::relativeTo('/var/log/app.log', '/var/www') ?? 'none'), "\n";
echo Core\Str::join(Core\Path::split('etc//hosts/'), ','), ' ', Core\Path::isAbsolute('C:/tmp') ? 'abs' : 'rel', ' ', Core\Path::isAbsolute('tmp') ? 'abs' : 'rel', "\n";
echo Core\Path::extension('Makefile') ?? 'none', "\n";
index.php index php
/var/www/html /var/www
/var/www/html/index.html
/var/www/html/index.php
/var/log/app.log
../log/app.log
etc,hosts abs rel
none

classes.name: Core\Process
classes.summary: Runs other programs. A program is started directly with a list of arguments, never through a shell, so an argument cannot add a second command. `run` waits for the program to end, and `spawn` returns a handle while it runs. Both need the `process.exec` capability.

members.name: run
members.signature: run(string $path, array<string> $argv, { cwd?: string, env?: array<string>, timeout?: Core\Time\Duration }): Core\Process\Result

doc.shortHtml: Runs the program at $path with the arguments in $argv, and waits until it ends. The program is started directly, never through a shell, so nothing needs escaping. Needs the process.exec capability for the program.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The program to start, as an absolute path. A relative path must be a string written directly in the code. It is joined to the folder of the file that contains it. PATH is not searched, so ls means a file named ls in that folder.

params.name: argv
params.descHtml: The arguments, one in each element: ["-n", "1", $host]. An element with a space, a quote or a ; in it is still one argument, on every platform.

params.name: cwd
params.descHtml: The folder the program starts in, as an absolute path. A relative path must be written directly in the code, and is joined to the folder of this file. Without it, the program starts in the same folder as this program.

params.name: env
params.descHtml: The environment variables of the program, as name => value. This replaces all of them, so a variable that is not in the array is not set. Without it, the program gets only these variables from this program: PATH, HOME or USERPROFILE, TEMP, TMP, LANG, and SYSTEMROOT on Windows. A secret value must be revealed first.

params.name: timeout
params.descHtml: The longest time the program may run, counted from the start. When it passes, the program is stopped and a TimeoutError is thrown.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Process\Result with the exit code and everything the program wrote to its output and to its error output. The program cannot write to this program's own output, so the two never mix.

errors.descHtml: process.exec does not allow this program, or it is a .bat, .cmd or .ps1 file. Those are not allowed on any platform, because Windows starts them through a shell. The error is also thrown when the program writes more than [limits] max_output in total. Then the program is stopped and nothing is returned. It is also thrown when cwd is a relative path, or when timeout is zero or shorter. An env name that is empty or has a = in it throws it too.
The program was still running when timeout passed. The program is stopped and nothing is returned.
The program could not be started or waited for. For example, nothing is at the path, the file is not a program, or the cwd folder does not exist.

members.name: spawn
members.signature: spawn(string $path, array<string> $argv, { cwd?: string, env?: array<string>, timeout?: Core\Time\Duration }): Core\Process\Handle

doc.shortHtml: Starts the program at $path with the arguments in $argv, and returns at once while the program runs. The handle it returns reads the program's output and writes to its input. The program is started directly, never through a shell. Needs the process.exec capability for the program.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The program to start, as an absolute path or a path relative to the working directory. PATH is not searched.

params.name: argv
params.descHtml: The arguments, one in each element. An element with a space, a quote or a ; in it is still one argument, on every platform.

params.name: cwd
params.descHtml: The folder the program starts in, as an absolute path. A relative path must be written directly in the code, and is joined to the folder of this file. Without it, the program starts in the same folder as this program.

params.name: env
params.descHtml: The environment variables of the program, as name => value. This replaces all of them, so a variable that is not in the array is not set. Without it, the program gets only these variables from this program: PATH, HOME or USERPROFILE, TEMP, TMP, LANG, and SYSTEMROOT on Windows. A secret value must be revealed first.

params.name: timeout
params.descHtml: The longest time the program may run, counted from the start. When it passes, the program is stopped and a TimeoutError is thrown.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Process\Handle for the running program. Other requests keep running while this one waits on the handle. Call wait or kill on it before your script or request ends. A program that is still running then is stopped, and Novis reports an error.

errors.descHtml: process.exec does not allow this program, or it is a .bat, .cmd or .ps1 file. Those are not allowed on any platform, because Windows starts them through a shell. It is also thrown when cwd is a relative path, or when timeout is zero or shorter. An env name that is empty or has a = in it throws it too.
The program could not be started. For example, nothing is at the path, the file is not a program, or the cwd folder does not exist.

classes.summaryHtml: Runs other programs. A program is started directly with a list of arguments, never through a shell, so an argument cannot add a second command. run waits for the program to end, and spawn returns a handle while it runs. Both need the process.exec capability.

classes.name: Core\Process\Handle
classes.summary: A program that `Core\Process::spawn` started and that may still be running. `readStdout` and `readStderr` read its output a part at a time, and `writeStdin` writes to its input. `wait` waits for the end and returns a `Core\Process\Result`, and `kill` stops the program at once. Call one of them before your script or request ends. A program that is still running then is stopped, and Novis reports an error.

doc.shortHtml: Waits until the program writes to its standard output, and returns what it wrote. Call it in a loop to read the output one part at a time while the program runs. Other requests keep running while this one waits.
doc.returnHtml: The next part of the output, as bytes, up to 64 KiB. A part is whatever has arrived: it can be less than one line or several lines. At the end of the output the result is null, and every later call also returns null. Use as string to convert a part to text.

errors.descHtml: The timeout given to spawn has passed. The program is stopped, and every later call except kill throws this error too.
The operating system could not read the output. The output is then closed, so the next call returns null.

doc.shortHtml: Waits until the program writes to its standard error, and returns what it wrote. Programs write their error messages and warnings there. It works like readStdout, and the two outputs are never mixed.
doc.returnHtml: The next part of the error output, as bytes, up to 64 KiB. At the end of the error output the result is null, and every later call also returns null. Use as string to convert a part to text.

errors.descHtml: The timeout given to spawn has passed. The program is stopped, and every later call except kill throws this error too.
The operating system could not read the error output. The error output is then closed, so the next call returns null.

doc.shortHtml: Sends $data to the program's standard input. The call waits until the program has taken all of it. A tainted value is allowed here, because the program reads it as data and does not run it as a command.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The data to send, as bytes. All of it is sent. Use as bytes to convert a string.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The input stays open, so you can call writeStdin again. wait closes the input, and then the program sees the end of it.

errors.descHtml: The timeout given to spawn has passed. The program is stopped, and every later call except kill throws this error too.
The operating system could not send the data. This happens most often when the program has already ended, or after wait.

doc.shortHtml: Closes the program's standard input, waits until the program ends, and returns its result. While it waits, the server keeps handling other requests.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Process\Result with the exit code, and the output and error output that readStdout and readStderr did not read yet. If you already read all of the output, both are empty. A second call returns the same exit code and empty output.

errors.descHtml: The output that was not read yet is larger than [limits] max_output. The program is then stopped.
The timeout given to spawn has passed. The program is stopped, and every later call except kill throws this error too.
The operating system could not read the output or get the exit code.

doc.shortHtml: Stops the program at once, whatever it is doing. If the program has already ended, kill does nothing and throws no error. Call kill or wait before your script or request ends. A program that is still running then is stopped, and Novis reports an error.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing. Call wait afterwards to get the exit code. It is not 0 for a program that was stopped.

errors.descHtml: The operating system could not stop the program.

classes.summaryHtml: A program that Core\Process::spawn started and that may still be running. readStdout and readStderr read its output a part at a time, and writeStdin writes to its input. wait waits for the end and returns a Core\Process\Result, and kill stops the program at once. Call one of them before your script or request ends. A program that is still running then is stopped, and Novis reports an error.

classes.name: Core\Process\Result
classes.summary: The result of a program that has ended. `Core\Process::run` and `Core\Process\Handle::wait` return one. `exitCode` returns the program's exit code, and `stdout` and `stderr` return what it wrote to its output and its error output. The program has already ended, so these methods never throw an error.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the exit code of the program. Most programs return 0 when they succeed, and another number when they fail.
doc.returnHtml: The exit code, as an int. On Linux and macOS, it is -1 when a signal stopped the program before it could return an exit code.

doc.shortHtml: Returns everything the program wrote to its standard output.
doc.returnHtml: The output, as bytes. A program can write data that is not valid text, so the result is not a string. Use as string to convert it to text. That throws an error if the output is not valid UTF-8.

doc.shortHtml: Returns everything the program wrote to its standard error. Programs write their error messages and warnings there. This output is never mixed with stdout.
doc.returnHtml: The error output, as bytes. Use as string to convert it to text.

classes.summaryHtml: The result of a program that has ended. Core\Process::run and Core\Process\Handle::wait return one. exitCode returns the program's exit code, and stdout and stderr return what it wrote to its output and its error output. The program has already ended, so these methods never throw an error.

classes.name: Core\Program
classes.summary: Information about the whole program. `implementing` returns a new object of every class that implements an interface or extends a class. `implementingWith` returns the same objects, each with one attribute of its class. `constructors` returns a function for each of these classes, which creates an object with the arguments you pass. Novis finds these classes when it compiles the program, so nothing is searched while it runs. `id` returns a text that identifies this version of the program.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a new object of every class that is a T. T is an interface or a class, and you write it between < and >: Core\Program::implementing<Module>(). When T is a class that is not abstract, T itself is in the list. Abstract classes are not included. Each class needs a constructor without arguments, or the program does not compile. Novis finds the classes when it compiles the program, so nothing is searched while it runs.
doc.returnHtml: An array<T> with one new object per class, sorted by class name. Every call creates new objects. The array is empty when no class is a T.

members.name: implementingWith
members.signature: implementingWith<I, T>(string $member = ""): array<{ instance: I, attribute: ?T }>

doc.shortHtml: Returns the same objects as implementing<I>(), each with one attribute of its class. You write the interface or class I and the shape T of the attribute between < and >: Core\Program::implementingWith<Page, { path: string }>("render"). Novis reads the attributes when it compiles the program, so nothing is searched while it runs.

params.name: member
params.descHtml: The name of the method, property or constructor parameter that has the attribute. An empty string reads the attributes of the class itself.

doc.returnHtml: An array with one row per class, sorted by class name. Each row is { instance: I, attribute: ?T }. attribute is null when the class has no attribute of the shape T. Two matching attributes on one class do not compile.

members.name: constructors
members.signature: constructors<T, C>(): array<{ class: string, make: C }>

doc.shortHtml: Returns a function for every class that implementing<T>() lists, in the same order. You write the interface or class T and a function type C between < and >: Core\Program::constructors<Module, callable(Config): Module>(). Each function creates a new object of its class with the arguments you pass. A class whose constructor does not accept these arguments does not compile.
doc.returnHtml: An array with one row per class, sorted by class name. Each row is { class: string, make: C }. class is the full class name. No object is created until you call make.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a text that identifies this version of the program. It is a BLAKE3 hash of all the compiled code and of the environment it was compiled for. The same code on the same server gives the same value on every run.
doc.returnHtml: 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The value changes when the code or the environment changes. It is safe to print, because a hash does not show any source code.

errors.descHtml: The program was started without an identity. nvs run always gives a program one, so this happens only when a program is started some other way.

classes.summaryHtml:
Information about the whole program. implementing returns a new object of every class that implements an interface or extends a class. implementingWith returns the same objects, each with one attribute of its class. constructors returns a function for each of these classes, which creates an object with the arguments you pass. Novis finds these classes when it compiles the program, so nothing is searched while it runs. id returns a text that identifies this version of the program.

Core\Program::implementing<T>() is written with its type argument — T is an interface — and expands at compile time to an array literal of new expressions, one per non-abstract class in the program that implements T, sorted by fully-qualified name. Nothing is scanned at run time, and every element is a fresh instance typed T. A class is "in the program" when an autoload root reaches it: the compiler parses every file under every declared root for this one query, so a class never named by any require is still found. Abstract classes and the interface itself are not entries; a class reaching T through a parent class or through an interface that extends T is.

Core\Program::implementingWith<I, T>($member) is the same list with one attribute read off each class. Every row is { instance: I, attribute: ?T }: the instance, and the one attribute on that class's own $member whose fields satisfy the shape T, or null when there is none. $member is a method name, a property name, or the empty string for the attributes on the class itself. This is how a framework finds its pages and their routes in one call: implementingWith<View, { path: string }>("render") gives each page beside the path its #[Core\Route] carries, so the path is written once. Everything is resolved while compiling, and a member some implementor does not declare, or two matching attributes on one class, do not compile.

Core\Program::id() is the other member, and the only one here that runs. It answers this program's identity: BLAKE3 over every compiled unit's content hash, in program order, folded with the digest of the environment they were compiled for — so the same code on the same host answers the same 64 lowercase hex characters on every run, and any edit to any file in the program answers something else. All 32 bytes are returned; take a prefix if a shorter one is wanted, because a caller handed eight characters cannot get the other fifty-six back. It is computed once, before the program starts, so calling it in a loop costs nothing. Use it to bust a cache, version an asset URL, or tell one deployment's log lines from another's — it is a digest, so it is safe to echo and reveals no source, though a reader who watches it learns when the deployment last changed. It cannot be a constant: writing the id directly into a file would change that file's bytes, and so the id it just wrote down.

<?nvs
namespace App;

interface Greeter
{
    public function greet(): string;
}
<?nvs
namespace App;

class Formal implements Greeter
{
    public function greet(): string
    {
        return 'Good day.';
    }
}
<?nvs
namespace App;

class Casual implements Greeter
{
    public function greet(): string
    {
        return 'Hey!';
    }
}
<?nvs
autoload 'App' from './lib';

var $greeters = Core\Program::implementing<App\Greeter>();
echo 'found ', Core\Arr::count($greeters), "\n";
foreach ($greeters as App\Greeter $greeter) {
    echo $greeter->greet(), "\n";
}

// The id is a digest of these very files, so no example can print it and stay
// reproducible. Its shape is what holds from run to run.
string $id = Core\Program::id();
echo 'id is ', Core\Str::length($id), ' characters, and stable within the run: ', Core\Program::id() == $id ? 'yes' : 'no', "\n";
found 2
Hey!
Good day.
id is 64 characters, and stable within the run: yes

classes.name: Core\Queue
classes.summary: Runs work in the background. `push` saves a job as a row in the database set by `[queue] connection`, and a worker runs the job later. Inside a transaction on that connection, the job is saved only when the transaction commits. `status`, `cancel` and `delete` work on one job. `stats` and `purge` work on a whole queue.

doc.shortHtml: The state of a background job, as Core\Queue::status returns it. There are five states and no Failed state. A failed attempt is retried, so the job goes back to Pending.

members.name: push
members.signature: push(string $script, { args?: mixed, queue?: string, runAt?: Core\Time\Instant, maxAttempts?: uint, backoff?: Core\Time\Duration, key?: string, tag?: string, grants?: array<string>, memory?: string, cpuTime?: string, wallTime?: string, maxOutput?: string }): Core\Queue\Id

doc.shortHtml: Adds a job that runs $script in the background. The job is a row in the database set by [queue] connection. Inside a transaction on that connection, the job is saved only when the transaction commits. If the transaction rolls back, the job is not saved.

params.name: script
params.descHtml: The path of the file a worker runs, written the way spawn script writes one. A relative path starts at the folder of the file that calls push. It is a file, not a class or a function, so the job has no captured variables.

params.name: args
params.descHtml: The data the job receives. It is copied into the row and decoded into the types the job declares. It is never passed by reference, because the worker usually runs in another process.

params.name: queue
params.descHtml: The name of the queue the job goes in. Each worker takes jobs from the queues it is configured for, so you can keep slow work and fast work apart.

params.name: runAt
params.descHtml: The earliest time a worker may start the job. The default is now.

params.name: maxAttempts
params.descHtml: How many times the job may run before it moves to the dead-letter table (the table of jobs that failed too often). The default is [queue] max_attempts. The number is always finite, so a job cannot retry forever.

params.name: backoff
params.descHtml: The base wait between two attempts. The wait grows after each failed attempt, and the worker adds a small random amount. The default is one second.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: A key that stops duplicate jobs. While a job with this key is still pending, a second push with the same key adds nothing. It returns the id of the pending job.

params.name: tag
params.descHtml: A group name for the job. Many jobs can have the same tag. Only purge reads it, to delete one group of jobs. You cannot add a tag after the push.

params.name: grants
params.descHtml: The capabilities the job may use, written the way nvs.toml grants them. The list may only contain capabilities this request has. The default is what this request has. [] gives the job no capabilities.

params.name: memory
params.descHtml: The memory limit for the job, written like [limits] memory. [limits.hard] sets the highest value allowed. The default is the limit of this request.

params.name: cpuTime
params.descHtml: The CPU time limit for the job, written like [limits] cpu_time. It follows the same rules as memory.

params.name: wallTime
params.descHtml: The real time limit for the job, written like [limits] wall_time. It follows the same rules as memory.

params.name: maxOutput
params.descHtml: The limit on the output the job may print, written like [limits] max_output. It follows the same rules as memory.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Queue\Id for the new job. You pass it to status, cancel and delete. When key finds a pending job, it is the id of that job.

errors.descHtml: The configuration has no [queue] block, or the database driver of the queue's connection cannot run statements yet. It is also thrown when grants contains a capability this request does not have.
maxAttempts is 0, or backoff is negative. It is also thrown when grants contains a name that is not a capability, or a limit is one this request may not set.
The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the insert. The most common cause is that nvs queue migrate has not created the table yet.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the current state of one job, as a Core\Queue::State case. Every call reads the state from the database.

params.name: job
params.descHtml: The Core\Queue\Id that push returned. It identifies the job and its queue.

doc.returnHtml: Pending while the job waits, also while its runAt time or its backoff has not passed. Claimed while a worker runs it, Succeeded after it ran, Dead after it used all its attempts, and Cancelled after cancel stopped it.

errors.descHtml: The configuration has no [queue] block, or the database driver of the queue's connection cannot run statements yet. It is also thrown when neither table has the job, for example because delete deleted it.
The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the query. The most common cause is that nvs queue migrate has not created the tables yet.

doc.shortHtml: Removes one job from the queue if it is still waiting. A job that a worker already started keeps running, because cancel does not stop work in progress.

params.name: job
params.descHtml: The Core\Queue\Id that push returned. It identifies the job and its queue.

doc.returnHtml: true if this call cancelled the job. false if the job was no longer waiting: a worker took it, it already ran, or an earlier cancel removed it. After true, status returns Cancelled.

errors.descHtml: The configuration has no [queue] block, or the database driver of the queue's connection cannot run statements yet.
The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the update. The most common cause is that nvs queue migrate has not created the table yet.

doc.shortHtml: Counts the jobs of one queue. The result has five numbers: waiting jobs, running jobs, attempts used, jobs in the dead-letter table, and the attempts those jobs used. All five are read at the same moment.

params.name: queue
params.descHtml: The name of the queue, the same name push used in its queue option. Each call counts one queue.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Queue\Stats. Each number is a method, so you write $stats->pending(), not $stats->pending.

errors.descHtml: The configuration has no [queue] block, or the database driver of the queue's connection cannot run statements yet.
The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the query. The most common cause is that nvs queue migrate has not created the tables yet.

doc.shortHtml: Deletes the row of one job. The row can be in the jobs table or in the dead-letter table. A job that a worker is running is not deleted. You need the queue.purge capability for the queue of the job.

params.name: job
params.descHtml: The Core\Queue\Id that push returned. It still works after the job moves to the dead-letter table.

doc.returnHtml: true if this call deleted the row. false if there was nothing to delete: a worker is running the job, the job is not in this queue, or an earlier delete deleted it. After true, the row is gone, so status throws an error for this job.

errors.descHtml: The configuration grants no queue.purge for the queue of the job. A server has no such grant until the person who runs it adds one. It is also thrown when there is no [queue] block, or the database driver cannot run statements yet.
The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the delete. The most common cause is that nvs queue migrate has not created the tables yet.

members.name: purge
members.signature: purge(string $queue, { state?: Core\Queue::State, tag?: string, before?: Core\Time\Instant, limit?: uint }): uint

doc.shortHtml: Deletes the finished jobs of a queue and returns how many rows it deleted. Without state, it deletes the Succeeded and Cancelled jobs. Dead and Pending jobs are deleted only when you pass that state. Claimed jobs are never deleted. One call deletes at most limit rows, so you call it again until it returns 0. You need the queue.purge capability for the queue.

params.name: queue
params.descHtml: The name of the queue. It must match the name push used exactly. The queue.purge capability is checked for this name.

params.name: state
params.descHtml: One Core\Queue::State to delete in place of the default ones. Dead deletes from the dead-letter table. Pending deletes jobs that have not run yet. Claimed throws an error, because a worker is running those jobs.

params.name: tag
params.descHtml: Deletes only the jobs that push gave this tag.

params.name: before
params.descHtml: Deletes only the jobs added before this time. This is the time of the push, not the time of the next attempt.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: The most rows one call deletes, oldest first. The default is 1000. A delete without a limit can lock the table for a long time, and every push waits for it.

doc.returnHtml: The number of rows this call deleted, and 0 when nothing matched. while (Core\Queue::purge('email') > 0) {} deletes all of them, one batch at a time.

errors.descHtml: state is Core\Queue::State::Claimed. A worker is running those jobs, so their rows cannot be deleted.

The configuration grants no queue.purge for this queue. A server has no such grant until the person who runs it adds one. It is also thrown when there is no [queue] block, or the database driver cannot run statements yet.
The connection to the database failed, or the database rejected the delete. The most common cause is that nvs queue migrate has not created the tables yet.

classes.summaryHtml: Runs work in the background. push saves a job as a row in the database set by [queue] connection, and a worker runs the job later. Inside a transaction on that connection, the job is saved only when the transaction commits. status, cancel and delete work on one job. stats and purge work on a whole queue.

classes.name: Core\Queue\Id
classes.summary: The id of one background job, as `Core\Queue::push` returns it. It identifies the job and the queue the job is in. You pass it to `status`, `cancel` and `delete`. It has no methods of its own.
classes.summaryHtml: The id of one background job, as Core\Queue::push returns it. It identifies the job and the queue the job is in. You pass it to status, cancel and delete. It has no methods of its own.

classes.name: Core\Queue\Stats
classes.summary: The numbers that `Core\Queue::stats` returns for one queue. All five are read at the same moment. Each number is a method, so you write `$stats->pending()`, not `$stats->pending`.

doc.shortHtml: The number of jobs that wait for a worker. This includes jobs whose runAt time is still in the future, and jobs that wait between two attempts.
doc.returnHtml: A uint. It is 0 for a new queue and for a queue with no work left.

doc.shortHtml: The number of jobs that a worker is running now. A job whose worker stopped is still counted here. After the [queue] visibility time, another worker can start it again.
doc.returnHtml: A uint. When it equals the number of jobs your workers can run at once, the queue is busy but not stuck.

doc.shortHtml: The total number of attempts the jobs of this queue have used. If this number grows and pending does not, jobs are failing and running again.
doc.returnHtml: A uint for the jobs table only. The jobs in the dead-letter table are counted by deadLettered and deadAttempts.

doc.shortHtml: The number of jobs that used all their attempts and are now in the dead-letter table. These jobs did not finish, so this is a good number to alert on.
doc.returnHtml: A uint. It goes down only when purge or delete deletes a job from the dead-letter table.

doc.shortHtml: The total number of attempts the jobs in the dead-letter table used. Divide it by deadLettered to see how many attempts a job uses before it fails for good.
doc.returnHtml: A uint for the dead-letter table only. Every attempt is counted in this number or in attempts, never in both. Add the two to get the total.

doc.shortHtml: The number of jobs that push saved while a transaction was open on a different database connection. Such a job is saved at once, so a rollback of that transaction does not remove it.
doc.returnHtml: A uint for the jobs table only. It is 0 when every transaction that pushes a job runs on the connection that [queue] connection names.

classes.summaryHtml: The numbers that Core\Queue::stats returns for one queue. All five are read at the same moment. Each number is a method, so you write $stats->pending(), not $stats->pending.

classes.summary: Random numbers, bytes, tokens and choices from a cryptographic generator, so a value is safe to use for a key, a code or a password reset link. For a sequence that repeats from a seed, use `Core\Random\Seeded`.

params.descHtml: How many random bytes to use, 32 by default. The string has twice as many characters.

errors.descHtml: $bytes is 0, because an empty token is equal to every other empty token. It is also thrown when the result is larger than a buffer this process can allocate.

params.descHtml: The array to choose from.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to choose from.

params.name: count

doc.returnHtml: A new list of the chosen values, in random order, with the keys 0, 1, …. The keys of $a are not kept, and $a is unchanged.

errors.descHtml: $count is greater than the number of entries in $a.

params.descHtml: The array to reorder.

classes.summaryHtml:
Random numbers, bytes, tokens and choices from a cryptographic generator, so a value is safe to use for a key, a code or a password reset link. For a sequence that repeats from a seed, use Core\Random\Seeded.

Core\Random is always a CSPRNG: there is no seeded or insecure generator under this name, and no function sets a global seed. int draws from a closed range and throws on an empty one rather than swapping the bounds; pick, sample and shuffle draw from an array and answer values — a fresh array for shuffle, null from pick on an empty one. token is the hex text of bytes, two characters per byte, for a session identifier or a reset link.

Reproducibility is a separate type, Core\Random\Seeded, built from an explicit seed with new and carrying the same seven members: one seed is one sequence, every run, which is what a simulation or a fixture wants and what a session token must never be. Because it is a type rather than a mode, a parameter declaring which generator it takes cannot be handed the other one by mistake.

<?nvs
echo Core\Random::int(7, 7), "\n";
int $face = Core\Random::int(1, 6);
echo $face >= 1 && $face <= 6 ? 'a die face' : 'out of range', "\n";

array<string> $only = ['ace'];
echo Core\Random::pick($only), "\n";
array<int> $deck = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
echo Core\Arr::count(Core\Random::shuffle($deck)), "\n";
echo Core\Arr::count(Core\Random::sample($deck, 2)), "\n";

echo Core\Str::length(Core\Random::token(8)), "\n";
echo Core\Bytes::length(Core\Random::bytes(16)), "\n";
float $f = Core\Random::float();
echo $f >= 0.0 && $f < 1.0 ? 'in [0, 1)' : 'outside', "\n";

array<int> $none = [];
echo Core\Random::pick($none) == null ? 'nothing to pick' : 'picked', "\n";
try {
    Core\Random::int(5, 1);
} catch (RuntimeError $empty) {
    echo "empty range\n";
}

var $left = new Core\Random\Seeded(42);
var $right = new Core\Random\Seeded(42);
echo $left->token(4) == $right->token(4) ? 'one seed, one sequence' : 'diverged', "\n";
echo $left->int(1, 6) == $right->int(1, 6) ? 'and it stays that way' : 'diverged', "\n";
7
a die face
ace
5
2
16
16
in [0, 1)
nothing to pick
empty range
one seed, one sequence
and it stays that way

classes.name: Core\Random\Seeded
classes.summary: A random generator that starts from a seed you give it, so the same seed gives the same values every time. Use it for tests and simulations. For a key, a code or a token, use `Core\Random`.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a random integer from $min to $max, including both ends. It works like Core\Random::int, but the same seed always gives the same result.

params.name: min
params.descHtml: The lowest value the result can be.

params.name: max
params.descHtml: The highest value the result can be.

doc.returnHtml: An int from $min to $max. When the two are equal, the result is $min.

errors.descHtml: $min is greater than $max. The method does not swap the two values.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a random float from 0.0 up to, but not including, 1.0. It works like Core\Random::float, but the same seed always gives the same result.
doc.returnHtml: A float with 53 random bits. The result can be 0.0, but never 1.0.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $count random bytes from this generator's sequence. Use it for test data, never for a key. Anyone who knows the seed can compute the same bytes.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: How many bytes to return. It must be at least 1.

doc.returnHtml: A tainted bytes value with exactly $count raw bytes. It is tainted, so a parameter that needs a key does not accept it.

errors.descHtml: $count is 0, as with Core\Random::bytes, or it is larger than a buffer this process can allocate.

doc.shortHtml: Takes $bytes random bytes from this generator's sequence and returns them as lower-case hex. Use it for a stable test identifier, never for a session token.

params.name: bytes
params.descHtml: How many random bytes to use, 32 by default. The string has twice as many characters.

doc.returnHtml: A tainted string of 2 * $bytes hex digits, 0–9 and a–f. It is tainted, so a parameter that needs a key does not accept it.

errors.descHtml: $bytes is 0, or the result is larger than a buffer this process can allocate.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value of one random entry of $a. It works like Core\Random::pick, but the same seed always gives the same result.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to choose from.

doc.returnHtml: The value of one entry. When $a is empty, the result is null. With an array<?T>, you cannot tell this apart from an entry that is null.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $count different random entries of $a. It works like Core\Random::sample, but the same seed always gives the same result.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to choose from.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: How many different entries to return. It must not be more than the entries in $a.

doc.returnHtml: A new list of the chosen values, in the order they were chosen, with the keys 0, 1, …. The keys of $a are not kept, and $a is unchanged.

errors.descHtml: $count is greater than the number of entries in $a.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every entry of $a in a random order. It works like Core\Random::shuffle, but the same seed always gives the same order.

params.name: a

classes.summaryHtml: A random generator that starts from a seed you give it, so the same seed gives the same values every time. Use it for tests and simulations. For a key, a code or a token, use Core\Random.

classes.name: Core\RateLimit
classes.summary: Limits how often something may happen for one key, such as one account or one API key. `consume` counts in the shared store, so every server gives the same answer. `shed` counts in the memory of this server process only, to drop load quickly. Both return a `Core\RateLimit\Decision`.

members.name: consume
members.signature: consume(string $key, uint $limit, Core\Time\Duration $per, { burst?: uint, cost?: uint }): Core\RateLimit\Decision

doc.shortHtml: Charges $cost units against the allowance of $key, which is $limit per $per. The count is kept in the shared store. The result says if this call is inside the limit.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: Who the limit is for, such as an account, a tenant or an API key id. A tainted value is allowed. A secret value is not allowed, because the key is written to the store. Use Core\Hash::of of the secret instead.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: How many units are allowed in each $per. This is the average rate. It is not a limit on one single moment.

params.name: per
params.descHtml: The period in which $limit units are allowed.

params.name: burst
params.descHtml: How many units may arrive at the same moment. The default is $limit, which allows a whole period's units at once.

params.name: cost
params.descHtml: How many units this call uses. The default is 1. An expensive endpoint can use five units of the same limit, for example.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\RateLimit\Decision. Its retryAfter is null when the call is allowed. Otherwise it is the exact time to wait until the call would be allowed. It is not an estimate, and it is not rounded up to the next period.

errors.descHtml: The shared store cannot be reached, or it rejected the command. The call is never treated as allowed. Your code catches this error and decides whether to allow the call or not.

No [cache.shared] url is configured, or cache.shared is not granted. This is a deployment mistake, so it is not an IOError that your catch for a store failure handles. This error is also thrown when $limit, $per or $burst is zero. It is also thrown when the period is too short to divide into $limit units, or when $cost is larger than $burst.

members.name: shed
members.signature: shed(string $key, uint $limit, Core\Time\Duration $per, { burst?: uint, cost?: uint }): Core\RateLimit\Decision

doc.shortHtml: Charges $cost units against the allowance of $key, which is $limit per $per. The count is kept in the memory of this server process. The result says if this call is inside the limit. Use it to drop load. Use consume for a limit you promised to somebody.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: Who the limit is for. A tainted value is allowed. A secret value is not allowed, the same as for consume.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: How many units are allowed in each $per, in this server process. Every request this process serves counts against the same limit. Two server processes with a limit of 100 allow up to 200, so a number you promised belongs to consume.

params.name: per
params.descHtml: The period in which $limit units are allowed.

params.name: burst
params.descHtml: How many units may arrive at the same moment. The default is $limit.

params.name: cost
params.descHtml: How many units this call uses. The default is 1.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\RateLimit\Decision. It uses no external store, so it does not throw an IOError. The count is kept in the same memory as Core\Cache::memory(), which can forget an entry at any time. When a count is forgotten, the key allows a burst again.

errors.descHtml: $limit, $per or $burst is zero, the period is too short to divide into $limit units, or $cost is larger than $burst. These are the same errors that consume throws.

classes.summaryHtml: Limits how often something may happen for one key, such as one account or one API key. consume counts in the shared store, so every server gives the same answer. shed counts in the memory of this server process only, to drop load quickly. Both return a Core\RateLimit\Decision.

classes.name: Core\RateLimit\Decision
classes.summary: The result of one `Core\RateLimit::consume` or `shed` call. `allowed` says whether the call was inside the limit. `limit`, `remaining` and `retryAfter` give the numbers for `RateLimit` and `Retry-After` response headers.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether the call was inside the limit. Only an allowed call is charged.
doc.returnHtml: true when the units were charged. false when the call was over the limit and nothing was charged.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the $limit that was used for the decision. You can write a RateLimit header from the decision alone.
doc.returnHtml: The limit as it was passed.

doc.shortHtml: Returns how many more units are allowed at this moment.
doc.returnHtml: The units left in the burst, after this call was charged. It is 0 when the next unit has to wait.

doc.shortHtml: Returns how long to wait until the call would be allowed. The time is exact, and it comes from the clock of the store.
doc.returnHtml: null when the call is allowed. Otherwise, the Core\Time\Duration until the call would be allowed. A Retry-After header with this value tells each client its own time to try again. So the rejected clients do not all retry at the same moment.

classes.summaryHtml: The result of one Core\RateLimit::consume or shed call. allowed says whether the call was inside the limit. limit, remaining and retryAfter give the numbers for RateLimit and Retry-After response headers.

classes.name: Core\Reflect
classes.summary: Describes a value or a class while the program runs. `typeOf` returns what kind of value you have. `forClass` and `forObject` return a `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo` with the class's properties, methods, constants and attributes.

doc.shortHtml: The kind of a value while the program runs. There are ten cases, and every value matches exactly one of them.
Describes the class with the name $name. You do not need an object of that class.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The class's name as its declaration writes it, with the namespace and with no \ at the start. Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::name returns this name.

doc.returnHtml: A description of that class. The result is null if the running program declares no class with that name. This is not an error.

doc.shortHtml: Describes the class of $object: its name, and the properties that code outside the class can see.

params.name: object
params.descHtml: The value to describe. Reflection is for a value whose class is not known at compile time, so the parameter is mixed.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Reflect\ClassInfo for the object's own class. It describes the class and does not contain the object.

errors.descHtml: $object is not an object. A mixed value may be anything, so this method checks it and the caller does not need to.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the kind of value $value is right now. Use it on a mixed value.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to check. For any type but mixed, the compiler already knows the result, so this is useful for a value whose type is mixed.

doc.returnHtml: One Core\Reflect::TypeKind case. Every value matches exactly one case, because the cases do not overlap.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the property that each part of a property path names.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: A property path, such as customer.address.city of type propertyPath<Order>.

doc.returnHtml: One Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo for each part of the path, in order. Each one has the property's name, whether it is public, and its declared type. The type shows whether the next part is reached through an object, a nullable object or an array.

errors.descHtml: steps was called through a callable value, so the class the path starts at is not known.

classes.summaryHtml: Describes a value or a class while the program runs. typeOf returns what kind of value you have. forClass and forObject return a Core\Reflect\ClassInfo with the class's properties, methods, constants and attributes.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo
classes.summary: One `#[...]` attribute written on a class or on one of its properties or methods, as `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::attributes` returns it. `target` and `parameter` say where it is written. `fields` lists its payload's field names, and `field` returns one value.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the name of the type alias written in the attribute, as it is written.
doc.returnHtml: The written name. For the form #[{...}], which has no name, it is the empty string. The name is not resolved. The compiler uses it to check the payload object where the attribute is written. Your code never uses it to find an attribute.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the property or method that the attribute is written on.
doc.returnHtml: A property's name without the $, or a method's name. For the class or interface declaration itself, it is the empty string. For an attribute on a parameter, this is the method's name, and parameter returns the parameter's name.

doc.shortHtml: The parameter of target the attribute is written on.
doc.returnHtml: The parameter's name without the $. For an attribute that is not on a parameter, it is the empty string. With target, you can tell #[X] public function f(...) from public function f(#[X] int $n). These two attributes are on different declarations.

doc.shortHtml: The payload's field names, in the order the attribute writes them.
doc.returnHtml: One string for each field. This includes a field whose value Novis does not compute here. field throws an error for such a field.

doc.shortHtml: Returns one payload field's value, computed at compile time.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The field's name, as fields returns it.

doc.returnHtml: The value as a string, int, bool or float. These are the four types a payload field can have here.

errors.descHtml: The attribute's payload has no field of that name. This is a mistake in the program, so the method throws an error and does not return an empty value. fields returns the names that exist. Or Novis does not compute the field's value here. That is a class constant, an enum case or Foo::class, which depend on the namespace the attribute is written in. It is also any value that Core\Reflect\ConstantInfo cannot read. Core\Attributes::get reads all of these values at compile time, by shape.

classes.summaryHtml: One #[...] attribute written on a class or on one of its properties or methods, as Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::attributes returns it. target and parameter say where it is written. fields lists its payload's field names, and field returns one value.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\ClassInfo
classes.summary: One class, as `Core\Reflect::forClass` and `Core\Reflect::forObject` return it. `properties`, `methods`, `constants` and `attributes` list what the class declares. `get`, `set`, `call` and `construct` use a class whose name is only known at run time.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the name of the described class, with its namespace, as the declaration writes it.
doc.returnHtml: The class name, such as App\Model\User for a class in a namespace. It is never an alias that the calling code used.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the properties of the described class, its own and every inherited one. Each has its name, its visibility and its declared type.
doc.returnHtml: One Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo for each declared property. The properties of every parent class come first, then the class's own. A private or protected property is in the list, and its isPublic returns false. get checks whether this code may read it.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the names of the properties that code at this call site may read, in the same order as properties. The result depends on where the call is written.
doc.returnHtml: One name for each property that code here may read, without the $. Inside the described class, that is every declared property. Anywhere else, it is the public ones. properties returns the complete list. get throws an error here for exactly the properties that are in that list and not in this one.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether the described class declares a property called $name.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The property's name without the $, as the declaration writes it.

doc.returnHtml: true for a private or protected property as well as a public one. So you can tell a property you may not read from a misspelled name. properties tells you whether this code may read it.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the methods of the described class, its own and every inherited one. Each has its name, its visibility and the number of parameters it declares.
doc.returnHtml: One Core\Reflect\MethodInfo for each declared method, sorted by name. A method that the calling code may not call is in the list, and its isPublic() returns false. Listing a method does not call it. Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::call checks whether this code may call it.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the constants of the described class, its own and every inherited one. Each has its name and its visibility.
doc.returnHtml: One Core\Reflect\ConstantInfo for each constant of the class, its own declarations first. A constant that a subclass declares again appears once, with the declaration the class uses. The values are not in the list. Use constant to read a value, which checks whether this code may read it.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value of the class constant $name. The visibility rules are the same as for ordinary code at this call site, and nothing can turn them off.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The constant's name, as the declaration writes it, with no class name and no ::.

doc.returnHtml: The value, computed at compile time. It is a string, int, bool or float, the same type as the value in the declaration.

errors.descHtml: Code at this call site may not read the constant $name. Reflection has the same visibility rules as ordinary code. This error is also thrown everywhere for a constant whose declared type is secret. The mixed result cannot be secret, so the value would lose that protection.

The class declares and inherits no constant of that name. Or the constant's value is not a string, int, bool or float written directly in the code. hasValue checks this before the call. Both are mistakes in the program, not permission problems. That is how they differ from the RuntimeError above.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether the described class declares or inherits a method named $name.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The method's name, as the declaration writes it and as methods returns it.

doc.returnHtml: true for a method of the class at any visibility. false if the class has no method with that name. So when a call fails, you can tell a private method from a misspelled name.

doc.shortHtml: Returns every #[...] attribute written on the class's own declaration or on its own properties and methods.
doc.returnHtml: One Core\Reflect\AttributeInfo for each place an attribute is written, in source order. The class declaration's attributes come first, then those of each property and method. A method's parameters come after that method. Only the class's own declarations are included. constants also includes the parent classes. An attribute belongs to the declaration it is written on, so a parent class's attributes are not listed. Core\Attributes::get reads an attribute by the shape of its payload. It is checked at compile time and costs nothing at run time. Use attributes for a class whose name is not in your source code.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the $name property of $object. The visibility rules are the same as for ordinary code at this call site, and nothing can turn them off.

params.name: object
params.descHtml: An instance of the described class. The description is of a class and does not contain an object, so you pass the object to read here.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The property's name without the $, as properties returns it.

doc.returnHtml: The property's value. Its type is mixed, whatever type the property declares.

errors.descHtml: $object is not an object, or $name is a property that is not public. Reflection has the same visibility rules as ordinary code. Ordinary code outside the class gets the same error for this read.

$object is not an instance of the described class, or the class has no property called $name. Both are mistakes in the program, not facts about the value. That is how they differ from the RuntimeError above.

doc.shortHtml: Writes the $name property of $object, and then runs the PropertyObserver, as an ordinary write does. The visibility rules are the same as for ordinary code at this call site, and nothing can turn them off.

params.name: object
params.descHtml: An instance of the described class. You pass it here for the same reason as in get.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The property's name without the $, as properties returns it.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to store. It is checked against the type that the object's class declares for the property, because that type is not known at compile time.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. A following get returns the stored value, and the observer is told about that value.

errors.descHtml: $object is not an object, $name is a property that is not public, or $value does not have the type that the property declares. Ordinary code outside the class gets the same errors for the first two. A write through a mixed value gets the same error for the third.
$object is not an instance of the described class, or the class has no property called $name. As in get, these are mistakes in the program, so they have a different error class.
Whatever the class's own onPropertySet observer throws. The observer runs after the value is stored. If it throws, the write still fails, as an ordinary write does.

doc.shortHtml: Calls the $name method of $object with $arguments. The visibility rules are the same as for ordinary code at this call site, and nothing can turn them off.

params.name: object
params.descHtml: An instance of the described class. The description is of a class and does not contain an object, so you pass the object to call here.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The method's name without the (), as the declaration writes it.

params.name: arguments
params.descHtml: One entry for each declared parameter, in order. Keys are ignored. Entries after the last parameter are ignored. This argument is required even when the method has no parameters. In that case, pass [].

doc.returnHtml: Whatever the method returned. Its type is mixed, whatever type the method declares.

errors.descHtml: $name is not public, is not a method of the class, or is a Core method. Or $arguments has fewer entries than the method's parameters, or an entry has a type that its parameter does not accept. An ordinary call on a mixed value throws the same error, from the same check.
$object is not an object at all. A $object that is an object but not an instance of the described class is the LogicError above.

doc.shortHtml: Builds an instance of the described class and runs its constructor with $arguments. The visibility rules are the same as for a new written at this call site, and nothing can turn them off.

params.name: arguments
params.descHtml: One entry for each declared constructor parameter, in order. Keys are ignored. Entries after the last parameter are ignored. This argument is required even when the class declares no constructor. In that case, pass [].

doc.returnHtml: The new instance. Its type is mixed. For a class with no constructor, the new instance has the default values that the class declares for its properties.

errors.descHtml: The constructor is not public and this call site is outside the class. Or $arguments has fewer entries than the constructor's parameters, or an entry has a type that its parameter does not accept. Or this program does not declare the described class. An ordinary new makes the same checks.

classes.summaryHtml: One class, as Core\Reflect::forClass and Core\Reflect::forObject return it. properties, methods, constants and attributes list what the class declares. get, set, call and construct use a class whose name is only known at run time.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\ConstantInfo
classes.summary: One class constant, as `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constants` returns it. `name` and `isPublic` describe the declaration. `hasValue` says whether `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constant` can return its value.

doc.shortHtml: The constant's name, as the declaring class writes it.
doc.returnHtml: The name with no class name and no ::. Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constant takes this name.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether code outside the declaring class may use the constant.
doc.returnHtml: false for a private or protected constant. That constant is still in the list, as with Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo::isPublic. So you can tell a constant you may not read from a misspelled name.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether Novis computes the constant's value at compile time. Only then can Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constant return it.
doc.returnHtml: true for a string, int, bool or float written directly in the code. false for an array or object constant, and for an integer too large for int. Novis reads a constant only when its value is written directly in the code, and it does not evaluate other expressions. So this is false for exactly the constants that are also not allowed in type position.

classes.summaryHtml: One class constant, as Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constants returns it. name and isPublic describe the declaration. hasValue says whether Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::constant can return its value.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\EnumInfo
classes.summary: One enum, as `Core\Reflect\EnumInfo::of` returns it for the enum's name. `cases` lists the names of its cases, `valueOf` returns the value of one case, and `isUnsigned` says whether the values are `uint` or `int`.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a description of the enum with the name $name. An enum has no methods of its own, so this is the way to read the list of its cases.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The full name of the enum, with its namespace and with no \ at the start. Status::class gives this name.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Reflect\EnumInfo for that enum. The result is null if the program has no enum with that name, and also for the name of a class.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the full name of the enum.
doc.returnHtml: The name that was passed to of, with its namespace. You can pass it to of again to get a description of the same enum.

doc.shortHtml: Every case the enum declares, by name.
doc.returnHtml: One string per case, sorted by the value of the case from the smallest to the largest. Two cases with the same value are sorted by name. The order is not the order of the declaration. An enum with no case gives an empty list.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value of one case of the enum.

params.name: case
params.descHtml: The name of the case, as cases gives it. The name is case-sensitive.

doc.returnHtml: The value of the case. It is a uint if isUnsigned returns true, and an int otherwise. Use as uint or as int to store it in a variable of that type.

errors.descHtml: The enum has no case with that name. Use cases to get the names that exist.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether the values of the enum's cases are uint or int.
doc.returnHtml: true for an enum declared with : uint. false for an enum declared with : int or with no type, because an enum with no type is an int enum.

classes.summaryHtml: One enum, as Core\Reflect\EnumInfo::of returns it for the enum's name. cases lists the names of its cases, valueOf returns the value of one case, and isUnsigned says whether the values are uint or int.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\MethodInfo
classes.summary: One method of a class, as `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::methods` returns it. `name` and `isPublic` describe the declaration. `parameterCount` and `parameters` describe what the method takes.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the name of the method.
doc.returnHtml: The name as the class declares it, with no class name and no parentheses. A constructor is named constructor. You can pass the name to Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::hasMethod and Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::call.

doc.shortHtml: Tells you whether code outside the class may call the method.
doc.returnHtml: true for a public method, and false for a protected or private method. Those methods are still in the list that Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::methods returns. If isPublic returns false, Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::call from outside the class throws a LogicError.

doc.shortHtml: Returns how many parameters the method declares.
doc.returnHtml: The number of parameters, as a uint. $this is not counted. The number is also correct for a method the compiler adds, where parameters returns an empty array.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the parameters of the method, in the order they are written.
doc.returnHtml: One Core\Reflect\ParameterInfo for each parameter. $this is not included. For a method the compiler adds, such as the constructor of LogicError, the array is empty. parameterCount still returns how many arguments that method takes.

classes.summaryHtml: One method of a class, as Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::methods returns it. name and isPublic describe the declaration. parameterCount and parameters describe what the method takes.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\ParameterInfo
classes.summary: One parameter of a method, as `Core\Reflect\MethodInfo::parameters` returns it. `name` returns the name of the parameter, and `type` returns its declared type.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the name of the parameter.
doc.returnHtml: The name as the method declares it, without the $. This is the name you write for a named argument. A promoted constructor parameter has the same name as its property.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the declared type of the parameter, written the way the method writes it.
doc.returnHtml: The type as text, such as int, ?int, array<string> or App\User. A parameter declared in a source file always has a type, so the result is text. The result is null only if no type is known for the parameter. To check the type of a value, use Core\Reflect::typeOf.

classes.summaryHtml: One parameter of a method, as Core\Reflect\MethodInfo::parameters returns it. name returns the name of the parameter, and type returns its declared type.

classes.name: Core\Reflect\PropertyInfo
classes.summary: One property of a class, as `Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::properties` returns it. `name` and `isPublic` describe the declaration. `type` returns the type the property is declared with.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the name of the property.
doc.returnHtml: The name as the class declares it, with no $ and no class name. You can pass the name to Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::hasProperty, Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::get and Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::set.

doc.shortHtml: Tells you whether code outside the class may read and write the property.
doc.returnHtml: true for a public property, and false for a protected or private property. Those properties are still in the list that Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::properties returns. If isPublic returns false, Core\Reflect\ClassInfo::get from outside the class throws a RuntimeError.
