errors.descHtml: A capture decodes to bytes that are not valid UTF-8. The message names the capture and the position of the first bad byte.

doc.shortHtml: Lists the HTTP methods that the routes of $path accept, in the order the routes are declared. Use it when Core\Request::route() returns null, to choose between a 404 and a 405.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path, with no query string. The path of a request already has its mount prefix removed.

doc.returnHtml: The methods, each one once. An empty array means that no route has this path, so the status is 404. Otherwise the status is 405, and the array is the list for the Allow header. A path does not match when a capture is not a valid int, uint, decimal or Core\Uuid for its handler parameter, or is not one of the values its parameter allows.

doc.shortHtml: Calls the method of the route that the request matched. First, $gate->allows() checks the request. When no route method runs, dispatch sets the status and calls $gate->refused(). When the method throws an error, dispatch sets the status 500 and calls $gate->failed().

params.name: gate
params.descHtml: An instance of your class that implements Core\Router\Gate.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The route method or the gate writes the response, for example with echo or Core\Response::html. When the gate implements Core\Router\Responder, dispatch passes the value that a route method returns to $gate->respond(). Otherwise dispatch does not send that value. Each value captured from the path goes to the method parameter with the same name. An error that refused(), failed() or respond() throws is thrown by dispatch.

errors.descHtml: When the program has no #[Route]. When the program is not handling a request, for example a command-line program, a job or a test. When the route method has a parameter that no value in the path fills, such as a #[Query] parameter or an optional capture that the path does not have.

classes.summaryHtml:
The routes of your program. url(), urlAbsolute() and urlSigned() build a link to the route of a method. match() and methodsFor() check a path against the routes, and signedRoute() checks the signature of a signed link. dispatch() calls the method of the route that the request matched.

Core\Router::url builds a link to the route of a method, written Users::show with no (...): each {capture} in the path is substituted from $params, percent-encoded into its own segment, and $params may be left out for a route with no captures. It is only meaningful in a program that declares routes — the attributes chapter owns the declaration, and every #[Core\Route] needs a sibling #[Core\Access]. A method written directly in the code is checked while compiling, and a method with no route is a compile error. A method from a variable, such as an array<callable> or $users->show(...), is checked while the program runs, and the call throws an error when it has no route. A $params array missing a capture or carrying a key that is neither a capture nor a handler parameter declared #[Core\Query] is a compile error. A key that is declared #[Core\Query] becomes the link's query string, /users/7?page=2. urlAbsolute is url with the [[app]] origin from nvs.toml in front, and throws RuntimeError when none is configured.

methodsFor asks the table the other question, the one Core\Request::route() leaves open when it answers null: which verbs does this path claim? An empty array means no route claims it at all — the 404 — and a non-empty one is the list an Allow: header spells alongside a 405. Both forms of a terminal {page?} answer the same verbs, so /posts and /posts/3 are never a 404 and a 405 for one route. Nothing about it is a request: it is asked of the table, about a path, and the program decides what to send.

[[app]]
root = "."
origin = "https://example.test"
<?nvs
class Users
{
    #[Core\Route(path: '/users', method: Core\Http\Method::Get)]
    #[Core\Access(allow: Core\Audience::Public)]
    public function index(): string
    {
        return 'every user';
    }

    #[Core\Route(path: '/users/{id}', method: Core\Http\Method::Get)]
    #[Core\Access(allow: Core\Audience::Public)]
    public function show(uint $id): string
    {
        return 'user ' . $id;
    }

    #[Core\Route(path: '/users/{id}/files/{path...}', method: Core\Http\Method::Get)]
    #[Core\Access(allow: Core\Audience::Public)]
    public function file(uint $id, string $path): string
    {
        return $path;
    }
}

echo Core\Router::url(Users::index), "\n";
echo Core\Router::url(Users::show, ['id' => 7]), "\n";
echo Core\Router::url(Users::file, ['id' => 7, 'path' => 'a b/c.txt']), "\n";
echo Core\Router::urlAbsolute(Users::show, ['id' => 7]), "\n";
/users
/users/7
/users/7/files/a%20b/c.txt
https://example.test/users/7

classes.name: Core\Router\Match
classes.summary: The route that a path matched. `Core\Request::route()` returns the match of the request being served, and `Core\Router::match()` returns the match of a path you choose. `is()` checks which method the route belongs to. `params()` and `param()` return the values captured from the path, and `method()` returns the route's HTTP method. `accessAs<E>()` returns the route's access rule as a case of the enum `E`, and `access()` returns the same rule as its name. `attribute<T>()` returns an attribute of the route's method.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether the matched route belongs to a method. You write the method the way Core\Router::url takes it: $match->is(Shop::show).

params.name: route
params.descHtml: A method reference, such as Shop::show. A method that you write here must have a #[Route], or the program does not compile.

doc.returnHtml: true when the route belongs to this method, and false otherwise. A method with two #[Route]s, one for each HTTP method, gives true for both.

errors.descHtml: When $route is a variable and its method has no #[Route].

doc.shortHtml: Returns every value captured from the path, in the order of the path. Each key is the capture's name.
doc.returnHtml: An array of the captures. Each value is already percent-decoded, so %20 is a space. Each value has the type of its handler parameter: {id} read by uint $id is a number. A string capture is tainted, because the request sent it. An optional capture that the path does not have is not in the array. A route with no captures returns an empty array.

doc.shortHtml: Returns one value captured from the path, found by its name. It is the same value that params() has under that key.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The capture's name as the route's path writes it, without the braces.

doc.returnHtml: The capture, with the type of its handler parameter. The result is null when the route has no capture with this name, and when an optional {name?} is not in the path.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the HTTP method of the matched route. A handler with two #[Route] attributes uses it to see which of the two matched.
doc.returnHtml: The Core\Http\Method case written in the route's method:. A HEAD request matches a Get route, so the result is Core\Http\Method::Get.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the access rule of the matched route: the full name of the constant in its #[Access(allow: …)]. The server does not check it for you. A program that calls the route's handler checks it once, before that call.
doc.returnHtml: The name with its namespace, such as Core\Audience::Public or App\Role::Admin. Not tainted: it is the program's own text. Every route of a compiled program has one, so treat null as access denied.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the access rule of the matched route as a case of the enum you write between < and >. $match->accessAs<App\Role>() returns App\Role::Admin for a route with #[Access(allow: App\Role::Admin)]. Compare the result with a case, such as == Core\Audience::Public.
doc.returnHtml: The case of that enum, or null when the route's rule is not a case of that enum. Treat null as access denied. The type argument must be an enum.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the attribute of the route's method that has the shape you write between < and >. For a method with #[{ seconds: 60 }], $match->attribute<{ seconds: int }>() returns { seconds: 60 }. A gate uses it to read a setting for one route.
doc.returnHtml: The attribute as an object of that shape, or null when the method has no attribute with every field of the shape. The type argument must be a shape. Two matching attributes on one method do not compile.

classes.summaryHtml:
The route that a path matched. Core\Request::route() returns the match of the request being served, and Core\Router::match() returns the match of a path you choose. is() checks which method the route belongs to. params() and param() return the values captured from the path, and method() returns the route's HTTP method. accessAs<E>() returns the route's access rule as a case of the enum E, and access() returns the same rule as its name. attribute<T>() returns an attribute of the route's method.

A Core\Router\Match is what Core\Request::route() answers (null when nothing in the route table claimed this method and path); it is never constructed by hand. The server matches the incoming request against the compiled table once, before any of the program runs, and this is that result travelling on the request — so a handler never matches its own path a second time. Matching is not dispatching: nothing here calls the annotated method, and a match has nothing that can be called. The program calls the method itself, after it checks which method matched with is(); the attributes chapter shows that check, and how the program sends the 404 and the 405.

is(Shop::show) returns true when the route belongs to that method. You write the method the way Core\Router::url takes it: Class::method with no (...), for a static or an instance method. A method from a variable, such as an array<callable> or $shop->show(...), is checked while the program runs, and is throws an error when that method has no route. params() is every capture the path filled, keyed by the parameter it binds, and param() is that array read at one key — null for a name the route does not declare, including an optional {name?} the request left off. A capture is tainted string where the route declared string, still percent-encoded, and the int, uint, decimal or Core\Uuid the match already converted where it declared one of those, so a handler never parses a segment the router has parsed already — and a segment that would not convert did not match the route in the first place.

access() is the route's #[Core\Access(allow: …)] as a string: the full name of the constant, such as Core\Audience::Public or App\Role::Admin. The server does not enforce it. A program that calls route methods checks it once, before the switch, so the check also covers a route added later. Treat null as access denied. method() is the verb the matched #[Core\Route] declares, which tells apart the routes of one method that serves several verbs.

Reading it needs a request. Off the command line — and in a scheduled script, a job worker or a test — there is none, and the reader refuses rather than answering null, because "no request arrived" and "nothing matched" are different facts.

<?nvs
try {
    Core\Request::route();
} catch (LogicError $why) {
    echo "no request here\n";
}
no request here

classes.name: Core\Script
classes.summary: The script that is running now. `args()` returns the value the script was started with. `onExit()` adds a function that runs when the script ends, and `finish()` ends the script at once.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value that this script was started with. The parent script writes it as spawn script … with(args: …), and this script receives a copy.
doc.returnHtml: The value the parent passed, with the same shape. It is null when the parent gave no args:, and in the first script, which no other script started.

doc.shortHtml: Adds a function that runs when this script ends. It runs at a normal end, after exit, after Core\Script::finish() and after an exception that nothing caught. The functions run once each, in the order they were added. A FATAL error and a cancelled script run none of them.

params.name: hook
params.descHtml: The function to run. It receives one Core\Script\ExitReport that describes the ending, and its return value is not used. It may also take no parameter. If it throws an error, the error is logged and the next function still runs.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The list belongs to this request only. Adding the same function twice runs it twice. A function added while the list runs is added to the end of the same list. A function cannot change the ending, because the report is fixed before the first one runs. exit or Core\Script::finish() inside one of these functions stops that function, and the error is logged as a RuntimeError.

doc.shortHtml: Ends this script at once. Every finally block between the call and the top of the script runs first. Then the functions added with Core\Script::onExit() run. A request handler calls it when its response is complete.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The call does not return, no code after it runs, and no catch block catches it. The Core\Script\ExitReport has the reason Finish, the status 0 and no error. On a server, the response that the handler set is sent, and work added with Core\Task::afterResponse still runs. Under nvs run, the script ends.

classes.summaryHtml: The script that is running now. args() returns the value the script was started with. onExit() adds a function that runs when the script ends, and finish() ends the script at once.

classes.name: Core\Script\ExitReport
classes.summary: Describes how a script ended. Each function added with `Core\Script::onExit()` receives one. `reason()` returns the kind of ending, `status()` returns the exit status, `error()` returns the exception that ended the script, if there was one, and `memoryPeak()` returns the most memory the script used. The values cannot change.

doc.shortHtml: How a script ended, as Core\Script\ExitReport::reason() returns it. A FATAL error and a cancelled script have no case, because they run no exit function.
Returns how the script ended, as a Core\Script\ExitReport::Reason case.
doc.returnHtml: Normal when the last statement ran, ExitCall after exit, UncaughtThrow after an exception that nothing caught, and Finish after Core\Script::finish().

doc.shortHtml: Returns the status that the process exits with.
doc.returnHtml: 0 for a normal end and after Core\Script::finish(). After exit($n), it is $n. After an exception that nothing caught, it is 1. The status is fixed before the first function runs.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the exception that ended the script, if there was one.
doc.returnHtml: When the reason is UncaughtThrow, the Throwable that nothing caught, with its own class, message and backtrace. For every other ending, null.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the most memory the script used while it ran, in bytes. This is the same number Core\Budget::memoryPeak() returns.
doc.returnHtml: The highest number of bytes the script used at one time, read when the script ended. It is read before the first function runs, so memory a function uses does not change it.

classes.summaryHtml: Describes how a script ended. Each function added with Core\Script::onExit() receives one. reason() returns the kind of ending, status() returns the exit status, error() returns the exception that ended the script, if there was one, and memoryPeak() returns the most memory the script used. The values cannot change.

classes.name: Core\Script\Handle
classes.summary: A script that `spawn script` started. The only thing you can do with it is `await` it, which waits until that script ends.
classes.summaryHtml:
A script that spawn script started. The only thing you can do with it is await it, which waits until that script ends.

Core\Script\Handle is the value spawn script 'file.nvs' answers: the name of a child script already running in its own isolated memory. It has no members. The only thing to do with one is await it, which waits for the child and answers its result — ok, output, value and error — and a second await on the same handle throws LogicError, because the first one collected the child. A child's own failure arrives as ok being false, never as a throw in the parent. Spawning needs the script.spawn capability from nvs.toml; the construct, its with(...) options and the result's fields are in concurrency.

[[app]]
entry = "main.nvs"

[app.capabilities.script]
spawn = true
<?nvs
echo 'child says hello';
return 6 * 7;
<?nvs
var $job = spawn script 'child.nvs' with(output: 'capture');
echo 'spawned', "\n";

var $done = await $job;
echo 'ok=', $done->ok ? 'true' : 'false', "\n";
echo 'output=', $done->output, "\n";
echo 'value=', $done->value as int, "\n";

try {
    var $again = await $job;
} catch (LogicError $twice) {
    echo 'a handle is awaited once', "\n";
}
spawned
ok=true
output=child says hello
value=42
a handle is awaited once

classes.name: Core\Secret
classes.summary: A `secret` value cannot be printed, logged or sent. `reveal()` and `revealBytes()` return it as a plain `string` or `bytes`. Each call needs a reason, which says why this line may use the secret.

doc.shortHtml: Returns a secret string as a plain string. Use it only on the line that must print, send or store the secret.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The secret text. A plain string is also allowed, and is returned unchanged.

params.name: reason
params.descHtml: Why this line needs the secret. It is for the people who read the code, and the program never reads it. A secret value is not allowed here.

doc.returnHtml: The same text, as a string. If $value was also tainted, the result is still tainted.

doc.shortHtml: Returns secret bytes as plain bytes, such as a key the program must save. It works like reveal(), for bytes.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The secret bytes. Plain bytes are also allowed, and are returned unchanged.

params.name: reason
params.descHtml: Why this line needs the secret. It is for the people who read the code, and the program never reads it. A secret value is not allowed here.

doc.returnHtml: The same bytes, as bytes. If $value was also tainted, the result is still tainted.

classes.summaryHtml:
A secret value cannot be printed, logged or sent. reveal() and revealBytes() return it as a plain string or bytes. Each call needs a reason, which says why this line may use the secret.

Core\Secret::reveal answers its operand with the secret qualifier dropped, and ::revealBytes does the same one base over. A secret value is refused at every sink that would disclose it — echo and print, an interpolation, Core\Json::encode, Core\Serialize::encode, a spawn script boundary, a Throwable message, a debug dump — and each of those refusals tells you to call this. That is the whole design: there is no generic unwrap(), because a catch-all invites false confidence. Disclosure is a line you write, at the one call site where handing the secret over is the point, and grep finds every one of them.

The second argument is that reason, written for the next reader. Nothing consumes it at run time.

Revealing removes secret and nothing else. A value that was also tainted still is: where the value came from is a different question from who may see it, so Core\Secret::reveal over a secret tainted string answers a tainted string and the sinks that refuse untrusted input still refuse it. Revealing a value that was never secret is the identity and is legal — refusing it would cost a diagnostic and prevent no exposure.

<?nvs
secret string $token = 'hunter2';
secret bytes $key = 'raw-key' as bytes;

// Without these two lines, every `echo` below is a compile error naming
// `rule:security/secret-sinks-refuse`'s terminal sink.
string $revealed = Core\Secret::reveal($token, 'this command exists to print the token');
bytes $raw = Core\Secret::revealBytes($key, 'the signer takes the key as bytes');

echo $revealed, "\n";
echo "Bearer {$revealed}\n";
echo Core\Bytes::length($raw), "\n";

// Nothing is normalized on the way through: the value that comes back is the
// value that went in.
secret string $padded = '  spaced  ';
echo '[', Core\Secret::reveal($padded, 'the padding is part of the credential'), "]\n";
hunter2
Bearer hunter2
7
[  spaced  ]

classes.name: Core\Serialize
classes.summary: Turns a value into `bytes` and back. `encode()` writes the bytes, and `decode()` builds the same value again from them. Use it to save a value in a file or a cache and read it later.

doc.shortHtml: Turns a value into bytes that decode() can read back. The value can be a number, a string, an array or an object, and it can contain other arrays and objects.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to turn into bytes. Two places that point to the same object still point to one object after decode().

doc.returnHtml: The bytes. They are tainted when $value can contain text from outside the program. That is a tainted string, or a mixed or object value, anywhere inside it. In that case, call Core\Taint::assertTrustedBytes on the bytes before decode().

errors.descHtml: $value contains a callable, an open file or connection, or an object with a secret property. It is also thrown when arrays and objects are nested more than 256 levels deep.

doc.shortHtml: Builds the value again from the bytes that encode() returned. It reads only this format. Bytes that came from outside the program, such as a request body, are tainted, and a call with them does not compile.

params.name: payload
params.descHtml: The bytes that encode() returned. If they are tainted and your program wrote them itself, call Core\Taint::assertTrustedBytes on them first.

doc.returnHtml: The value. An object in it is a new object of the class with the same name in this program, and its constructor does not run.

errors.descHtml: $payload was not written by encode(), is incomplete, or has extra bytes at the end. It is also thrown when it names a class this program does not have, or a class whose properties are different now.

classes.summaryHtml:
Turns a value into bytes and back. encode() writes the bytes, and decode() builds the same value again from them. Use it to save a value in a file or a cache and read it later.

Core\Serialize::encode copies the whole value graph under a value into bytes in Novis's own closed format, and decode rebuilds it: an object comes back as an instance of the class this program declares, its declared properties assigned directly — no constructor runs, and no hook method runs either. A cycle is preserved as a cycle. decode answers mixed, so narrow it with as; it refuses foreign bytes, another format version, and a class whose declared properties no longer match with ParseError, and encode throws LogicError on a callable.

<?nvs
class Slot
{
    public function constructor(public int $n)
    {}
}
class Ring
{
    public int $id = 0;
    public ?Ring $self;
    public function constructor(int $id)
    {
        $this->id = $id;
        $this->self = null;
    }
}

bytes $blob = Core\Serialize::encode(new Slot(7));
Slot $back = Core\Serialize::decode($blob) as Slot;
echo 'n=', $back->n, "\n";

var $ring = new Ring(1);
$ring->self = $ring;
Ring $copy = Core\Serialize::decode(Core\Serialize::encode($ring)) as Ring;
echo 'cycle=', ($copy->self?->id ?? 0), "\n";

try {
    Core\Serialize::decode("O:4:\"Slot\":1:{s:1:\"n\";i:7;}" as bytes);
} catch (ParseError $e) {
    echo "refused\n";
}
n=7
cycle=1
refused

classes.name: Core\Server
classes.summary: Tells a program about the server it runs under. `isDraining()` returns `true` when the server has started to shut down. `traceId()` returns the id of the current request.

doc.shortHtml: Returns true when the server has started to shut down. From then on, the server accepts no new connections and finishes the requests it already has.
doc.returnHtml: true after the server stopped accepting new connections. false while it still accepts them. A program that no server runs, such as a command-line program, always gets false.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the id of the current request. Every request has one. The server writes the same id into its log lines and into the traceresponse header of the response.
doc.returnHtml: 32 lower-case hexadecimal characters. If the request came with a traceparent header, the id is the one in that header.

errors.descHtml: The program is not handling a request. This is the case in a command-line program or a test.

classes.summaryHtml: Tells a program about the server it runs under. isDraining() returns true when the server has started to shut down. traceId() returns the id of the current request.

classes.name: Core\Session
classes.summary: Keeps values for one visitor from one request to the next. Call `start()` first, then use `get()` and `set()`. By default, the values are saved in a SQLite file in the data folder. `[session] backend = "shared"` saves them in the shared cache instead.

doc.shortHtml: Opens the session of this request. Call it once, before any other method of this class. The session identifier is read from the session cookie.

params.name: presented
params.descHtml: The identifier to open. Leave it out to read it from the cookie named by [session] cookie, which is nvsid by default. If the store has no session under the identifier, a new, empty session is opened. This happens when the identifier expired, and when somebody made it up.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. After it, the other methods of this class can read and change the session. A new session is not saved, and no cookie is sent, until the program saves a value in it. Then the response sends its identifier in the session cookie.

errors.descHtml: The program is not handling a request. A command-line program, a job and a test have no session.

This request already called start(). It is also thrown when the server has no data folder for the default store. With [session] backend = "shared", it is thrown when [cache.shared] url is not set, or the program does not have the cache.shared capability.
The store cannot be reached. The user may still have a session there, so do not treat them as signed out.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value saved under one key in the session of this request.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The key to read. If the session has no value under it, the result is null. A key that was set to null gives the same result.

doc.returnHtml: The value saved under $key, or null. Reading does not change the session, so a request that only reads its session does not write it back to the store.

errors.descHtml: This request has not called start(), or it called destroy(). There is no session to read.
The saved session contains an object of a class this program does not declare. This happens when another program saved it.

doc.shortHtml: Saves a value under one key in the session of this request. If the key already has a value, it is replaced.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The key to save the value under.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to save: a string, a number, a bool, null, an array or an object. A tainted value (text that came from the request) is not allowed here, so the call does not compile.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The session is saved to the store once, when the request ends. The first value saved in a new session also sends the session cookie.

errors.descHtml: This request has not called start(), or it called destroy(). There is no session to save into. It is also thrown on the first save in a new session when [session] cookie is not a valid cookie name.
$value cannot be saved: it is a callable or a resource, or it contains one. It is also thrown on the first save in a new session after the response was sent, because the cookie cannot be sent then.
As get(), because set() reads the whole session first.

doc.shortHtml: Deletes one key and its value from the session of this request.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The key to delete. If the session has no value under it, remove() does not throw an error and the session does not change.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. After it, get() returns null for $key. The other keys keep their values. To delete every key, use clear().

errors.descHtml: This request has not called start(), or it called destroy(). There is no session to change.
As set(). The values that are left are saved again, and a value set() does not allow cannot be saved.
As get(), because remove() reads the whole session first.

doc.shortHtml: Removes every value from the session of this request. The session stays open and keeps its identifier.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The client keeps the same session cookie, and set() works again at once. To end the session completely, for example when a user signs out, use destroy().

errors.descHtml: This request has not called start(), or it called destroy(). There is no session to empty.

doc.shortHtml: Gives the session a new identifier and deletes the old one from the store. Call it when a user signs in, so an identifier that somebody else knew stops working.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The data in the session does not change. The response sends the new identifier in the session cookie. The old identifier no longer finds the session.

errors.descHtml: This request has not called start(), or it called destroy(). With [session] backend = "shared", it is also thrown when [cache.shared] url is not set or the program does not have the cache.shared capability. It is also thrown when [session] cookie is not a valid cookie name.
The store cannot be reached. The old identifier may still work, so do not treat the user as signed in.

doc.shortHtml: Ends the session of this request and deletes its data from the store. Call it when a user signs out.
doc.returnHtml: Nothing. After it, this request has no session. The other methods of this class throw a RuntimeError until you call start() again, and that call opens a new, empty session.

errors.descHtml: This request has not called start(), or it already called destroy(). With [session] backend = "shared", it is also thrown when [cache.shared] url is not set or the program does not have the cache.shared capability.
The store cannot be reached. The data is still in the store, and the session stays open, so you can try again.

members.name: setSecret
members.signature: setSecret(string $key, secret string $value, array<secret bytes> $keys): void

doc.shortHtml: Saves a secret, such as an access token, in the session of this request. The secret is encrypted with a key from $keys, so the store only sees encrypted bytes.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The key to save the secret under. get() returns null for this key. Only getSecret() with the same $keys can read the secret.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The secret to save, for example an access token or a refresh token of the user.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: A list of encryption keys, newest first. Core\Crypto::generateKey() creates one. The first key encrypts the secret.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The session is saved to the store once, when the request ends.

errors.descHtml: This request has not called start(), or it called destroy(). There is no session to save into.
$keys is empty, or its first key is not 32 bytes long.
As get(), because setSecret() reads the whole session first.

doc.shortHtml: Reads a secret that setSecret() saved in the session of this request. If the secret cannot be decrypted with $keys, the result is null.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The key the secret was saved under. A secret saved under one key cannot be read under another key.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: A list of encryption keys, newest first. Every key in the list is tried. When you add a new key at the front, secrets saved with the older keys can still be read.

doc.returnHtml: The secret saved under $key, or null. The result is null when nothing is saved under $key, when no key in $keys decrypts it, and when the saved bytes were changed. Reading does not change the session.

errors.descHtml: This request has not called start(), or it called destroy(). There is no session to read.
$keys is empty, or a key in it is not 32 bytes long.
As get(), because getSecret() reads the whole session first.

classes.summaryHtml: Keeps values for one visitor from one request to the next. Call start() first, then use get() and set(). By default, the values are saved in a SQLite file in the data folder. [session] backend = "shared" saves them in the shared cache instead.

classes.name: Core\Signal
classes.summary: Runs a function of your program when the process gets a signal to stop. The program can then finish its work cleanly. `Core\Server::isDraining()` tells whether a shutdown has started.

doc.shortHtml: Registers a function that runs when the process gets a signal to stop. The signal can come from Ctrl-C, from SIGTERM, or from the person who stops the server. The function runs once, between two statements. At that time Core\Server::isDraining() already returns true.

params.name: handler
params.descHtml: The function to run. It gets no arguments and returns nothing. Every stop signal has the same effect, so the function cannot tell which one arrived. If it throws an error or reaches the request's memory limit, the rest of it does not run.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. Each request has its own function, and a second call replaces the first. The function is deleted when the request ends, and other requests cannot see it. It cannot stop the shutdown or delay it.

classes.summaryHtml: Runs a function of your program when the process gets a signal to stop. The program can then finish its work cleanly. Core\Server::isDraining() tells whether a shutdown has started.

classes.name: Core\Signature
classes.summary: Signs a set of named values with a secret key, so your program can check later that nobody changed them. Signed links and password reset tokens are typical uses. The values are readable by anyone who has the token, so do not sign a secret.

members.name: sign
members.signature: sign(array<string> $payload, { keys: array<secret bytes>, until: ?Core\Time\Instant } $settings): string

doc.shortHtml: Signs $payload with the newest key in $settings.keys and returns a token. The token contains the payload, and Core\Signature::verify returns it again. The same payload, keys and until always give the same token.

params.name: payload
params.descHtml: The values to sign, each under a name. The order of the names is not signed. verify returns the values sorted by name.

params.name: settings
params.descHtml: The keys, and the time when the token stops being valid. You must write both.

shape.descHtml: The keys, newest first. $keys[0] signs the token. The older keys are there so that verify still accepts tokens made before you added a new key. A list of one key is [$key].
The time after which verify throws an error for this token. The time is part of the signed data, so nobody can change it. Write null for a token that never expires.

doc.returnHtml: The token. It contains only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, - and _, so you can put it in a URL or a cookie without escaping it. It is about 4/3 × (payload + 40) characters long.

errors.descHtml: $settings.keys is empty, or its first key is not 32 bytes long. Core\Crypto::generateKey() returns a key of the right length.

doc.shortHtml: Checks that $token was made by Core\Signature::sign with a key in $keys, and that it has not expired. It returns the signed payload, or throws an error. Every value in the payload is tainted (treated as input from outside). A signature shows who made the data. It does not show that the data is safe to use.

params.name: token
params.descHtml: The token as your program received it, for example from a URL. A tainted string is allowed here.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The keys you gave sign, newest first. A token made with any key in this list is accepted. A token made with a key you removed from the list is not.

doc.returnHtml: The signed payload, sorted by name. Every value is a tainted string.

errors.descHtml: $keys is empty, or one of its keys is not 32 bytes long.

$token was not made with any key in $keys. This includes a changed token, text that is not a token, and a token for a signed URL. All of these give the same message, so an attacker learns nothing from it. An expired token also throws RuntimeError, with a different message that gives the time it expired.

classes.summaryHtml: Signs a set of named values with a secret key, so your program can check later that nobody changed them. Signed links and password reset tokens are typical uses. The values are readable by anyone who has the token, so do not sign a secret.

classes.name: Core\SignedCookie
classes.summary: Stores a value in a cookie. The browser keeps the cookie, but cannot read or change the value. `seal` encrypts the value with a secret key, and `open` checks the cookie and returns the value again.

doc.shortHtml: Encrypts $value with the newest key in $keys and returns text for the cookie $name. Nobody without the key can read or change the value. Core\SignedCookie::open returns the value again for the same name.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The name of the cookie, such as cart. open needs the same name. A cookie sent back under another name does not open.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to store. open returns exactly this string.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The keys, newest first. $keys[0] encrypts the value. The older keys are there so that open still accepts cookies made before you added a new key. A list of one key is [$key].

doc.returnHtml: The cookie text. It contains only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, - and _, so a Set-Cookie header can carry it without escaping. It is about 4/3 × (length + 40) characters long. Each call returns different text for the same value, because each call adds new random bytes.

errors.descHtml: $keys is empty, or its first key is not 32 bytes long. Core\Crypto::generateKey() returns a key of the right length.
The request does not have enough memory left for the cookie.

members.name: open
members.signature: open(string $name, string $cookie, array<secret bytes> $keys): tainted string

doc.shortHtml: Checks that $cookie was made by Core\SignedCookie::seal for the cookie $name with a key in $keys, and returns the value stored in it. A changed cookie throws an error. The value is tainted (it counts as input from outside the program), because your program may have stored text that a visitor sent.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The name you gave seal. This is usually the name the cookie arrived with.

params.name: cookie
params.descHtml: The cookie text as your program received it from the request. A tainted string is allowed here.

params.name: keys
params.descHtml: The keys you gave seal, newest first. A cookie made with any key in this list is accepted. A cookie made with a key you removed from the list is not.

doc.returnHtml: The value that was given to seal, exactly as it was, as a tainted string.

errors.descHtml: $keys is empty, or a key that open tries is not 32 bytes long. open tries the keys in order and stops at the first one that opens the cookie.

$cookie was not made for $name with any key in $keys. This includes a changed cookie, an empty cookie, text that is not a cookie, a cookie made for another name, and a cookie made with a key you removed. All of these give the same message, so an attacker learns nothing from it.

classes.summaryHtml: Stores a value in a cookie. The browser keeps the cookie, but cannot read or change the value. seal encrypts the value with a secret key, and open checks the cookie and returns the value again.

classes.name: Core\Socket
classes.summary: A WebSocket connection from a client to your server. A request calls `upgrade` to turn itself into a connection that runs a script of its own. That script calls `current` to get the connection, then `receive` and `send` to talk to the client.

members.name: upgrade
members.signature: upgrade(string $entry, mixed $args = null, mixed $limits = null, ?array<string> $grants = null, ?string $on = null): void

doc.shortHtml: Turns this request into a WebSocket connection that runs $entry. The connection starts when the request ends. It runs separately and shares no memory with the request.

params.name: entry
params.descHtml: What the connection runs: the path of a file, the same as spawn script takes, or a static method written Chat::run. An anonymous function is not allowed, because the connection shares no values with the request.

params.name: args
params.descHtml: The values the connection starts with. They are copied into the connection. For a method, each value goes to the parameter with the same name. A tainted value is still tainted in the connection.

params.name: limits
params.descHtml: Lower limits for the connection, written as spawn script writes them: { memory: "8M", cpu_time: "2s" }. The keys are memory, cpu_time, wall_time, max_output and max_tasks. A limit higher than the server's own has no effect. The connection stops when it reaches one.

params.name: grants
params.descHtml: The capabilities the connection may use, such as ["fs.read"]. It gets only the names in this list that the request itself has. An empty list gives it none. Without this option, it gets what the request has.

params.name: on
params.descHtml: Where the connection runs. Only "here" is allowed, because the connection runs on the core that accepted the client. "worker" does not compile.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The call prepares the connection, and it starts when the request ends.

errors.descHtml: The request is not a WebSocket request. The $entry file is not granted by script.spawn or does not compile. Or this request already called upgrade.
An $args value cannot be copied into the connection: a resource, a secret, or an array nested too deep. For a method, $args is missing a parameter or has a name the method does not declare.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the WebSocket connection this script is running for. It is the first line of every script that Core\Socket::upgrade starts.
doc.returnHtml: The connection. Call receive and send on it to talk to the client. Each call returns a new object for the same connection, so compare what the client sends, not the objects.

errors.descHtml: The script is not running for a connection. An ordinary request, a spawn script child and a command line program all throw this.

doc.shortHtml: Waits for the next message and returns it. A message comes from the client, or from a topic this connection subscribed to.
doc.returnHtml: The next message, or null when the client has closed the connection. A connection script reads in a loop that stops at null. topic() on the message is null for a message from the client, and what the client sent is tainted. A connection that falls too far behind its topics is closed, and then this returns null too.

errors.descHtml: The script is not running for a connection, so there is no client to wait for.
The connection broke, or the client sent something the WebSocket protocol does not allow.

doc.shortHtml: Sends one text message to the client, and waits until it is written.

params.name: frame
params.descHtml: The text to send. The client receives it as one message. A tainted string is allowed, so you can send back what the client sent you.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing.

errors.descHtml: The script is not running for a connection, so there is no client to send to.
The connection broke, or the client stopped reading and the message could not be written in time. The wait always ends.

doc.shortHtml: Sends one binary message to the client, and waits until it is written. send is the same method for text.

params.name: frame
params.descHtml: The bytes to send. They are sent as they are, and nothing checks them.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing.

errors.descHtml: The script is not running for a connection, so there is no client to send to.
The connection broke, or the client stopped reading and the message could not be written in time, as for send.

classes.summaryHtml: A WebSocket connection from a client to your server. A request calls upgrade to turn itself into a connection that runs a script of its own. That script calls current to get the connection, then receive and send to talk to the client.

classes.name: Core\Socket\Message
classes.summary: One message on a WebSocket connection, as `Core\Socket::receive` returns it. A message from the client has `text` or `bytes`. A message from a topic has a `topic` and a `value`.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the name of the topic the message was published to.
doc.returnHtml: The topic name for a message from a topic. It is null for a message from the client. The name is not tainted, because your program chose it when it subscribed.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the text of a text message from the client.
doc.returnHtml: The text, exactly as the client sent it. It is tainted, because it comes from the client. It is null for a binary message and for a message from a topic.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the bytes of a binary message from the client.
doc.returnHtml: The bytes, exactly as the client sent them. They are tainted, because they come from the client. It is null for a text message and for a message from a topic.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value that was published to the topic.
doc.returnHtml: A copy of the published value. Changing the copy does not change the value the publisher has. It is null for a message from the client.

classes.summaryHtml: One message on a WebSocket connection, as Core\Socket::receive returns it. A message from the client has text or bytes. A message from a topic has a topic and a value.

classes.name: Core\Sse
classes.summary: An event stream from your server to a client, as a browser's `EventSource` reads it. A request calls `stream` to answer with events, or `upgrade` to start a script that keeps sending after the request ends. Code that did not open the stream calls `current` to get it, and `send` writes one event.

members.name: upgrade
members.signature: upgrade(string $entry, mixed $args = null, mixed $limits = null, ?array<string> $grants = null, ?string $on = null): void

doc.shortHtml: Responds to this request with an event stream that runs $entry in a new isolate. The isolate has its own memory, its own limits and its own capabilities. It shares nothing with the request except the values copied in from $args.

params.name: entry
params.descHtml: What the stream runs. It is a file path, or a static method written Feed::run. A file path is resolved and checked the same way as for spawn script. It cannot be an anonymous function. An anonymous function can capture variables, and an isolate shares only compiled code.

params.name: args
params.descHtml: The values the stream starts with. Each one goes to the entry's parameter of the same name. They are deep-copied into the isolate, so they are never shared references. A secret value is not allowed. A tainted value stays tainted in the isolate.

params.name: limits
params.descHtml: Lower limits for the stream, with the same syntax as for spawn script: { memory: "8M", cpu_time: "2s" }. The keys are memory, cpu_time, wall_time, max_output and max_tasks. A limit higher than the server's own has no effect. The stream stops when it reaches one.

params.name: grants
params.descHtml: The capabilities the stream may use, such as ["fs.read"]. It gets only the names in this list that the request itself has. An empty list gives it none. Without this option, it gets the capabilities of the request.

params.name: on
params.descHtml: Where the stream runs. Only "here" is allowed, because the stream runs on the core that accepted the client. "worker" does not compile.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The call itself opens the stream. A handler does not return it, because the return value of a handler is not used.

errors.descHtml: The program is not handling a request. This is true for every command-line program and every spawn script child. It is also thrown when script.spawn does not allow the $entry path, or the file does not compile. A second call in the same request also throws it.

An $args value cannot be copied into an isolate. Examples are a resource, or a secret that is not revealed. For a static method entry, it is also thrown when $args is missing one of the method's parameters or has a name the method does not have.

doc.shortHtml: Responds to this request with an event stream that ends when the request ends. The headers are sent as soon as you call it. Each event reaches the client when you send it.
doc.returnHtml: A Core\Sse to send events on. It is the same class that upgrade uses, so a helper function works with both. A browser's EventSource reconnects when this stream ends. Use this stream with fetch, or with a progress display that closes itself.

errors.descHtml: A status was set on this request before the stream was opened. An event stream always has status 200. It is also thrown when this response is already streaming a body, because a response has only one body.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the event stream this program is writing. It works for a stream opened by upgrade and for a stream opened by stream.
doc.returnHtml: The same Core\Sse that upgrade or stream returned. A helper function that takes one works with both kinds of stream.

errors.descHtml: The program is not writing an event stream. This is true for every command-line program and every spawn script child. It is also true for a request with an ordinary body. A streamed response body is not an event stream either.

doc.shortHtml: Waits for the next value published to a topic this stream subscribed to. It returns that value as one message.
doc.returnHtml: The next message, or null when the stream has ended. The null ends a while (var $msg = $sse->receive()) loop. A message has the published value and the name of its topic. A stream that falls too far behind also gets null. Its queue is full, so the stream is closed and publishers do not wait for it.

errors.descHtml: This stream was opened by stream, not by upgrade. It ends with the request, so no published value can reach it, and there is nothing to wait for.

doc.shortHtml: Sends one event to the client. The event has the data, an optional event name and an optional id. The client sends the id back when it reconnects.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The data the client receives. A string is sent as it is. Any other value is encoded as JSON, the same way as by Core\Json::encode. A tainted value is allowed. The data is cleaned and split into data: lines, so it cannot change any other field.

params.name: event
params.descHtml: The event name the client listens for, or null for the default message. An attacker could use this name to control the client. So a tainted value does not compile here.

params.name: id
params.descHtml: The id the client sends back in Last-Event-ID when it reconnects, or null for no id. A tainted value does not compile here, for the same reason. The server keeps no old events. To resume, your handler reads the header and uses your own event log.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The event is formatted and added to the response body.

errors.descHtml: $event or $id contains a line break or a NUL byte. Either one would end the event early and change what the client does. It is also thrown for an empty $data, because a client ignores an event with no data.

doc.shortHtml: Tells the client how long to wait before it reconnects. It is sent as a separate block, and the client sees no event.

params.name: after
params.descHtml: How long the client waits before it reconnects. It is sent in whole milliseconds. A wait shorter than one millisecond is sent as 0, without an error.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The block is added to the response body.

errors.descHtml: $after is negative. A wait cannot be shorter than zero.

classes.summaryHtml: An event stream from your server to a client, as a browser's EventSource reads it. A request calls stream to answer with events, or upgrade to start a script that keeps sending after the request ends. Code that did not open the stream calls current to get it, and send writes one event.

classes.name: Core\Sse\Message
classes.summary: One value that arrived on an event stream's script, returned by `Core\Sse->receive`. `topic` returns the name of the topic it was published to, and `value` returns what was published.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the topic this value was published to. It is one of the topics this stream subscribed to.
doc.returnHtml: The topic's name. It is never null, because every message on an event stream comes from a topic. Your program chose the name, not a client, so it is not tainted.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the value a publisher published to the topic. It is copied from the publisher's isolate, like every value sent between isolates.
doc.returnHtml: The published value. If it was tainted, it is still tainted. It is a copy, so a change to it does not change anything the publisher sees.

classes.summaryHtml: One value that arrived on an event stream's script, returned by Core\Sse->receive. topic returns the name of the topic it was published to, and value returns what was published.

classes.name: Core\Storage
classes.summary: Saves files by name in a folder that `nvs.toml` sets up as a disk. `put` writes a file, `get` reads it back, `delete` removes it and `list` returns the names on the disk. A name is one plain word such as `invoice-1042.pdf`, never a path.

members.name: put
members.signature: put(string $disk, string $key, bytes $contents, { overwrite?: bool }): void

doc.shortHtml: Saves $contents as the file $key on $disk. A file that is already there is replaced, unless overwrite is false.

params.name: disk
params.descHtml: The name of a [storage.<name>] block in nvs.toml. That block sets the folder the files are saved in. A tainted value is not allowed here, because the program chooses the disk and user input never does.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name of the file on the disk. It is 1 to 255 ASCII letters, digits, ., - and _, and it does not start with a .. A / or a \ throws an error, so a key never points into another folder.

params.name: contents
params.descHtml: The bytes to save. The whole value is written.

params.name: overwrite
params.descHtml: Whether a file that already has this key may be replaced. The default is true. With false, put throws an IOError if the key is already used.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The file is on the disk when put returns.

errors.descHtml: No [storage.<name>] block with this name sets a root. Or $key is not a valid key. Or the fs.read or fs.write capability does not include the file's path.
The file could not be written. This includes overwrite: false for a key that is already used.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the file $key on $disk. If there is no file with that key, the result is null.

params.name: disk
params.descHtml: The name of a [storage.<name>] block in nvs.toml. That block sets the folder the files are saved in. A tainted value is not allowed here, because the program chooses the disk and user input never does.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name of the file on the disk. It is 1 to 255 ASCII letters, digits, ., - and _, and it does not start with a .. A / or a \ throws an error, so a key never points into another folder.

doc.returnHtml: The file's bytes, or null if nothing was saved under this key. The bytes are tainted, because a visitor may have written the file.

errors.descHtml: No [storage.<name>] block with this name sets a root. Or $key is not a valid key. Or the fs.read or fs.write capability does not include the file's path.
The file is there, but it could not be read.

doc.shortHtml: Deletes the file $key from $disk.

params.name: disk
params.descHtml: The name of a [storage.<name>] block in nvs.toml. That block sets the folder the files are saved in. A tainted value is not allowed here, because the program chooses the disk and user input never does.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The name of the file on the disk. It is 1 to 255 ASCII letters, digits, ., - and _, and it does not start with a .. A / or a \ throws an error, so a key never points into another folder.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing. The file is gone when delete returns.

errors.descHtml: No [storage.<name>] block with this name sets a root. Or $key is not a valid key. Or the fs.read or fs.write capability does not include the file's path.
There is no file with this key, or it could not be deleted. Deleting a missing file throws this error, so a typo in a key is reported.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the keys of the files on $disk, sorted by their bytes. get can read every key in the result.

params.name: disk
params.descHtml: The name of a [storage.<name>] block in nvs.toml. That block sets the folder the files are saved in. A tainted value is not allowed here, because the program chooses the disk and user input never does.

params.name: prefix
params.descHtml: Only keys that start with this text are returned. The default is empty, which returns every key. A prefix that is not empty and not a valid key throws an error, because no key can start with it.

doc.returnHtml: The matching keys, sorted. An empty array if no file matches. Only regular files with a valid key are listed. A folder, a symlink and a file with any other name are not in the result.

errors.descHtml: No [storage.<name>] block with this name sets a root. Or prefix is not empty and not a valid key. Or the fs.read capability does not include the disk's folder.
The disk's folder could not be read. It does not exist, or it is not a folder.

classes.summaryHtml: Saves files by name in a folder that nvs.toml sets up as a disk. put writes a file, get reads it back, delete removes it and list returns the names on the disk. A name is one plain word such as invoice-1042.pdf, never a path.

classes.name: Core\Str
classes.summary: Functions for text: measure it, search it, cut it, change its case and build new strings. Every position and length counts characters the way a person sees them, so an accented letter or an emoji counts as one.

doc.shortHtml: The four Unicode normal forms (UAX #15) that Core\Str::normalize can change text into. A form is either composed or decomposed, and either canonical or compatibility.

Counts the graphemes in $s. A grapheme is what a person counts as one character, so a letter with a combining accent counts once. Every Core\Str function counts in graphemes. The result is never a byte count.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to measure.

doc.returnHtml: The number of graphemes. The empty string gives 0.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the one character at position $index of $s. A character is what a person sees as one letter, so "é" is one character.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to read from.

params.name: index
params.descHtml: The position of the character. The first character is at 0. A negative position counts from the end, so -1 is the last character.

doc.returnHtml: A string with exactly one character in it.

errors.descHtml: There is no character at $index. The position is at or past the length of $s, counting from either end.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s is the empty string "". A string of spaces is not empty, and neither is "0".

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to check.

doc.returnHtml: true when $s has no characters, otherwise false.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $needle appears anywhere in $haystack.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The string to search in.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The text to search for. The search is case-sensitive.

doc.returnHtml: true when $needle is in $haystack, otherwise false. An empty $needle is in every string, so the result is true.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s starts with $prefix.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to check.

params.name: prefix
params.descHtml: The text $s must start with. The check is case-sensitive.

doc.returnHtml: true when $s starts with $prefix, otherwise false. An empty $prefix is at the start of every string, so the result is true.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s ends with $suffix.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to check.

params.name: suffix
params.descHtml: The text $s must end with. The check is case-sensitive.

doc.returnHtml: true when $s ends with $suffix, otherwise false. An empty $suffix is at the end of every string, so the result is true.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the part of $s that starts at $offset and has $length characters. Positions count characters as a person sees them, so "é" is one character.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to take the part from.

params.name: offset
params.descHtml: Where the part starts. The first character is at 0. A negative offset counts from the end.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: How many characters to take. A negative length stops that many characters before the end. null takes everything to the end.

doc.returnHtml: The part as a new string. It is "" when the part is empty or the offset is past the end. $s does not change.

members.name: indexOf
members.signature: indexOf(string $haystack, string $needle, { from?: int, caseInsensitive?: bool }): ?uint

doc.shortHtml: Finds the first place where $needle appears in $haystack and returns its position. The first character is position 0.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The string to search in.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The string to search for. An empty needle matches where the search starts.

params.name: from
params.descHtml: The position where the search starts. A negative value counts from the end. The default is 0.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: When true, upper-case and lower-case letters match each other. Each character is compared by its lower-case form, so ß does not match SS. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The position of the first match at or after from, counted in characters as Core\Str::length counts them. You can pass it to Core\Str::slice. The result is null when there is no match.

members.name: lastIndexOf
members.signature: lastIndexOf(string $haystack, string $needle, { before?: int, caseInsensitive?: bool }): ?uint

doc.shortHtml: Finds the last place where $needle appears in $haystack and returns its position. The first character is position 0.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The string to search in.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The string to search for.

params.name: before
params.descHtml: Searches only the characters in front of this position, so a match must end here or earlier. A negative position counts back from the end. The default is the whole string.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: When true, upper-case and lower-case letters count as the same. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The position of the last match, or null when there is none. Matches may overlap, so lastIndexOf("aaa", "aa") returns 1.

doc.shortHtml: Counts how many times $needle appears in $haystack.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The string to search in.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The text to count. The search is case-sensitive. It must not be empty.

doc.returnHtml: The number of times $needle appears, or 0 when it does not appear. Matches do not overlap, so countOf("aaa", "aa") is 1.

errors.descHtml: $needle is empty.

members.name: compare
members.signature: compare(string $a, string $b, { caseInsensitive?: bool, natural?: bool }): int

doc.shortHtml: Compares two strings to sort them.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The first string.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The second string.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: When true, upper and lower case letters are equal. ß and SS are still different. The default is false.

params.name: natural
params.descHtml: When true, digits inside the strings are compared as numbers, so "img2" comes before "img12". The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: -1 when $a comes first, 0 when the two are equal, and 1 when $b comes first.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the part of $s before the first $needle, without the needle. With { last: true }, it cuts at the last $needle.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to cut.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The separator to cut at. The search is case-sensitive. The needle is not part of the result.

params.name: last
params.descHtml: When true, cuts at the last needle. The default is false, which cuts at the first one.

doc.returnHtml: The text before the needle. If the needle is not in $s, the result is null. If the needle is at the start, the result is an empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the part of $s after the first $needle, without the needle. With { last: true }, it cuts at the last $needle.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to cut.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The separator to cut at. The search is case-sensitive. The needle is not part of the result.

params.name: last
params.descHtml: When true, cuts at the last needle. The default is false, which cuts at the first one.

doc.returnHtml: The text after the needle. If the needle is not in $s, the result is null. If the needle is at the end, the result is an empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Joins the strings in $parts into one string, with $separator between each two neighbouring strings.

params.name: parts
params.descHtml: The strings to join, in the order of the array.

params.name: separator
params.descHtml: The text that goes between two neighbouring strings. The default is the empty string "".

doc.returnHtml: The joined string. An empty array gives "".

doc.shortHtml: Splits $s into parts at every place where $separator is found.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to split.

params.name: separator
params.descHtml: The text to split at. Upper and lower case are different. It must not be empty.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: A positive limit gives at most that many parts. The last part contains the rest of the string. A negative limit deletes that many parts from the end. 0 gives the whole string as one part. The default is no limit.

doc.returnHtml: The parts in order, without the separator. The empty string gives [""]. A negative limit that deletes every part gives [].

errors.descHtml: $separator is empty.

doc.shortHtml: Splits a string with holes into its text and its holes.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: A string with holes, such as string<propertyPath<Order>>. Each {name} in it is a hole.

doc.returnHtml: The text and the holes in order. The array starts and ends with text, and text and holes take turns. So an even index is text and an odd index is a hole. Text can be the empty string. In text, {{ is already { and }} is already }. If $text is tainted, the text is tainted too. The holes are not.

doc.shortHtml: Divides $s into pieces of $size characters each. A piece never cuts a character in half.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to divide.

params.name: size
params.descHtml: How many characters each piece has. It must be at least 1.

doc.returnHtml: The pieces in order. Only the last piece can be shorter than $size. The result is [] for the empty string.

errors.descHtml: $size is 0.

doc.shortHtml: Splits $s into its lines. A line ends at \n, at \r\n or at \r, on every system.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to split.

doc.returnHtml: One string for each line, without its line break. A line break at the very end does not add an empty line. An empty line in the middle is kept as "". An empty string gives [].

doc.shortHtml: Divides $s into its characters, the way a person counts them. An accented letter, a flag or an emoji with a skin tone is one character, even when it is several code points. These are the characters Core\Str::length counts.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to divide.

doc.returnHtml: One string for each character, in order. An empty string gives [].

doc.shortHtml: Lists the code points of $s. A code point is the number Unicode gives to one symbol. One character a person sees can be several code points.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to read.

doc.returnHtml: One uint for each code point, in order. Each number is between 0 and 0x10FFFF and is never a surrogate. The result is [] for the empty string.

members.name: replace
members.signature: replace(string $s, string $search, string $replacement, { caseInsensitive?: bool, limit?: uint }): string

doc.shortHtml: Replaces every occurrence of $search in $s with $replacement. Matches are found from left to right and do not overlap. The new text is not searched again.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to change.

params.name: search
params.descHtml: The text to find. An empty $search matches nothing.

params.name: replacement
params.descHtml: The text that replaces each match.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: If true, upper-case and lower-case letters match each other, so "A" finds "a". The default is false.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: The most matches to replace, counted from the left. 0 replaces nothing. The default is every match.

doc.returnHtml: The changed string. If nothing matched, the result is $s unchanged.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces several texts in $s in one call. Each key of $pairs is a text to find, and its value is the text that replaces it. The string is read once, from left to right. Where several keys match at the same place, the longest one is used. The new text is not searched again.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to change.

params.name: pairs
params.descHtml: The replacements. Each key is the text to find, and its value is the text that replaces it. An empty key is ignored.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: If true, upper-case and lower-case letters match each other. If two keys then match the same text, the key written first is used. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The changed string. If $pairs is empty or nothing matched, the result is $s unchanged.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces a part of $s with $replacement. The part is the text Core\Str::slice returns for the same $offset and $length.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to change.

params.name: offset
params.descHtml: The character where the part starts. 0 is the first character. A negative offset counts from the end.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: How many characters the part has. A negative length stops that many characters before the end. null means the part runs to the end.

params.name: replacement
params.descHtml: The text that replaces the part. "" deletes the part.

doc.returnHtml: The changed string. If the part is empty, for example with a $length of 0, $replacement is inserted at $offset.

doc.shortHtml: Adds copies of $padding before $s until the result is $length characters long.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to pad.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: The length to reach, in characters as a person counts them.

params.name: padding
params.descHtml: The text to add. The last copy is cut short when only part of it fits. The default is one space.

doc.returnHtml: The padded string. If $s already has $length characters or more, it is returned unchanged.

errors.descHtml: $padding is empty and $s is shorter than $length. It is also thrown when the result is larger than this process can hold.

doc.shortHtml: Adds copies of $padding after $s until the result is $length characters long.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to pad.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: The length to reach, in characters as a person counts them.

params.name: padding
params.descHtml: The text to add. The last copy is cut short when only part of it fits. The default is one space.

doc.returnHtml: The padded string. If $s already has $length characters or more, it is returned unchanged.

errors.descHtml: $padding is empty and $s is shorter than $length. It is also thrown when the result is larger than this process can hold.

doc.shortHtml: Removes the given characters from both ends of $s.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to trim.

params.name: characters
params.descHtml: The characters to remove, in any order. a..z is the three characters a, . and z. The default is space, tab, newline, carriage return, NUL and vertical tab.

doc.returnHtml: $s without those characters at its start and its end. The middle of $s is not changed.

doc.shortHtml: Removes the given characters from the start of $s.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to trim.

params.name: characters
params.descHtml: The characters to remove, in any order. a..z is the three characters a, . and z. The default is space, tab, newline, carriage return, NUL and vertical tab.

doc.returnHtml: $s without those characters at its start. The rest of $s is not changed.

doc.shortHtml: Removes the given characters from the end of $s.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to trim.

params.name: characters
params.descHtml: The characters to remove, in any order. a..z is the three characters a, . and z. The default is space, tab, newline, carriage return, NUL and vertical tab.

doc.returnHtml: $s without those characters at its end. The rest of $s is not changed.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $times copies of $s, joined into one string.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to repeat.

params.name: times
params.descHtml: How many copies to write.

doc.returnHtml: The repeated string. It is "" when $times is 0 or $s is empty.

errors.descHtml: The result would be larger than this process can hold.

doc.shortHtml: Reverses the order of the characters in $s. A character is what a person sees as one character, so "café" becomes "éfac" and an accent stays on its letter.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to reverse.

doc.returnHtml: The reversed string. It has the same length as $s. The empty string gives "".

members.name: wrap
members.signature: wrap(string $s, uint $width, { breakWith?: string, cutLongWords?: bool }): string

doc.shortHtml: Splits $s into lines of at most $width characters. It breaks a line at a space and writes breakWith in place of that space. A character is what a person sees as one character, so "é" counts as one.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to wrap.

params.name: width
params.descHtml: The longest line, in characters. With 0, every space is a line break.

params.name: breakWith
params.descHtml: The text written at each line break. The default is "\n". Where $s already contains this text, a new line starts there.

params.name: cutLongWords
params.descHtml: With true, a word longer than $width is cut into pieces of $width characters. With false, the default, a long word stays whole on a line of its own.

doc.returnHtml: The wrapped text. A text of at most $width characters is returned unchanged. A result over the memory limit stops the request.

errors.descHtml: breakWith is "", or $width is 0 and cutLongWords is true.

doc.shortHtml: Changes every letter of $s to lower case. It uses Unicode's rules, so ÄRGER becomes ärger.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to change.

doc.returnHtml: The string in lower case. Characters that are not letters do not change. The result can have a different length from $s.

doc.shortHtml: Changes every letter of $s to upper case. It uses Unicode's rules, so straße becomes STRASSE.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to change.

doc.returnHtml: The string in upper case. Characters that are not letters do not change. The result can be longer than $s.

doc.shortHtml: Changes the first letter of $s to upper case and keeps the rest as it is. It uses Unicode's rules, so ärger becomes Ärger.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string whose first character changes.

doc.returnHtml: The string with its first character in upper case. An empty string gives "".

doc.shortHtml: Changes the first letter of $s to lower case and keeps the rest as it is. It uses Unicode's rules, so Ärger becomes ärger.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string whose first character changes.

doc.returnHtml: The string with its first character in lower case. An empty string gives "".

doc.shortHtml: Case-folds $s: every letter changes to one fixed form, so text that differs only in upper and lower case gives the same result.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to fold.

doc.returnHtml: The folded string. It is a key for comparing, not text to show: ß becomes ss and ﬁ becomes fi. fold("STRASSE") == fold("straße") is true.

doc.shortHtml: Changes $s into one of the four Unicode normal forms. Two ways to write the same text then give the same string.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to normalize.

params.name: form
params.descHtml: Which form to use. Nfc and Nfd keep every character's meaning. Nfkc and Nfkd also replace look-alike characters: ﬁ becomes fi.

doc.returnHtml: The normalized string. Nfc is the form to store and compare text in. A string of ASCII characters is returned unchanged.

doc.shortHtml: Builds a string of one code point. A code point is the number Unicode gives to one symbol. To build one byte, use Core\Bytes.

params.name: codePoint
params.descHtml: The number of the symbol. It is at most 0x10FFFF and is not in the surrogate range 0xD800 to 0xDFFF.

doc.returnHtml: A string that contains that one code point. 0x20AC gives "€".

errors.descHtml: $codePoint is above 0x10FFFF, or it is in the surrogate range 0xD800 to 0xDFFF. Unicode gives no symbol to these numbers.

doc.shortHtml: Builds a string from a list of code points, in order. It does the opposite of Core\Str::codePoints.

params.name: codePoints
params.descHtml: The numbers of the symbols, in order. Each one is at most 0x10FFFF and is not in the surrogate range 0xD800 to 0xDFFF.

doc.returnHtml: The string. An empty array gives "".

errors.descHtml: An element is above 0x10FFFF, or it is in the surrogate range 0xD800 to 0xDFFF. No part of the string is returned.

doc.shortHtml: Fills the placeholders in $template with $arguments and returns the text. The placeholders are %s %d %u %f %e %g %x %X %o %b %%, with flags, a width, a precision and positions such as %1$s. The result never depends on the locale.

params.name: template
params.descHtml: The template. It must be trusted text, so a tainted string is not allowed. When the template is written directly in the code, its placeholders are checked when the program compiles.

params.name: arguments
params.descHtml: The values for the placeholders, in order, or by position with %1$s. Every value must be used by at least one placeholder.

doc.returnHtml: The filled-in text. A width or a precision counts characters, as Core\Str::length does. %f always writes . before the decimals.

errors.descHtml: A placeholder is not valid, the template uses more arguments than were passed, an argument is not used, or a value does not fit its placeholder. For example, %d does not accept an array.
A width or a precision is larger than any string this process can hold. A smaller one that is over the memory limit stops the request.

classes.summaryHtml:
Functions for text: measure it, search it, cut it, change its case and build new strings. Every position and length counts characters the way a person sees them, so an accented letter or an emoji counts as one.

Every member of Core\Str is a static function over a string that answers a new value; none changes its argument. Every position, length and count is in graphemes — user-perceived characters — so length("👍🏽") is 1, no slice or chunk ever splits a character, and a byte count is Core\Bytes::length. A string has no $s[0] and no </>: Core\Str::at, Core\Str::slice and Core\Str::compare are those spellings.
